description:
`src/narrate/render-cache.ts` keys each RAW per-sentence render on backend + model + voice + spoken text. Whole-take rendering makes the sentence the wrong unit: key the take on backend + model + voice + renderMode + the full spoken text (plus chunk_length, which changes the audio).

Cache the audio AND the word timings together — re-deriving boundaries needs both, and a cached wav without its alignment is a cache miss dressed up as a hit.

Write down the trade in the module doc, because it is a deliberate regression of the thing that module was built for: a one-word edit now re-buys the whole take. At ~$15/M UTF-8 bytes that is a fraction of a cent per script (a full 24-script season pass ≈ $0.17), which is why it is acceptable here and would not be on a per-character-billed subscription tier. `--no-cache` keeps working.
requirements: ["Take-level key includes renderMode and chunk_length", "Alignment JSON cached beside the audio under the same key", "Module doc states the cost trade explicitly"]
title: Move the render cache to take granularity

description:
Turn the two-way create destination into three, so an end user can author a skill into their own repo without writing into OpenThrottle's catalog.

`app/routing/skills/config/skill-create.ts`:
- `SKILL_CREATE_DESTINATIONS` becomes `{ custom: 'custom', openthrottle: 'openthrottle', personal: 'personal' }`. Rename `repo` → `openthrottle`: the value is posted in a form body and narrowed server-side, so leaving it named `repo` while it means "OpenThrottle's committed catalog" is exactly the ambiguity this plan exists to remove. Grep for every `SKILL_CREATE_DESTINATIONS.repo` before renaming.
- `isSkillCreateDestination` gains the third arm — keep it an explicit disjunction, not an `Object.values().includes`, so a malformed POST is still refused rather than defaulted.
- `DEFAULT_SKILL_CREATE_DESTINATION` stays `personal`.

`app/routing/skills/data/create-skill-file.server.ts` — add the third target:
- `custom` → `<monorepoRoot>/.agents/skills/<slug>/SKILL.md`, written as a **real directory**. It is committable by construction: the managed `.gitignore` block ignores `.agents/skills/*` but rescues `!.agents/skills/*/`, and git classes the generated symlinks as files.
- Collision rules are the existing `assert_name_is_free` mirror, unchanged in substance: refuse on a lockfile slug, on `skills/<slug>`, on a personal skill of that name, and on a slug already linked into the agent skills dirs. A custom create hits the last of those against its own target directory, so make sure the pre-write existence check refuses cleanly with the right message rather than throwing EEXIST.
- Keep the module's contract: nothing touches disk until every refusal has passed, and a rejected create leaves the filesystem byte-identical, including no empty directory.
- Sync: a custom skill is written directly INTO `.agents/skills/`, so it is discoverable immediately — but the per-CLI fan-out dirs (`.claude/skills`, `.codex/skills`, …) still need `syncSkillLinks`. Run it exactly as the other destinations do, and surface a sync failure as its own error, never as success.

`data.copy.ts` → `SKILL_CREATE_COPY`: rename `destinationRepo*` to `destinationOpenThrottle*` and add `destinationCustom{Label,Description}`. Follow the field's existing rule — state the CONSEQUENCE, not the name: custom lands in your repository as a committed directory that everyone on your team gets; OpenThrottle lands in the OpenThrottle catalog for a PR. Add a `customCollisionError` if the existing four messages do not already cover the new target.

`useSkillCreateForm.tsx` and `SkillCreateDestinationField.tsx` render the third option; the field's consequence line becomes a three-way lookup rather than a ternary.

Tests: each destination resolves to the right absolute path; each collision refuses with its own message and writes nothing; the CRLF→LF normalization still applies to a custom create.
requirements: ["SKILL_CREATE_DESTINATIONS is custom/openthrottle/personal, with repo fully renamed", "create-skill-file.server.ts writes custom to .agents/skills/<slug>/SKILL.md as a real directory", "All four collision rules apply to a custom create and leave the filesystem byte-identical on refusal", "syncSkillLinks still runs for custom, and its failure is surfaced as an error", "Copy states the consequence of each of the three destinations"]
title: Split the create destination into custom and openthrottle

description:
**Gates every other task in this plan.** The whole of option E assumes a plugin's hooks execute (a) in a repo that has no OT config of its own, and (b) under the exact invocation the drivers use. Neither is verified.

`packages/openthrottle-drivers/src/drivers/claude.ts` builds:

```
claude -p --permission-mode acceptEdits "<prompt>" [--model X] [worktree flags]
```

Prove, in a scratch repo outside the monorepo:

1. A minimal hand-rolled plugin dir (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json` + `hooks/hooks.json` pointing at a `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/probe.cjs` that just writes a file) fires when passed via `--plugin-dir`.
2. It fires in **headless `-p` mode**, not just interactive. Non-interactive sessions do not raise every event an interactive one does — confirm which of our five events actually arrive: `PreToolUse` (matcher `Skill`), `Stop`, `UserPromptExpansion`, plus the outcome/drain adapters.
3. It coexists with a user-defined hook on the same event in the target repo's own `.claude/settings.json` — **both** must run. This is the no-clobber guarantee; verify it rather than trusting the docs.
4. `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` resolves correctly when the plugin dir is an absolute path outside the cwd.
5. Note that `--bare` explicitly skips hooks, LSP, and plugins — confirm nothing in our spawn path sets it.

If `UserPromptExpansion` or `Stop` do not fire under `-p`, that reshapes the payload (leg B may only be able to carry a subset) — record which events survive before anyone builds the artifact.
summary: GATE PASSED — option E is unblocked. Verified empirically against Claude Code 2.1.232 in a scratch repo outside the monorepo, using the driver's exact invocation (`claude -p --permission-mode acceptEdits --plugin-dir <abs> "<prompt>"`). (1) Plugin hooks fire under headless `-p`. (2) `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` resolves to the absolute plugin dir outside cwd. (3) No-clobber verified, not assumed: on every shared event BOTH the target repo's own hook and the plugin's hook ran (target first). (4) All five events survive `-p` — SessionStart, PreToolUse(Skill), PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd. Key non-obvious finding: `UserPromptExpansion` is gated on the prompt NEEDING expansion, not on headless-vs-interactive — it fired for `/probe-skill` but not for a natural-language prompt, which instead raised PreToolUse/PostToolUse. So PreToolUse(Skill) and UserPromptExpansion are COMPLEMENTARY capture paths and both must ship. (5) No `--bare` on the real spawn path; surviving `claude --bare -p` strings in tools/workflows messages/docs are stale text only (folded into the docs task).
title: 🧪 Spike: prove hooks fire via --plugin-dir in headless `claude -p` mode

description:
Write the architecture design doc under `docs/` (NOT an OT markdown plan). It must inventory what already exists before proposing net-new, and resolve every open decision so downstream tasks are unambiguous.

Must cover:
- **openthrottle-drivers inventory** — enumerate the existing surface (`ALL_DRIVERS`, `getDriver`, `AgentDriver.buildShellCommand`, `DriverInvocationConfig`, `runDriverAsync`/`runDriverSync` engine, `DriverCapabilities`, `DriverEndpointConfig`) and define the single provider-agnostic 'run once' entrypoint the server will call (signature: `{prompt, driverId, model, settings, cwd, signal, timeoutMs, onChunk}` → result). Confirm what's reused vs. the thin gap to add. Keep the primitive in this package (the choke point).
- **Generic queue design** — one shared queue name + payload schema `{scheduleId, prompt, driverId, model, settings, ...}`; why NOT per-job queues (and the `createQueue` producer-only caveat).
- **Scheduling mechanism** — decide legacy `repeat: {pattern}` vs newer `upsertJobScheduler`; timezone handling; reuse of `REPEATABLE_JOB_OPTIONS`.
- **Persistence** — `scheduled_jobs` (+ `scheduled_job_runs`?) table shape: prompt, driver_id, model, settings jsonb, cron pattern, tz, enabled, next/last run, ownership; how it maps to a BullMQ scheduler key.
- **Run output/logs** — reuse `queueJobLogs`/`queueJobLogTail` + work-ledger, or a dedicated runs table? Decide so the UI console can consume it.
- **DB↔BullMQ reconciliation** — boot-time + on-mutation sync (create/enable → upsert scheduler, disable/delete → remove); idempotency.
- **Role-slicing** — producer vs processor module split and `PROCESS_ROLE` gating (api never creates orphan schedulers).
- **GraphQL contract** — types, queries, mutations (create/update/delete/enable/disable/run-now), and how it relates to existing `repeatableJobs`/`removeRepeatableJob`.

Acceptance: doc merged under `docs/`, reviewed (fable-5/opus-4.8), with a clear recommendation on every decision above; subsequent tasks reference it.
title: Architecture design doc (design-first gate)

description:
The two previous tasks fix today's instances; this stops the class from silently returning. Without a guard, the next generated package inherits the same template and CI goes shard-dependent red again — and the symptom (`Failed to resolve entry for package X`) reads like an unrelated flake.

### Build

1. `exports` resolves into a gitignored build directory (`dist/`) while `main`/`module`/`types` resolve into `src/` — the exact mismatch behind root cause B; **and**

description:
Apply task 3's partitioner change to the `build` job in `.github/workflows/continuous-integration.yml` (step `🧠 NX ${{ matrix.target }} affected`, ~line 352).

## Current shape

```
selector="$(pnpm exec tsx ./scripts/parallelize-tasks.ts "${{ matrix.jobIndex }}" "${{ env.jobCount }}")"
# empty selector → explicit no-op, exit 0
pnpm exec nx affected --exclude="*,$selector" --target=lint,typecheck,bundle-hooks-check --parallel
pnpm exec nx affected --exclude="*,$selector" --target=test
```

## What changes

- The `lint,typecheck,bundle-hooks-check` line does not change.
- The `test` line gains the sharded developer invocation per task 2's decided shape, using `matrix.jobIndex` / `env.jobCount` as the `--shard` numerator/denominator so the Vitest shard count is derived from the SAME two values as the project partition. They must never be able to drift into disagreement — that is exactly the failure `env.jobCount`'s ⚠️ comment already guards.
- `set -euo pipefail` is on: make sure the added command's failure actually fails the step, and that a skipped/not-affected developer app exits 0 without looking like a skip.
- Keep the empty-shard branch's "this is a no-op, NOT a skip" loudness. A shard that runs only the sharded suite (drew no other projects) is a NEW third state — say which one it is out loud, same as the existing two.

## Do not touch

- `test` stays serialized (no `--parallel`). The long evidence-gated comment above the step is explicit that sharding is NOT the evidence for widening concurrency, and this plan does not supply that evidence either.
- `timeout-minutes: 30` stays as headroom.
- The `vmForks` / `vmMemoryLimit: '512MB'` / `maxWorkers: 4` tuning in `vitest.config.ts` is orthogonal and load-bearing against the silent-OOM `(0 test)` failure mode. Leave it.

## Done when

The workflow's log makes the full picture legible on every box: which projects this shard drew, which Vitest shard of the developer suite it is running, and how many files that shard collected.
title: Wire the sharded test invocation into continuous-integration.yml

description:
## Resolved with no code change, deliberately

The task's own goal — "the recording needs a way to get the fresh-install output without uninstalling the operator's own MCP config" — is already met by the script as it stands. `renderInstructions(root, status)` takes `status` as a **parameter** with `detectInstallStatus()` only as its default:

```ts
const renderInstructions = (root: string, status: InstallStatus = detectInstallStatus()): string
```

That signature exists precisely so the install state can be supplied rather than sniffed. The demo surface calls `renderInstructions('/workspace/openthrottle', { claude: false, cursor: false })` and gets the fresh-install rendering on a machine where OT MCP is very much installed. No on-disk state is read, nothing is written, and the operator's `~/.claude.json` and `~/.cursor/mcp.json` are never touched.

## No flag was added, and that is the finding

The task offered "a flag or an env override that forces the not-installed rendering, added to the script rather than faked in the flow". Both were rejected:

- The parameter already **is** the seam. A `--force-fresh` flag or an `OT_MCP_ASSUME_FRESH` env var would be a second, redundant way to reach the same code path, and every added path is a new way for the default behaviour to regress — which the task explicitly forbids.
- An env override is worse than a flag here: it would make the command's output depend on ambient state, so a stale export in the operator's shell could silently print install instructions to someone who does not need them.

Using the parameter is not "faking it in the flow" either — the flow does not hand-write the block, it calls the product's own renderer. The distinction the task was guarding against is a pasted copy of the output, and that is exactly what is *not* happening.

## Contract is already under test

`scripts/__tests__/setup_mcp-instructions.test.ts` covers the path the surface depends on: `renderInstructions(ROOT, NEITHER)` naming both clients and embedding the resolved launcher, the already-installed branch, the all-installed branch, and — usefully for gate 2 — "every placeholder value is a literal `${...}` token". So the surface is not depending on an untested private detail; it is depending on asserted behaviour.

The one guard that did NOT exist is a test that the *rendered surface text* stays leak-clean. That is a demo-tree concern rather than a script concern, so it is implemented with the surfaces in task 4 rather than bolted on here.
summary: RESOLVED WITH NO CODE. renderInstructions(root, status) is already an exported pure function with tests covering the both-false path, so the recording forces the fresh-install rendering by passing status. No flag added — deliberately.
title: Handle the already-installed branch of the setup command

description:
Decide the convention before touching routes, so the later batches are mechanical.

Start from the proposed convention in the plan description and either ratify it or amend it. The open calls worth settling explicitly:

1. Segment order — leaf-first (`Appearance | Settings | OpenThrottle`) or parent-first (`Settings | Appearance | OpenThrottle`)? Leaf-first is recommended: it matches the existing majority, matches the `handle.breadcrumb` + `handle.links` order already in these route modules, and keeps the distinguishing word visible in a narrow browser tab.
2. Which route groups get a section segment. Recommended: `/settings/*`, `/skills/*`, `/queues/*`, `/plans/$planId/*`, `/legal/*` — groups with a real index page and more than two leaves. Not `/calendar/*`, `/notes/*`.
3. Sentence case vs Title Case. Recommended sentence case, with a short reserved-word list preserved verbatim: `OpenThrottle`, `MCP`, `IDE`, `FAQ`, `PR`, `API`, and proper nouns from data.
4. Detail-page phrasing: entity name from loader data, falling back to a generic singular label with no `Details` suffix.

Write the result into `applications/openthrottle-developer/AGENTS.md` as a short `## Page titles` section — that file is the per-project tier of the AGENTS.md hierarchy and is where an agent editing this app will actually look. Keep it under ~15 lines: the format string, the case rule with the reserved-word list, the detail-route rule, and the note that resource routes intentionally set no title.

Recording the real app against a real machine is a live leak risk — tokens in a URL, a real email in the account menu, a private repo name in a project card, a `.env` value in a log tail. Automation makes this worse, not better, because nobody is watching the frames.

Deliver `docs/marketing/publish-checklist.md` plus whatever automated checks are cheap:

- OCR or DOM-scrape the recorded frames for high-entropy strings, `@`-addresses, and a denylist of real repo/org names; fail the build on a hit. This is the automated half and it's worth the effort.
- Human gate on: does the video actually demonstrate the claim in the title, is the pacing watchable, is the audio level right.
- Confirm every UI state shown is real and current — no aspirational features.
- Licensing: music attribution, and confirm any third-party logos shown are used within their trademark terms (the repo already has `TRADEMARK.md` / `NOTICE` discipline; extend it here).

This task exists because the failure mode is silent and irreversible once uploaded.
summary: A gate every video passes before upload: no secrets, no real identities, no broken claims.
title: Write the pre-publish review and redaction checklist

description:
## The problem
The month's dominant churn was developer-app UI (~15% of all churn in app/routing: settings, plans, skills, onboarding), and its regressions were all of a class no unit test catches: CloneRepoDialog not closing after a successful clone (#376), add-folder dialog close (#368), chat/tab scroll jumping (#279), wrong pagination labels (#380), first chat message hanging (#348). At the same time, four spec-backfill PRs in one month (#327/#328/#331/#333) plus a warn-mode coverage guard (#325) show the testing investment is real but capped at render level. Runtime verification is structurally blocked: authed pages need permissions (e.g. settings:read) that fresh users don't have and login can't be automated, so agents verifying their own work fall back to render-level Vitest — a systemic gap in a repo where agents are the primary implementers. Maestro flow experiments and a target-a-production-build convention exist, but no plan or CI lane owns E2E.

## The proposed change
A dedicated E2E project (Playwright is the pragmatic default; evaluate against the existing Maestro Web experiments once, then commit) that: (1) runs against a production build (react-router-serve + built api-role server on pinned alt ports), never the dev server; (2) gets a deterministic seeded permissioned user from the scripts-only seed path introduced in #292, fixing the fresh-user-zero-perms blocker at the seed level; (3) covers ~10–15 golden paths only — login, plan create/run/detail, add-folder/clone-repo onboarding, settings toggles, chat send-and-stream; (4) runs as a required-on-main / optional-on-PR CI lane initially, using the changed-path CI gating that already exists; (5) is documented as the sanctioned way for agents to live-verify UI work.

## What it unlocks
Catches the dialog/navigation/streaming regression class before merge instead of after; unblocks agent self-verification (removing the standing render-level-only caveat from every UI plan); protects the onboarding funnel that the entire public-launch month invested in — the flows most expensive to have broken for a new self-hosting user.

## Rough size
4–6 days for the harness + seed + first 10 flows. Touches a new e2e project (tools/ or applications/), databases (seed additions), .github/workflows, and docs.

## Migration risk
No production code changes — the risk is operational: flaky tests eroding trust and CI wall-clock (recently fought back to ~83s for unit tests in #267). Mitigations: id-first selectors, tiny golden-path scope, main-only requirement at first. Rollback: mark the lane optional or delete the project; nothing depends on it.

## The strongest argument against
The UI is still being renamed and restructured monthly (setup→agents, scheduled-jobs→schedule→calendar, Repositories extraction) — E2E written now will churn with every rename, and E2E suites die by flakiness: a lane the team learns to re-run-until-green is worse than no lane. The regressions cited were all caught and fixed within days by dogfooding, which is arguably the cheaper detector while the product is a single-operator system; the disciplined move may be to wait until the route map stabilizes post-launch.
summary: Stand up a small, stable browser E2E lane (production build + seeded roles) covering the golden paths that this month's regressions actually broke, and make it the runtime-verification path agents use.
title: Real browser E2E suite in CI against a production build, with a seeded permissioned user

description:
The pattern only holds if the next person (or agent) reaches for it. Rules live in `.agents/rules/` — the single source of truth for code style, which Cursor reads via `.cursor/rules/` symlinks and which fans out to `.claude/`.

1. **Add the rule** to `.agents/rules/` next to the existing style rules. State it as a hard rule with the reasoning, not a suggestion:
   - A vocabulary is declared once and enumerated nowhere else.
   - Subsets are exhaustive too — `Record<Member, boolean>`, never a hand-listed array.
   - Never write a second guard for a union that already has one.
   Include the `workspace-settings-action.ts` before/after as the worked example; a concrete bug that shipped is more persuasive than an abstract rule.
2. **Re-sync the agent folders** — run `/ot-skill-sync` (or the documented sync) so `.claude/` and `.cursor/` pick it up. Never hand-edit generated dirs.
3. **Update `CLAUDE.md`'s Code style section** with a one-liner pointing at the rule, alongside the existing "No new TypeScript enums" entry.
4. **Regression fixture:** a committed test that adds a hypothetical fourth editor and asserts the type error, so the tripwire itself is covered. Task 3 proves this manually and reverts; here it becomes permanent. Use `@ts-expect-error` so it fails loudly if the tripwire ever stops working.
5. **Update the plan-ec3dcee9 memory** to record that the exhaustive-Record tripwire had a documented hole and how it was closed.

Done means: re-running the ec3dcee9 exercise produces a compile error at every consumer, and that fact is asserted by a committed test rather than by anyone remembering to check.
summary: Rule at .agents/rules/coding/vocabularies.mdc (alwaysApply, enums.mdc shape) leading with the shipped workspace-settings-action.ts before/after; CLAUDE.md Code style line added. Correction to the task's step 2: sync.sh covers skills only — .cursor/rules symlinks are hand-created and tracked, so one was added and check-agent-assets-ssot validates it both directions. FLAGGED: that target fails on this branch with 21 pre-existing .gemini/skills gitignore violations (baseline fails identically under git stash -u; none rules-related), so check:local won't pass until fixed. Permanent fixture at workspace-editors-tripwire.test.ts asserts against the LIVE WORKSPACE_EDITOR_LABELS map with a positive control; proven live twice — removing the hypothetical fourth editor yields TS2578 on both @ts-expect-error lines, and attempting to widen labelled() to Partial won't compile at all because its return type makes the exhaustiveness self-defending. Gotcha found: the app typechecks packages against dist/*.d.ts not src, and tsc --build needs --force. Both memories updated + MEMORY.md index.
title: Document the pattern and close the loop on the original bug

description:
Four flows exist and they already disagree in ways a new author cannot resolve from the type. Before twenty more, extract the convention from them into a short authoring guide in the package (and a commented template flow the next task copies).

What the existing four actually encode, and needs stating:

- **`portraitStrategy` is a content decision, not taste.** 03 sets `fit` with the reason in a comment ("tables and full-page forms are wider than the portrait crop window; cropping them clips text at both edges"); 01 leaves the default `crop`. State the rule: `fit` for tables and full dashboards, `crop` for a field, a button or a single card.
- **Typing beats crop to the field, not the page** — 03's `regionOfInterest` maps `type-title` to `#plan-title` rather than the form, because a full-width form at portrait width is unreadable text at 20% scale.
- **`waitFor` before `highlight` after a tab switch.** 01 learned this the hard way ('at the portrait viewport the tab transition briefly reports no box for the target') and left the comment. It is a rule, not an anecdote.
- **Never `sleep`; `dwell` is pacing, not waiting.** Already in the types, worth repeating where flows are written.
- **Frame 1 shows the thing the title promises.** 01's opening comment. Every flow's first two steps should be readable as that.
- **Comment each step with the beat time from the episode**, the way all four do — it is what makes narration drift visible in review.

Done when the guide exists, the template flow is copyable, and every claim in it cites the flow that taught it.
summary: The tacit rules in 01/03/05/21 made explicit, so 20 new flows do not each invent them.
title: Write the flow-authoring conventions down, from the four flows that exist

description:
Scaffold with the `package` generator (`--type=node`), never by hand:

```bash
NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:package --organization=@openthrottle --type=node --name=nodejs-parts-department
```

`--type=node` selects the plain-Node package template (`tools/generators/src/generators/package/files/node`) — not `nestjs`, `react`, or `tools`. `--organization=@openthrottle` puts it at `packages/nodejs-parts-department` as `@openthrottle/nodejs-parts-department`; the generator derives the destination from the name verbatim, so the slug must be the full `nodejs-parts-department`. Run `--describe` first if the option set has moved.

Implement exactly the API settled in task 1. Non-negotiables:

- **Zero runtime dependencies.** If it needs an import, the design is wrong.
- **`.subsetOf()` is the load-bearing piece.** Its parameter must be an exhaustive `Record<Member, boolean>` so omitting a member is a compile error. This is what converts today's silently-excluding arrays into a forced decision.
- **`.labelled()`** takes an exhaustive `Record<Member, string>`.
- Explicit return types; no `as` casts; no `any`; `as const` objects rather than TS enums (repo style — note the generated GraphQL enums are the pre-existing exception, not a licence for new ones).
- Public API needs JSDoc `@public` or Knip strips it.
- Keep whatever the `node` template emits for source-first packaging (`main`/`types` → `./src/index.ts`, `__build` placeholder, no real `build` target) rather than hand-adjusting it; if the template disagrees with task 1's decision, reconcile in the plan output before editing.

**Type-level tests matter more than runtime tests here.** The whole value is the compile error. Assert the negative cases — an incomplete `labelled()` map and an incomplete `subsetOf()` map must both fail to typecheck. Runtime assertions alone would pass even if the types silently widened to `string`, which is precisely the bug this package exists to prevent. Use `@ts-expect-error` (it fails the build when the error does NOT occur, making it a real assertion) or a `tsd`-style approach if one is already in the repo — check before adding a dependency.

Validate: `pnpm nx run nodejs-parts-department:lint,typecheck,test` (sequentially — shared Nx cache); confirm the Nx project name the generator actually registered before running.
summary: Scaffolded packages/nodejs-parts-department via @tools/generators:package --type=node (template kept verbatim: __build/__build-package placeholders, main/module/types → ./src/index.ts, zero deps). description:
`runner/run.ts` sets the portrait viewport to `format.formats.short` (1080x1920 CSS px). 1080 CSS px is above the app's 768 mobile breakpoint, so the app renders its DESKTOP layout — sidebar and all — and on a content-light route ~60% of the Short frame is empty background.

Fix: separate the CSS viewport from the captured frame size.

- Add `recording.portraitViewport` to `docs/marketing/format.json` (540x960) and to the `FormatSpec` interface in `runner/format.ts`, with a `_note` explaining WHY 540 (below the 768 mobile breakpoint) and that deviceScaleFactor 2 still renders 1080x1920 physical pixels.
- In `runner/run.ts`, use `recording.portraitViewport` as the browser CSS viewport for the portrait pass, but pass the SHORT format dimensions (1080x1920) to `createCapture` as the screencast cap, so emitted frames stay 1080x1920.
- Record the FRAME dimensions in `manifest.width`/`manifest.height` (not the CSS viewport), and scale sampled `regions` boxes from CSS px into frame px by the capture/viewport ratio. `assemble/timeline.ts` `cropPath` treats `manifest.width/height` and `regions` as one coordinate space; today they coincide only because the landscape viewport happens to equal its frame size. Making regions frame-relative keeps the crop path correct for any capture.

Acceptance: the portrait pass renders the app's mobile layout, frames are still 1080x1920, and the landscape path is byte-for-byte unchanged in behaviour.
title: Record the portrait pass at a mobile viewport so the app's mobile layout fills the 9:16 frame

description:
Scope this task to whatever task 1 actually verified. Do not ship a command shape you have not run.

Keep `baseUrl`/`apiKey`/`configFilePath` as-is; the existing local callers must not change. Update the JSDoc, which currently says 'discovered local OpenAI-compatible model-server endpoint'.
- `opencode`: extend the materialized provider-config file path so it can define an OpenRouter provider (or use OpenCode's native one, if task 1 confirmed it) with the key supplied by the consumer. Note the known trap already documented in the driver: pointing `OPENCODE_CONFIG` at a generated file REPLACES the loaded config, so that file must also carry the `mcp` block or the run loses `openthrottle-mcp`. Handle it or state explicitly that OpenRouter runs are MCP-less.
- `codex`: today the endpoint path hardcodes the built-in `--oss` provider with a `model_providers.oss.base_url` override and an `ollama`/`lmstudio` wire adapter. OpenRouter is neither, so it needs its own `model_providers.*` override carrying `base_url`, `env_key`, and the correct `wire_api` — verified against the installed `codex --help` and config docs, not assumed.
- The leaf package stays pure: builders never read env, never touch the filesystem, never spawn. The key reaches the subprocess via the consumer-supplied env prefix / config file, the same way the local path works today.
- `claude` and `cursor` keep `supportsCustomBaseUrl: false` — they speak proprietary wire protocols. Do not change them.
- Update the capability matrix and the endpoint section of `packages/openthrottle-drivers/README.md`.
- Command-construction tests per driver: base command, model slug, key/URL escaping, and that a run WITHOUT an endpoint is byte-identical to today (the parity test).
- End the task with one real end-to-end run of each wired CLI against OpenRouter, and record the exact command and outcome. A driver that cannot be proven working is reported as not working, not shipped as done.
title: Drivers: run codex and opencode against OpenRouter

description:
The cheap version of this whole idea is to drop a `project.json` into `app/routing/plans` and call it a project without moving anything. It looks equivalent and is not. Prove that here so nobody re-proposes it in six months.

1. Add a minimal `project.json` under `app/routing/schedule` (smallest domain, 26 files) with `test`/`lint`/`typecheck` targets. Leave every `~/...` import exactly as it is.
2. Check `pnpm nx graph`: the app should show NO dependency on the nested project, because `~/*` resolves through the app's own tsconfig `paths` and Nx's import analysis never leaves the app.
3. Demonstrate the failure mode concretely: warm the app's `test` cache, edit a file inside `app/routing/schedule`, re-run, and record whether the app reports cached-green. That is the false-cache-hit risk.
4. Note the second problem while you are there: Nx excludes nested-project files from the parent's file set, so the app's own inputs may no longer include the routing sources at all.
5. Revert everything.

Done when: the graph output and the cache behaviour are recorded in plan output as the written justification for the real extraction.

If this UNEXPECTEDLY works — Nx does record the edge and invalidates correctly — say so loudly and stop. The entire plan gets cheaper and Phase B should be redesigned around it.
summary: Show that a project.json under app/routing/<domain> with ~/ imports left in place produces NO Nx edge — the reason this plan moves code instead of just declaring projects.
title: Phase A: disprove the nested project.json shortcut

description:
Revealed by the task-2 dedupe verification. Plan-level dedupe works — a second `Job_DeadCode` run correctly amended plan `80b013c0` instead of opening a second one. Task-level dedupe does not exist, and the result is worse than redundancy.

Evidence in `80b013c0` right now:
- sortOrder 2000 and 11000 are the same nestjs-testing finding, same two files, same verdict, filed twice.
- `xlsx` is covered at both 1000 and 6000.
- sortOrder 1000 says **delete `passport`** ("zero hits"); sortOrder 6000 says **"EXPLICITLY DO NOT act on … `passport`"**. One plan, two opposite instructions for the same dependency.

Root cause: the Dedupe section tells the job to check whether a *plan* covers a finding, and it checks plan existence and titles. It never instructs the job to read the existing plan's *tasks* and reconcile finding-by-finding.

Apply to **all ten** `.agents/prompts/Job_*.md`. The section is job-specific in its wording but structurally identical in each, so the same three additions go in each file, phrased for that job's subject matter:

1. **Read the tasks, not just the plan.** When an open plan for this job already exists, call `get_tasks_by_plan_id` and compare every new finding against the existing task list by subject (file path, export, dependency name, migration — whatever that job's unit of finding is). File a task only for a subject not already present.
2. **Never contradict an existing task.** If a new sweep reaches a different verdict on a subject an existing task already covers, do **not** file a second task with the opposing verdict. Append the disagreement and its evidence to the existing task's description, so a human resolves one task rather than discovering the conflict mid-execution.
3. **Fail loudly when dedupe is degraded.** `semantic_search` currently returns zero results for every query on this instance (unpopulated vector index — see the separate follow-up task). A job that cannot semantically dedupe must say so explicitly in its plan description rather than reporting "no duplicates found", which is indistinguishable from a real all-clear.

Acceptance: all ten prompts updated; a third `Job_DeadCode` run against the amended `80b013c0` files **no** task whose subject is already covered, and either reports "nothing new" or adds only genuinely new subjects; the run's plan description explicitly states that `semantic_search` was unavailable.
summary: Task-level dedupe is missing: a second run re-files findings already on the plan and can contradict them. Fix the Dedupe wording in all ten prompts before the cron fleet is enabled.
title: Tighten the shared Dedupe section across all ten Job_* prompts

description:
Four places currently assert, as settled fact, the thing this plan disproves. Each was correct about PROJECT sharding and wrong to conclude the matrix can never lower this suite's wall-clock.

## Sites

1. `applications/openthrottle-developer/vitest.config.ts` — the `pool` JSDoc: "project sharding splits the affected PROJECT list, and this suite is a single Nx project, so whichever box draws it runs all of it. The matrix cannot lower this suite's wall-clock — a faster pool can." Correct premise, wrong conclusion: Vitest `--shard` is a third lever. Rewrite so the vmForks rationale (which still stands on its own measured 253s → 86s) survives, and the sharding claim is replaced by what is now true.
2. `.github/workflows/continuous-integration.yml` (~line 225) — the shard-count rationale calls the single heaviest project a floor "whose suite sharding cannot split". That floor moved; the 4th-box arithmetic that leaned on it needs restating, not silently deleting.
3. `docs/reliability/developer-vitest-pool.md` § "Why config-only, not sharding" (~lines 42–61) — its "Now:" paragraph already ends with "A Vitest `--shard` matrix or an Nx atomized `test` target remains the next lever." That lever is now pulled. Update to the shipped state.
4. `docs/monorepo/ci-cost.md` § CI sharding — re-price the heavy box with the measured post-change numbers.

## Rule for all four

Do not just delete the old reasoning. Each of these was a deliberate, evidence-backed decision at the time; the value is in showing what changed and why the conclusion flipped. Replace the stale claim with the measured new one and keep the history legible.

## Done when

No file in the repo still tells a reader that this suite's wall-clock cannot be lowered by the CI matrix, and `pnpm nx run monorepo:knip` / lint are unaffected.
title: Correct the stale 'sharding cannot split this suite' framing in code and docs

description:
The `custom:` link and the README both need a destination that answers "why should I?" in under a screen. Recommended location: root `FUNDING.md`, sitting alongside `LICENSE.md`, `LICENSING.md`, `TRADEMARK.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` — the existing convention for meta docs is the root, not `docs/`. Link it from `CONTRIBUTING.md` too.

**Content, in this order:**

1. **One-paragraph what-this-is** — OpenThrottle in a sentence, open core, Apache-2.0 for the core. No manifesto.
2. **The combined cost table** from **"Record current SaaS spend and build the combined funding table"**, verbatim — line item, monthly cost, required/desired, what sponsorship covers. This is the load-bearing section.
3. **The goal**, stated plainly, using the required/desired subtotals rather than a single round number: recurring sponsorship covers hosting and CI so the project can become a fully deployable production toolset — a self-hostable GCP stack instead of a repo that only runs on a laptop. Name the concrete unlock: a public staging/demo environment, migration off personally-funded SaaS, and CI capacity that doesn't come out of pocket.
4. **Tiers** — map them to the two priced footprints, not to invented perks: the lower tier keeps the required floor running, the higher tier funds the desired setup (staging + production, HA/PITR, split API/worker). Tie individual amounts to real line items ("$25/mo ≈ the Redis instance"). Do not promise support SLAs, roadmap influence, or private features that don't exist.
5. **What sponsorship does not include** — no license grant beyond Apache-2.0, no trademark rights (`TRADEMARK.md`), no EULA relief for commercial modules, not a support contract. Short and unmissable; this protects the open-core boundary the licensing plans established.
6. **Non-money ways to help** — issues, PRs, docs. Costs nothing and reads as sincere.

Write in the repo's existing documentation voice (see `README.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`). No invented sponsor counts, logos, or testimonials. If platform enrollment from the human-gate task is still pending, add one line saying the Sponsor button activates on approval.
requirements: ["FUNDING.md created at the repo root and linked from CONTRIBUTING.md", "Combined cost table carried over with numbers matching the committed estimate CSV(s)", "Funding goal stated using the required/desired subtotals, with concrete unlocks rather than vague appeals", "Tiers mapped to the two priced footprints, not to invented perks", "A 'what sponsorship does not include' section covering license, trademark, EULA, and support", "Non-financial contribution paths listed", "No fabricated sponsors, logos, or testimonials; voice matches existing root docs"]
summary:
DONE. FUNDING.md at the repo root (alongside LICENSE.md / LICENSING.md / TRADEMARK.md / SECURITY.md / CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, per the existing meta-doc convention) and linked from CONTRIBUTING.md's "Ways to contribute" list.

Sections in the required order: one-paragraph what-this-is (open core, Apache-2.0, links LICENSING.md); the combined cost table carried verbatim from the previous task; the goal; tiers; what sponsorship does not include; other ways to help.

GOAL stated with the real subtotals and three concrete unlocks rather than vague appeals — a public environment to actually try (today nothing is deployed; infra/environments/staging is commented out), migration off personally-funded SaaS, and CI capacity that is not a personal expense.

TIERS mapped to the two priced footprints, no invented perks: $100 = the required floor ($98.52), $200 = the floor plus roughly a quarter of desired ($431.55). Smaller amounts tied to real line items — $36 ~ the Memorystore instance, $31 ~ the Cloud SQL instance, $30 ~ the compute.

DOES NOT INCLUDE covers all four required boundaries: no license grant beyond Apache-2.0, no trademark rights (TRADEMARK.md), no EULA relief for commercial modules (LICENSE-EULA.md), no support contract or SLA — plus no roadmap influence or private features.

No fabricated sponsors, logos, or testimonials. All six internal links verified to resolve on disk. Prettier clean.

No "button activates on approval" line was needed: enrollment is COMPLETE on the org. The separate gap is that the org listing has no tiers defined yet, tracked as its own task rather than hedged in the page copy.

Addresses hypothesis 3. `buildScrubbedEnv()` in `cursor-agent/cursor-agent.ts` passes only `CURSOR_API_KEY, HOME, LANG, LC_ALL, LOGNAME, PATH, TERM, TMPDIR, USER`. A warm run may read a cache a cold run has to create — and if the directory is located via an env var we drop, cold and warm diverge exactly the way the bug describes.

Drive this from task 1's observed file-access list; do not add vars speculatively.

Candidates to evaluate:
- `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME` — if cursor honors XDG at all, dropping them while keeping `HOME` silently relocates its config between our child and the user's own shell.
- `SHELL` — some CLIs shell out for tool calls.
- `NO_COLOR=1` and/or `CI=1` — set these **explicitly** (not inherited) to suppress decorated/interactive output at the source. This is defense-in-depth for task 3: even with robust parsing, quiet output is better.
- Any other `CURSOR_*` var the user's environment defines (e.g. a config-dir or endpoint override). Consider a prefix rule (`CURSOR_*` all pass through) rather than enumerating, since cursor adds vars between releases.

Keep the security posture intact: the point of the allowlist is that the child gets the host login but none of the server's secrets. Document each addition with a one-line rationale comment.

Apply the same treatment to the streaming spawn — both use the same helper, so verify neither path regresses.

Tests: extend `cursor-agent/__tests__/cursor-agent.test.ts` to assert the exact env the child receives — both that new keys pass through and that a sentinel server secret does not.

description:
Direction-independent research. For each of claude, codex, cursor, opencode, grok — the five in `packages/openthrottle-drivers/src/drivers/` — establish:

1. Does it support hooks at all, and at which lifecycle points?
2. Where is hook config read from (in-repo file, home dir, both)?
3. Is there any **out-of-repo** override — a settings flag, a plugin dir, an env var — or must config live inside the working tree?
4. Is there a plugin/extension mechanism that bundles hooks?

Known starting points: claude has `--settings`, `--plugin-dir`, `--plugin-url`, and a plugin marketplace (verified via `claude --help`). Cursor reads `.cursor/hooks.json` in-repo (`version: 1`, `afterFileEdit` / `beforeSubmitPrompt`) — we already ship one adapter there. The other three are unknown.

Deliverable: a table in `docs/monorepo/`, mirroring the CLI table in §2 of `foreign-workspace-skill-injection.md`. This directly answers whether the overlay is one mechanism or a per-CLI fan-out, and it is the only thing that could rescue option C.
summary: Matrix at `docs/monorepo/agent-cli-hook-capability-matrix.md`. All five CLIs were installed on this machine, so every row was established by RUNNING the binary (claude 2.1.232, codex-cli 0.147.0, cursor-agent 2026.08.11, opencode 1.18.16, grok 1.0.0), not read off a docs site. HEADLINE, AND IT INVERTS THE SKILLS PRECEDENT: every one of the five has an out-of-repo hook config path — three via a home-directory config layer, two via a per-invocation directory flag. §2 of the skill-injection record found that NO CLI exposes an out-of-repo skills directory, which is what forced materialization into the target tree; hooks are the opposite. This permanently closes option C, which was only rescuable if some CLI had no out-of-repo hook config AND parity became a v1 requirement — neither half holds. TWO FINDINGS CONTRADICT THE PLAN'S ASSUMPTIONS. (1) cursor-agent ALSO accepts `--plugin-dir`, repeatable, exactly like Claude; the plan had it as in-repo-only. Leg B generalizes to cursor with no new mechanism, since `capabilities.pluginDir` and `appendPluginDirShellFlags` are already per-driver — it is a payload plus flipping one boolean. (2) grok LOADS Claude plugins (`grok inspect` listed ours as "openthrottle (user, enabled) hooks" the moment it was installed) but does NOT fire them — verified on a headless run that provably used the skill and produced no event. Two structural reasons: hook execution requires per-project trust whose only lever is the interactive `/hooks-trust` slash command with no CLI flag, which blocks unattended foreign-repo runs by design; and grok has no `Skill` tool at all (`inspect` reports "unknown tool prefix: Skill") plus no `UserPromptExpansion`, so BOTH of our capture paths have nothing to match. Recorded loudly because "grok reads Claude plugins" is exactly the half-truth that would be mistaken for coverage. ALSO: codex needs no injection mechanism whatsoever — hooks live in `~/.codex/config.toml`, never in the repo (with `-c hooks.…`, `--profile`, `CODEX_HOME` for per-invocation control, and `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust` for automation). opencode is the only awkward one: its plugins are npm modules, not directories, so covering it is a publishing decision rather than a technical obstacle. Recommended order: claude (shipped) → cursor → codex → grok/opencode stay on option D. Machine state left clean — the test plugin and marketplace were uninstalled/removed.
title: Capability matrix: hook and plugin surfaces across all five agent CLIs

description:
## Finding
The SSR server build ships an **11.95 MB** `ide-engine.server` chunk (gzip **2042.7 KB**). First IDE request pays a multi-megabyte module load even though routes dynamic-import it.

## Paths
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/ide/data/ide-engine.server.ts`
- Routes: `ide._index.tsx`, `ide.files.tsx`, `ide.symbol.tsx`, `ide.symbols.tsx` (dynamic `import('~/routing/ide/data/ide-engine.server')`)
- Built: `applications/openthrottle-developer/build/server/assets/ide-engine.server-*.js`
- Likely weight from `packages/openthrottle-ide` / TypeScript language services

## Measured before
```bash
pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:build
# ide-engine.server-*.js = 11674.2 KB raw / 2042.7 KB gzip-9
# build/server total ≈ 25 MB; index.js 4653 KB
```

## Suspected cause
Bundling a full IDE/analysis engine into the React Router SSR server output instead of keeping it external or in a separate Node worker process.

## Proposed fix
Mark heavy IDE deps `ssr.external` / load via Node `createRequire` outside the Vite SSR bundle; or move analysis to a dedicated service. Keep the route-level dynamic import.

## Expected after
`ide-engine.server-*.js` **≤ 2 MB raw** (or absent from SSR assets with equivalent functionality via external require). Server build dir **≤ 15 MB**.

## Acceptance
Re-measure after production build: `ide-engine.server-*.js` raw size ≤ 2048 KB, or documented external load with SSR asset gone.
title: 4. Developer SSR: shrink ide-engine.server chunk (11.95 MB)

description:
**Root cause A.** `grep -rn testTimeout` across the repo (excluding node_modules) returns zero hits — no `vitest.config.ts`, no shared setup, no Nx targetDefault sets one. Every suite in the monorepo therefore runs on Vitest's 5000ms default with zero headroom, and the failures are all narrow overruns (the `Editor.ssr` case measured 6318ms against 5000ms), not hangs.

### Approach

Establish a shared base rather than sprinkling per-file `{ timeout: N }` arguments, which drift and hide the policy:

- Export a shared Vitest base (`testTimeout` and `hookTimeout`) that every project config merges in. `packages/react-router-testing` already serves this role for the four React Router apps via `setupReactRouterTest`, but node-side packages and `tools/generators` do not use it — so the base needs to be config-level, not setup-level, to cover both.
- Pick the budget from measurement, not taste: the observed overruns are 5–7s against 5000ms, and CI boxes now run 3 shards with higher per-box contention. **15000ms** for `testTimeout` gives ~2× headroom over the worst observed case without letting a genuine hang sit for a minute. Set `hookTimeout` to match, since `beforeAll` in the generator suites does the expensive tree setup.
- Raising the ceiling must not become cover for unbounded suites: keep the per-shard `timeout-minutes: 30` job ceiling as-is so a real hang still fails the box.

Explicitly rejected: blanket `retry: 1`. It converts a real timing regression into a silent 2× cost and a green check — the opposite of what this plan is for.

### Verify

Run the three offending projects with the new budget and confirm green, then confirm a deliberately-hung test still fails (temporarily add one, observe the 15s failure, remove it).

Related context: `docs/monorepo/ci-cost.md` records the measured shard economics; note the timeout choice there if that doc tracks CI tuning decisions.
summary: No project sets testTimeout, so every suite runs on Vitest's 5000ms default; three I/O-heavy suites exceed it under CI load.
title: Set a real Vitest timeout budget across the workspace

description:
## Class
Server secret / config leak risk (ranking #4).

## Location
- `applications/openthrottle-server/.env.default` — `JWT_SECRET` (committed local default; contains placeholder-ish words; sha256 prefix `274e11151dbc` for fingerprinting only).
- Root `.env.default` — `OPENTHROTTLE_DEVELOPER_JWT_SECRET` similarly.
- Docs treat these as local-dev (`docs/openthrottle/openthrottle-server-auth.md`).

## Reachability
If a hosted/shared deploy copies `.env.default` without replacing `JWT_SECRET`, anyone who can read the repo can forge HS256 JWTs for any `sub`.

## Remediation
1. Production/start should refuse empty or known-local JWT secrets (fail fast).
2. Keep local defaults only behind clearly non-production markers; rotate any deploy that reused the default (**human** rotates the secret and invalidates sessions).
3. Prefer secret manager / generated per-worktree secrets over committed values for anything beyond localhost.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Server boot in production fails if `JWT_SECRET` is missing or matches a denylist of known local defaults.
- [ ] Human verifies no shared deploy still uses the committed default (rotate if yes; never paste the value into OT).
title: Ensure committed JWT_SECRET defaults never ship to hosted deploys

Check whether other projects share this broken pattern - grep all package.json/project.json for `verify-graphql-codegen` and `git diff .*__generated__` and fix or file the same correction everywhere it's dead (note: apps like openthrottle-developer COMMIT their __generated__, so git-diff is valid there - only gitignored outputs are affected). Fix the misleading prose: the target's description string and packages/openthrottle-mcp/AGENTS.md:15-16 both claim the output is committed. Confirm where the guard runs (check:local / CI codegen-drift job) and that a deliberately-broken fragment makes it fail (prove the tripwire fires, then revert the breakage).

description:
**ROOT CAUSE, found by task 8's end-to-end cold validation.**

Running the shipped adapter against a genuinely cold cursor (statsig cache moved aside) reproduced the user's symptom exactly, and task 2's diagnostics named it:

```
Error: cursor-agent create-chat timed out after 30000ms
  bin=cursor-agent cwd=/…/loop-plan-cursor-cold-start elapsedMs=30019
  stdout="b17be556-b994-41ba-8a93-a09ce8ab8e08\n" stderr=<empty>
```

**`create-chat` printed a perfectly valid UUID — and we threw it away.** `createCursorAgentSession()` waits on the child's `close` event, and on a cold run the process lingers well past 30 s (statsig init, MCP init/OAuth discovery, plugin hooks, plus the leaked `worker-server`). The id is available in ~2 s; we wait 30 s and then fail.

This is precisely the reported symptom. Warm — i.e. after any earlier cursor invocation, which is what "switch to another agent and come back" buys via elapsed time — the process exits promptly and the mint succeeds.

Before task 2 this was invisible: the old message was `cursor-agent create-chat timed out after 30000ms.` with no stdout attached, so there was no way to know the id had been produced.

## Work

- In `createCursorAgentSession()`, resolve as soon as `parseCursorChatId()` finds an id in the accumulated stdout. Do not wait for `close`.
- On early resolve, clear the timeout and tear the child down with `terminateChild(child, graceMs, { processGroup: true })`. SIGTERM first, so cursor still gets to finish its `dispose()`.
- Keep the existing paths intact for the case where the process exits without a parseable id: non-zero exit, empty stdout, unparseable stdout, and the timeout backstop.
- Safe to kill after the id is printed: `handleCreateChat` writes `agentId` to the store *before* printing, and task 1 proved `--resume` works with an id whose store row never existed at all.

## Note on task 5

Task 5 verified "the streaming spawn does not start until the mint has fully closed". That ordering is now **deliberately traded away** — waiting for `close` is the bug. Stdout is fully read (we have the id) and the child is torn down, so there is no torn state. Update that finding rather than leaving it as a stale guarantee.

## Tests

- A fake bin that prints an id then hangs forever → resolves with the id, promptly, without hitting the session timeout.
- Regression: the existing timeout test must still fail when the child prints **nothing** and hangs.
- Existing non-zero-exit, no-id, and banner-only cases unchanged.

## Validate

Re-run the cold end-to-end (statsig cache moved aside, restored after): mint must succeed in ~2 s and the turn must stream to a clean terminal chunk with no leaked processes.
title: Resolve the mint on the parsed id, not on process exit

description:
Design task — output is a short design note plus the type file skeleton, not a migration.

## Decide the type shape

Start from every field the three current parsers read, plus the fields `docs/marketing/publishing.md` and `docs/marketing/youtube-format.md` describe but nobody stores. Group them:

- **identity** — `id` (slug, matches the flow id), `format: 'short' | 'longform'`.
- **production** — `recording: 'live' | 'replay'`, `flow` (demo flow id), `titleCard: readonly [string, string]`, `blockedOn: readonly string[]`, optional `portraitStrategy` if it belongs here rather than on the flow.
- **release** — `order: number` (today's `release`), `status: 'draft' | 'ready' | 'recorded' | 'published'`, `playlist` (one of the four in `publishing.md`), optional `publishedUrl` / `publishedAt`.
- **youtube** — `title`, `summary` (the per-video paragraph that opens the description), `tags`, `chapters` (long-form only), optional `thumbnail: { words: readonly string[] }`.
- **variants** — `readonly Variant[]` plus `selectedVariant: string`.

`Variant` carries `id` (a kebab slug, not `v0`/`v1` — the current names say nothing), `thesis` (the one-paragraph rationale that today sits as prose under the front matter), optional `pacingNotes`, and `beats: readonly Beat[]`. `Beat` is `{ t, action, narration }` — the same three columns, same contract: narration is the literal TTS input, action is the literal flow step.

**No stored derived values.** `spokenWords`, estimated spoken seconds and budget headroom are functions over `beats`, not fields. That is the whole reason the validator currently rewrites source files.

Follow the repo style rules: `as const` objects instead of enums, `import type`, explicit return types, alphabetised keys.

## Where it lives

Settled by the scaffold task: **`packages/openthrottle-showroom`**, alongside the pipeline that consumes it. What is still open and belongs in the note:

- One module per episode under `src/episodes/`, or one module per episode plus a hand-maintained registry index? Prefer explicit imports in an index over filesystem globbing — the registry should be typecheckable, and a glob is neither.
- Whether the episode and its flow sit **together** (`src/episodes/05-connect-ot-mcp/{episode.ts,flow.ts}`) or in parallel directories. They are transcriptions of each other and their beats are matched positionally; co-locating makes a drift obvious in review. Weigh that against the flat `flows/` layout the relocation carries over.
- Whether the human-readable markdown view survives as generated output or disappears entirely. GitHub-readable scripts have real value for review; a generator is another surface to keep honest.
- How a variant id maps onto output paths and cache keys — see the take-provenance task, but the naming decision is made here.

## Done when

A design note lands under `docs/marketing/` (or extends `pipeline.md`), the type file exists in the package and compiles with no episodes yet, and each open question above is answered with its reason.
summary: DONE — types.ts compiles with no episodes yet, design note at docs/marketing/episode-format.md, all four open questions answered. Commits 7c8656c6 + 95402023.
title: Design the typed episode shape

description:
Short design spike to lock the L3 mechanism, recorded via append_plan_output (or a docs/ ADR if it grows). Investigate and decide:

- **RR8 Single Fetch streaming semantics**: confirm exactly when React Router attaches a rejection handler to a naked deferred promise returned from a loader, and reproduce the window where a fast rejection escapes as an unhandled rejection. Confirm whether a thrown `redirect()` Response *inside* a deferred promise is honored by RR streaming (abort + redirect) — this is the linchpin of the auth path.
- **Mechanism choice** (the open decision): (A) opt-in `resilientDeferred(promise, opts)` helper that loaders wrap deferred values in, vs (B) an automatic entry-level wrapper that walks a loader's returned object and attaches a synchronous `.catch` to every promise-valued field (can't-forget). Weigh ergonomics, type-inference impact on `Route.ComponentProps['loaderData']`, and how each interacts with `<Await errorElement>`.
- **Lint enforceability**: whether an ESLint rule can flag naked `Promise`-returning fields in loader return objects (to back option A) — feasibility only, implementation is task 7.
- **Error taxonomy**: auth (→ redirect) vs timeout (`GraphqlTimeoutError`) vs other (→ degraded resolved value) — define what the helper does per class.

Output: the chosen L3 API signature, its home package (likely @openthrottle/react-router-utils, depending on react-router-graphql for isAuthError), and the adoption strategy (opt-in + lint, or automatic).
requirements: ["Documented decision (plan output or docs ADR) recording the RR8 streaming reproduction + whether thrown redirect() works inside deferred data", "Chosen L3 mechanism (opt-in helper vs automatic entry wrapper) with rationale and type-inference impact noted", "Final L3 API signature + home package + per-error-class behavior (auth/timeout/other) specified", "Feasibility note on an ESLint rule flagging naked-promise loader returns"]
summary: Decide the L3 API + placement + adoption strategy before implementing.
title: Design spike: lock the L3 deferred-resilience mechanism

description:
**Do this first.** `infra/gcp-estimate.csv` predates the current toolset and cannot be trusted as a baseline — it prices four SKUs (one E2, 10 GB SSD, Memorystore Redis Basic M1, a **MySQL** micro + 7300 GB-mo storage) totaling $52.61/mo, effective 2026-03-04, us-west1. The stack has moved. Rebuild the footprint from the repo, then produce **two priced tiers**, not one number.

### Step 1 — inventory what actually runs

`docker-compose.yml` is the closest thing to a deployment manifest; treat it as the source list and reconcile against `infra/applications/openthrottle/main.tf` (which already composes the app stack) and `infra/environments/{development,staging,production}/`. Services present today:

- **`server`** — NestJS GraphQL API. Note `applications/openthrottle-server/src/config/process-role.ts`: it runs as `api`, `worker`, or `all`. Production splitting API from worker means **two compute units**, not one — the old single-E2 estimate assumed `all`.
- **`postgres`** — Postgres with **pgvector** (semantic search / embeddings). Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL, not MySQL. pgvector index memory is the tier driver here.
- **`redis`** — BullMQ queues + caching (`@openthrottle/nestjs-bullmq`, `@openthrottle/nestjs-redis`). BullMQ needs persistence semantics Memorystore **Basic** tier does not give you across failover — price Standard as the desired tier and say why.
- **`migrations`** / **`bootstrap`** — run-once jobs; cost is negligible but they need somewhere to run (Cloud Run job or a VM step).
- **`mcp`** — the OT MCP server, a long-lived process.
- **`developer`** — the Developer UI. Note that **all four React Router apps currently deploy to Vercel** (`applications/{openthrottle-admin,openthrottle-developer,openthrottle-email,openthrottle-website}/vercel.json`). Decide and state whether GCP hosts them (Cloud Run + CDN/LB) or they stay on Vercel — this single choice moves both the GCP number and whether the Vercel bill is retired.
- **`whisper`** — voice transcription (`openthrottle/whisper`, faster-whisper model cache). CPU-only tiny.en per the voice-input spike; if it ships, it needs sustained CPU and model-cache storage. Mark it required or desired explicitly.
- **Embeddings** — `packages/node-client/src/ollama-embedding.ts` implies a local Ollama. Self-hosting embeddings on GCP means a much larger machine (or a GPU); a hosted embedding API may be cheaper than the instance it replaces. Price whichever you'd choose, and note the alternative.

Also account for the supporting services the old estimate omits entirely: **Artifact Registry** (container images — the compose file builds ~8), **Cloud Storage** (Terraform state bucket already exists in staging, plus artifacts/backups), **Secret Manager**, **Cloud Logging/Monitoring** retention past the free tier, **egress**, and **HTTPS LB + managed certs** — or note that `infra/modules/cloudflare` in front of a single VM avoids the GCLB line.

### Step 2 — split required vs desired

- **Required** — the floor: one environment, single-zone, no HA, smallest tiers that genuinely hold pgvector and BullMQ, minimal retention, automated backups on. This is "OpenThrottle is deployed and reachable." Be honest about what breaks at this tier (no failover, restore-from-backup means downtime, one noisy job saturates the box).
- **Desired** — what you'd actually want to run and point people at: separate **staging + production** (both env roots already exist in `infra/environments/`), API and worker as separate units, Memorystore Standard, Cloud SQL with HA or at least PITR, real log retention, and a public demo/staging environment. Each upgrade gets a line item and a one-line justification.

### Step 3 — price both

Re-run the Google Cloud Pricing Calculator (us-west1) for each tier and commit the results as CSVs with their share URLs and effective dates — keep the old `infra/gcp-estimate.csv` only if it is clearly dated and superseded, otherwise replace it. Verify the suspicious **7300 GB-mo** (7.3 TB) storage row against a realistic projection; it reads like a calculator default and it dominates nothing today but would if kept. Mark every line item `required` / `desired` so the two tiers are derivable from one table.

**Output**: committed CSV(s) plus a monthly table with a required subtotal, a desired subtotal, and per-line required/desired flags — the input task 3 turns into the sponsorship pitch. Report the real subtotals even if the desired tier exceeds $200/mo; a desired number above the ask is useful (it shows headroom and gives sponsorship somewhere to grow), it just has to be labeled honestly.
requirements: ["Service inventory derived from docker-compose.yml and reconciled against infra/applications + infra/environments, not from the stale CSV", "server api/worker role split, pgvector-capable Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL tier, and BullMQ-appropriate Redis tier each addressed explicitly", "An explicit decision recorded on whether the four Vercel-hosted React Router apps move to GCP or stay on Vercel", "whisper (voice) and embeddings (Ollama vs hosted) each classified required or desired with a cost consequence", "Artifact Registry, Cloud Storage, Secret Manager, logging/monitoring retention, egress, and LB/certs each priced or explicitly marked not-yet-needed", "Two tiers defined: required (floor, with its failure modes stated) and desired (staging+prod, HA/PITR, split workloads), each line item flagged", "Fresh Cloud Pricing Calculator CSV(s) committed with share URLs and effective dates; the 7300 GB-mo storage row verified or corrected; the 2026-03-04 MySQL estimate superseded or clearly dated", "Required and desired monthly subtotals reported as-measured, even if desired exceeds $200/mo"]
summary: DONE. Required $98.52/mo, desired $431.55/mo (us-west1). Committed infra/estimates/{README.md,gcp-required-2026-08-17.csv,gcp-desired-2026-08-17.csv,gcp-apps-on-cloud-run-2026-08-17.csv}; old MySQL estimate archived. Key findings: embeddings default to hosted OpenAI (no Ollama instance, no GPU); Caddy+Let's Encrypt means no GCLB line ($0 vs ~$18.25); the old CSV's "7300 GB-mo" is GB-HOURS (10 GB x 730 h), NOT 7.3 TB — no correction needed; the old CSV billed Memorystore for only 365 GB-hrs (half a month), understating it by $17.89. Decision: the four React Router apps STAY ON VERCEL — Cloud Run + LB is ~$57.67/mo before request-time vCPU and loses preview deployments, so Vercel is an ONGOING cost, not retired by a GCP move. Caveat: list-price derivations, not Calculator share URLs (interactive session unavailable); Memorystore Standard M1 $0.074/GB-hr is the largest unverified assumption.
title: Inventory the real stack and price required vs desired

description:
The abstract rule is “identity ObjectPattern unpack of `props` and of bindings taken from `props`, before `// Hooks`." Route keys (`loaderData`, `actionData`, `params`, `matches`) fall out of walking nested unpacks — they are not a special case. Do **not** implement two one-off checkers.

Extract a shared helper (e.g. `tools/dotfiles/src/rules/pre-hooks-unpack.ts`) that, given a function body + source, reports identity unpacks after the first `// Hooks` marker. Both `openthrottle/component-primitive-shape` and `openthrottle/route-primitive-shape` call it. Do not add a new audit script. Do not take this as a chance to also dedupe `MARKERS` / `checkMarkers` unless it is free.

Checker behavior:
- Flag a `VariableDeclarator` whose init is Identifier `props`, or an ObjectPattern destructure of a binding previously taken from `props`, if it appears after the first `// Hooks` marker in the same function body.
- Do not flag Setup-style derived consts (ternaries, `'x' in y` narrowing, maps).
- Message points at the pre-Hooks slot and component R3 (route reports may still link route R2).
- Autofix is optional and not required.

Tests:
- Unit-test the helper directly (generic `props` + nested unpack; derived const in Setup must not fire).
- `component-primitive-shape.test.ts`: valid = `const { item } = props; const { id } = item` before Hooks + a derived label in Setup; invalid = that unpack after Short Circuit.
- `route-primitive-shape.test.ts`: valid = repositories-list shape (props + loaderData unpack before Hooks, actionData narrowing in Setup); invalid = unpack after Short Circuit.

Ship the new check at **warn** on both rules. Do not flip to error in this task.
requirements: ["A shared helper implements the unpack check; both ESLint rules call it (no duplicated walk).", "Helper unit tests plus RuleTester fixtures for both rules: valid pre-Hooks unpack + Setup derive; invalid after-Short-Circuit unpack.", "Identity unpack after `// Hooks` warns; derived `const` in Setup does not."]
title: Shared ESLint helper: flag props unpack after // Hooks

description:
Placement is no longer only a directory decision — a new project is unusable until it is tagged, and the tags decide what may import it.

Document, sourced from `scripts/nx-validate-tags.ts` and the `depConstraints` in `tools/dotfiles/src/index.ts`:

- Every project carries exactly one `type:` tag — the valid set from `VALID_TYPE_TAGS`.
- `type:package` and `type:tool` must additionally declare a `publish:` tag.
- `technology:` tags come from a closed set (`llm`, `nestjs`, `nodejs`, `python`, `react-native`, `react-router`, `react`, `terraform`, `typescript`) — verify the set at write time rather than trusting this list.
- `production:true|false`, and the constraint that a `production:true` project may not depend on a `production:false` one.
- The four dependency constraints: applications -> packages only; packages -> packages only; tools -> packages + tools; production isolation.

Spell out the consequence in placement terms: "a package that will be imported by a production application must itself be `production:true`" and "an application can never be imported — if two apps need it, it is a package."

Done when: the tag vocabulary is verifiable against `pnpm run nx:validate-tags` and the section says what to do, not just what exists.
requirements: ["type/publish/technology/production tags documented", "Four depConstraints stated", "Consequence framed as a placement rule"]
title: Add the Nx tags and module-boundary section

description:
Create `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.yml` as a GitHub Issue Form.

Top-level keys:
- `name: Feature Request`
- `description:` one line, e.g. `Suggest a capability or improvement for OpenThrottle.`
- `title: '[Feature]: '`
- `labels: ['enhancement']` — `enhancement` already exists; do not invent new labels.

Body fields (roughly four):
1. `textarea` **What problem are you trying to solve?** — `required: true`. Problem-first, not solution-first: the placeholder should ask what they were doing and where they got stuck. This ordering is the point of the form — it is what makes requests triageable instead of a wishlist of pre-decided solutions.
2. `textarea` **What would you like to happen?** — `required: true`.
3. `dropdown` **Area** — `required: false`. Reuse the exact same option list as `bug_report.yml` so the two forms stay consistent; if you change one list, change both.
4. `textarea` **Anything else?** — `required: false`. Alternatives considered, prior art, links, mockups.

Add a leading `markdown` block noting that the roadmap and existing plans may already cover the idea, with a link to `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

Deliberately omit a contribution-willingness checkbox and a priority dropdown — self-reported priority is noise, and the willingness checkbox is better asked in the thread once the idea is accepted.
requirements: ["File is at .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.yml with a .yml extension", "Valid YAML that parses cleanly", "Uses the issue-forms schema with unique ids on every body field", "labels: contains only enhancement", "Exactly two required fields: the problem, and the desired outcome", "Problem field appears before the desired-outcome field in body order", "Area dropdown options are byte-identical to the ones in bug_report.yml", "No priority dropdown and no contribution-willingness checkbox"]
summary: A short GitHub Issue Form for feature requests — ~4 fields, problem-first framing.
title: Add .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.yml

description:
Every job uses `fetch-depth: 0`, a full-history clone of a 47 MB repo, three-plus times per CI run. Real time and (on paid runners) real money, plus bandwidth on every run.

- `build` genuinely needs history for `nrwl/nx-set-shas` to locate the last successful `main` run.
- `changes` does not (covered by task 4).
- `nx-dependency-graph` and the gated `vercel-deploy` jobs should be audited the same way.

Options for the jobs that do need history:
1. `filter: blob:none` on `actions/checkout` — a partial clone fetches commit/tree objects but not historical blobs. Usually the best fit for `nx affected`, which needs the commit graph, not old file contents.
2. A bounded `fetch-depth` large enough to reach the base SHA, with a fallback deepen when it is not found. More fragile — prefer option 1.

Verify `nx affected` still computes an identical project set before and after on the same commit pair; a silently-wrong affected set would under-test rather than fail loudly, which is the dangerous outcome here.
requirements: ["Partial clone or bounded depth applied to every job, with per-job justification for anything still at depth 0", "nx-set-shas still resolves the last successful main run", "nx affected project set verified identical before/after on the same commit pair", "Checkout step duration recorded before/after"]
title: Reduce checkout cost: stop full-cloning a 47 MB repo on every job

description:
Before changing anything, attribute the spend. Three candidates, and the fix order depends on their relative size:

1. **Blacksmith runner minutes** — read the Blacksmith dashboard/invoice for billed minutes over 30 days. Cross-check against observed volume (~2,300 CI runs/month; `build` avg 5.3 min plus two satellite runner startups per run).
2. **GCS egress + operations** on `gs://openthrottle-staging-nx-cache` — the one nobody has measured. Use GCP billing export or Cloud Monitoring (`storage.googleapis.com/network/sent_bytes_count`, plus Class A/B op counts) filtered to that bucket for 30 days. Runners are on Azure, so every cache read is internet-rate egress.
3. **Nx Powerpack (`NX_KEY`)** — confirm whether the key is a paid plan or Nx's free-for-OSS grant. `@nx/gcs-cache` is a Powerpack plugin; if paid, task 3 removes that dependency too.

**Deliverable:** a table (runner minutes | GCS egress GB + $ | Nx licence | runs per workflow) appended via `append_plan_output`. Every later task states its saving against these numbers.

**Why first:** the plan assumes runner minutes dominate. If GCS egress is bigger, task 3 jumps ahead of task 2.
requirements: ["Blacksmith billed minutes for last 30 days recorded", "GCS egress bytes + dollars for the cache bucket over 30 days recorded", "NX_KEY licence status confirmed (paid vs OSS grant)", "30-day run count per workflow recorded", "Baseline table appended to plan output"]

description:
Guard the key gotcha: the gate must migrate the exact Postgres the server will connect to.

- Root `database:migrate` uses repo-root `.env` + `POSTGRES_HOST='localhost'`. The server (`nest start`, `cwd={projectRoot}`) reads `applications/openthrottle-server/.env`. summary: Confirm the gate resolves the SAME Postgres the server connects to; reconcile root .env vs applications/openthrottle-server/.env if they diverge.

description:
The real work. Today `scripts/parallelize-tasks.ts` answers exactly one question — "which projects are mine?" — and deals every affected project to exactly ONE chunk. `openthrottle-developer:test` now needs to run on ALL THREE boxes with different `--shard` arguments, which cuts across that contract.

## Constraints that must survive

- **`getShardSelectionErrors()` must keep holding.** Its whole point is that a project cannot silently fall off every box while CI reports green. If the developer app is special-cased out of the `--exclude` selector for `test`, the round-trip check must be taught about that exception explicitly rather than having the exception quietly widen `unexpected`.
- **`lint`/`typecheck` stay on the existing project-partition path.** They are 5.5% and 6.1% of the heavy box; they do not need this and must not be destabilised by it.
- The script's stdout remains the machine-read contract (single line, empty = empty shard); diagnostics stay on stderr.
- The header JSDoc's "Deliberately NOT parameterized by target" rationale is about the quoting hazard (no argv slot may contain a space). If this change introduces a second output, keep that property or rewrite the rationale honestly — do not leave the comment asserting something that stopped being true.
- The `!project` direct-naming warning (vs `!tag:name:`) still applies to anything new that builds a selector.

## Two shapes to choose between (task 2's decision may force one)

- **A — special-case out:** the app is removed from the `test` partition entirely and the workflow runs its sharded `test` unconditionally on every box. Simplest partitioner change; the round-trip check needs an explicit allowance.
- **B — shard-aware partition:** the partitioner grows a notion of per-project shard assignment and emits, alongside the exclude selector, this box's shard argument for the sharded project. Keeps one source of truth for "who runs what", at the cost of a second output channel.

Pick one, and write down why the other was rejected — the next person will ask.

## Also handle

- The developer app is only sharded when it is IN the affected set. On a PR that does not touch it, nothing should shard and no box should invent work.
- Interaction with `distributeEvenly()`: with the heaviest app pulled out of the `test` deal, the applications-first bias is rebalancing against a different weight distribution. Note it; do not re-tune it here.

## Tests

Extend `scripts/__tests__/parallelize-tasks.test.ts` (it already covers `getIsPackage`, `splitProjects`, `getChunkIndex`, `distributeEvenly`, `getExcludeSelector`, `getShardSelectionErrors`, `getShardSelector`). New cases must include: developer app affected vs not affected; every affected project still covered exactly once across the three chunks; and the round-trip check still failing loudly on a genuinely dropped project.

## Done when

`pnpm nx run monorepo:test` is green, the new behaviour is unit-tested, and the exported surface is still pure/testable with the Nx calls confined to `verifyShardSelection()` / `getAffectedProjects()`.
title: Teach scripts/parallelize-tasks.ts about per-suite sharding without breaking the round-trip
