description:
Follow-up from task `96f1c030`, which was SKIPPED this run because its "safe to delete" verdict was wrong.

## Problem

`packages/openthrottle-mcp/src/bin-http.ts`, `src/run-server-http.ts`, `src/http/mcp-http-auth.middleware.ts`, `esbuild.http.mjs`, and the package's `esbuild` devDependency are all load-bearing for the containerised streamable-HTTP MCP surface:

- `Dockerfile.NestJS:155` (`mcp-development` stage) — `CMD ["sh", "-c", "node_modules/.bin/tsx packages/openthrottle-mcp/src/bin-http.ts"]`
- `Dockerfile.NestJS:181` (`mcp-build` stage) — `RUN node packages/openthrottle-mcp/esbuild.http.mjs`
- `Dockerfile.NestJS:192` (`mcp` distroless stage, "the shippable image") — `CMD ["bin-http.mjs"]`
- `docker-compose.yml:497` `mcp` service (prod profile, `image: openthrottle/mcp:latest`) and `docker-compose.yml:531` `mcp-dev` service (`develop.watch` hot reload)

Because knip only follows the TypeScript import graph and these are shell-invoked container entrypoints, knip reports the whole cluster under `Unused files` and `esbuild` under unused devDependencies — every single weekly sweep. That recurring false positive already produced one task instructing deletion, whose ADDENDUM wrongly asserted the Docker grep was clean. Deleting would have broken the `mcp`/`mcp-dev` compose services and stripped the published image's entrypoint.

## Work

Teach knip about the entrypoints rather than re-triaging them by hand each week. In the knip config that covers `packages/openthrottle-mcp` (the `monorepo:knip` target's config):

1. Add `src/bin-http.ts` to the package's `entry` patterns, so `run-server-http.ts` and `http/mcp-http-auth.middleware.ts` become reachable through the normal import graph and drop off the report on their own.
2. Add `esbuild.http.mjs` to `entry` (it is a build script invoked by `node`, not imported), which should also clear the `esbuild` devDependency hit. If it does not, add `esbuild` to that project's `ignoreDependencies`.
3. Leave a short comment at each addition naming the Dockerfile stage that invokes it, so the next reader does not have to re-derive why a file with no importer is an entry.

While there: check whether the same blind spot affects the other Docker/CI-invoked entrypoints the plan description already lists as known false positives (`bootstrap.ts`, `ensure-migrations.ts`, `generate-mock-mail-fixture.mjs`, `sync-subtree.sh`). If they are cheap to declare the same way, do it in this pass — the point is to shrink the recurring manual-triage surface, not just to patch this one cluster.

## Acceptance criteria

- `pnpm nx run monorepo:knip` no longer reports `bin-http.ts`, `run-server-http.ts`, `http/mcp-http-auth.middleware.ts`, or `esbuild.http.mjs` as unused files, and no longer reports `esbuild` as an unused devDependency for `openthrottle-mcp`.
- No source file under `packages/openthrottle-mcp/src` is deleted or modified by this task — it is a config-only change.
- `docker compose --profile prod build mcp` still builds (or, if Docker is unavailable in the working environment, confirm by inspection that no Dockerfile/compose reference was touched).
- `pnpm nx run @openthrottle/openthrottle-mcp:build` and `:test` stay green.
summary: The openthrottle-mcp HTTP cluster is a shipped Docker entrypoint with no in-repo importer, so knip reports it as unused every sweep — it nearly got deleted this run. Declare the entrypoints in knip config instead.
title: knip config: register the Docker-invoked MCP HTTP entrypoints so they stop reporting as dead

description:
The two failures documented in `skills/ot-claude-loop/SKILL.md` — two tasks `IN_PROGRESS` at once, and a plan marked `COMPLETED` with open tasks — are exactly what a hook can catch, since there is no server-side reconcile in either direction.

Checks (all only when a plan is bound to the session):

1. `PreToolUse` on `update_task` → `IN_PROGRESS`: if another task on the plan is already `IN_PROGRESS`, refuse with a reason naming the task whose step-4 flip was skipped.
2. `PreToolUse` on `update_plan` → `COMPLETED`: if any task is still `IN_PROGRESS` / `PENDING` / `QUEUED`, refuse and list them.
3. `Stop`: if the session leaves a task `IN_PROGRESS` whose work was already committed, surface it so the next turn fixes it rather than stranding it.

Rules:

- **Opt-in and staged.** Default mode is `warn` (inject context, never block), promoted to `block` per check via env/config. Ship warn-only, soak on a real loop, then escalate. A wedged loop is worse than a stranded task.
- **Fail-open on infrastructure.** Server unreachable, no plan bound, ambiguous state → allow. Never block because OT was down. Every check needs a short timeout.
- Reasons must be actionable: which task, which flip, what to run — the agent should be able to self-correct from the message alone.
- Tests per check: violating state blocks (in block mode) / warns (in warn mode), clean state passes, server-down passes, no-plan-bound passes.
summary: PreToolUse/Stop guards against double IN_PROGRESS and premature plan COMPLETED, warn-mode first with fail-open on infra.
title: Enforce the loop invariants: block the known stranding failures

description:
Addresses hypothesis 1. Today `createCursorAgentSession()` returns `stdout.trim()` verbatim — so any banner, update notice, consent line, spinner, or ANSI byte on a cold run becomes the "session id", and the follow-up `--resume <garbage>` fails.

Work:
- Add a `parseCursorChatId(stdout: string): string | null` helper (new file, e.g. `cursor-agent/session-id.ts`, with its own tests). It should: strip ANSI escape sequences and a leading BOM, split on newlines, and select the line that actually looks like a chat id.
- Determine the real id shape from task 1's captured output before writing the matcher. If it is a UUID, validate as a UUID; if it is some other opaque token, validate conservatively (single token, no whitespace, plausible charset/length) rather than inventing a strict format that a future cursor release breaks.
- Reject-and-throw with the captured stdout when no line matches, rather than silently returning junk.
- Keep the tolerant path: prefer the **last** matching line, since banners print first.

Tests in `cursor-agent/__tests__/`: clean id; id preceded by an update banner; id with ANSI color codes; id with CRLF line endings; stdout with no id at all (throws, message contains the raw output); multi-line stdout where only the last line is an id.

description:
Beat 0:25 is "Click New rule; pick a tag; pick an action" over "Making one is two choices. The label to watch, and what to do."

`RuleForm.tsx` submits `title`, `tagAll` (one hidden input per selected tag), `actionType`, `actionPayloadJson`, `status`, `environment`, `tagAllow` and `enabled`. `RuleFormMatchSection` drives the tag match; `RuleFormActionSection` drives the action type.

Two problems. `actionPayloadJson` is raw JSON - typing a JSON blob on camera is the opposite of "two choices", and an `inject-task` rule with an empty payload may not produce anything visible, which would break the 0:42 payoff. And the two available action types are agent-plumbing concepts whose names do not read as "what to do about it" to a cold viewer.

Decide: either the flow touches exactly two controls and everything else is prefilled or defaulted - in which case verify on screen that a rule created that way actually fires, do not assume it - or the narration changes. Also check whether `/rules` shows `RulesIntroduction` (the onboarding empty state) rather than `RulesTable` when the list is short, because an onboarding pitch in frame changes what beat 0:09 is showing.

Record the decision here; if the narration changes, re-run `pnpm exec tsx scripts/validate-video-scripts.ts` against the 74-word budget.

description:
Create `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml` as a GitHub **Issue Form** (YAML schema), not a legacy Markdown template.

Top-level keys:
- `name: Bug Report`
- `description:` one line, e.g. `Something in OpenThrottle isn't working the way it should.`
- `title: '[Bug]: '`
- `labels: ['bug']` — `bug` already exists in the repo; do not add labels that don't exist.

Body fields (keep it to roughly these five — resist adding more):
1. `textarea` **What happened?** — `required: true`. Placeholder should ask for what they did, what they expected, and what they got instead. This single field replaces separate expected/actual/steps fields; that collapse is the main thing keeping the form lightweight.
2. `textarea` **Steps to reproduce** — `required: true`, numbered-list placeholder.
3. `dropdown` **Area** — `required: false`, multiple: false. Options drawn from the actual workspace layout: `openthrottle-server`, `openthrottle-developer`, `openthrottle-admin`, `openthrottle-website`, `openthrottle-email`, `packages / shared libraries`, `CLI / agentic tooling`, `Database / migrations`, `Build, Nx or CI`, `Not sure`. Verify these names against `applications/` and `packages/` before writing them.
4. `textarea` **Environment** — `required: false`, `render: shell` so it monospaces. Placeholder prompts for OS, Node version, pnpm version, and browser if relevant. Do NOT make this required — it is the field most likely to make a reporter give up.
5. `textarea` **Logs or screenshots** — `required: false`, `render: shell` or plain.

Also add a leading `markdown` block with one friendly sentence and a pointer to `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

Deliberately omit: version dropdowns (there is no published version scheme to pin to yet), a code-of-conduct acknowledgement checkbox (no `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` exists — adding a checkbox that links nowhere is worse than no checkbox), and a 'searched existing issues' checkbox (adds friction, rarely honest).
requirements: ["File is at .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml with a .yml extension", "Valid YAML that parses cleanly (e.g. via node -e with a YAML parser, or python3 -c 'import yaml,sys; yaml.safe_load(...)')", "Uses the issue-forms schema: top-level name/description/title/labels/body, body entries with type + id + attributes", "Every body field has a unique id", "labels: contains only labels that already exist in OpenThrottle/monorepo (bug)", "Exactly two fields are required: what happened, and steps to reproduce", "Area dropdown options match real application/package names in the workspace", "No version dropdown, no code-of-conduct checkbox, no 'I searched existing issues' checkbox"]
summary: A short GitHub Issue Form for bug reports — ~5 fields, only the triage-blocking ones required.
title: Add .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml

description:
Found by task 6 on run 32214813250. Task 4's done-criterion says the workflow log must make legible "how many files that shard collected". It does not.

## The symptom

On all three legs of PR #402, the developer suite's Vitest summary is **missing**:

- No `Test Files N passed (N)` for `openthrottle-developer` on any leg — only `monorepo`'s survives (leg 1, `15 passed (15)`).
- Per-file `✓` lines are truncated: 422 of 679 survive across the three legs combined (83 / 182 / 157 against expected 227 / 226 / 226).
- Nx's own `Successfully ran target test …` banner for the sharded `run-many` is absent too.
- Every line inside the task's output group carries one identical timestamp — Nx buffers the whole task output and emits it as a block, and the block is being truncated.

Correctness was never in doubt — task 6 settled it by reimplementing `BaseSequencer.shard()` and confirming **zero** misassigned files and zero cross-leg overlap. The problem is that the check the PR asks a reviewer to perform ("read the file counts, not the colour") cannot actually be performed from the log.

## Why this matters more than it looks

The whole plan's failure mode is silent-passing. The file-count check is the designated tripwire, and a tripwire nobody can read is worse than no tripwire — it invites a reviewer to tick the box on a green ✅ without the number ever having been visible.

## Do

1. Make the count survive into the log. First thing to try is `--outputStyle=stream` on the sharded `run-many` invocation, so Vitest's output pipes through live instead of being buffered into an Nx group. Confirm on a real CI run — this cannot be reproduced locally, where the summary prints fine.
2. If streaming alone does not do it, consider an explicit echo of the count (e.g. `vitest list --shard=… | wc -l` before the run), but prefer the real summary over a recomputed number — a recomputed count that drifts from what actually ran would be its own silent-pass.
3. Whatever lands, re-run CI and paste the three legs' counts into this plan's output, confirming they sum to the full-suite total.
4. Update the PR checklist item if the shape of the evidence changes.

## Done when

A reviewer can open any `build` leg and read, without tooling, how many developer test files that box collected — and the three numbers sum to the full suite.
title: Make the sharded suite's collected file count legible in the CI log

description:
Four docs currently overlap on "fresh clone → running", and `docs/README.md` § Getting started (lines 8–11) lists all four as peers with no ordering signal.

**Verified current state (2026-08-28)**

- `docs/openthrottle/local-quickstart.md` (10K) — the ordered fresh-clone path. Referrers: root `README.md`, `docs/README.md`, `mcp-registration.md`, `first-time-onboarding.md`, `.agents/personas/growth.md`, `openthrottle-website/app/routing/home/demo/data.landing.ts`.
- `docs/openthrottle/first-time-onboarding.md` (15K) — mental model + copy-paste prompt sequence. Referrers include `AGENTS.md`, `docs/README.md`, `authoring-plans-via-mcp.md`, two personas.
- `docs/openthrottle/run-openthrottle-server-developer.md` (13K) — daily native loop. Referrers include `AGENTS.md`, `databases/README.md`, `skills/ot-stack/SKILL.md`, `packages/openthrottle-mcp/docs/verification-environment.md`, two personas.
- `docs/openthrottle/run-locally-oss.md` (5.5K) — confirmed positioning, not usage: line 3 is a **Positioning:** block, line 5 says "Use this doc for README, website, or pitch copy", and the only sections are "Key message", "What runs locally (OSS)", "Optional vs required for local-only".

**Do**

1. Keep all three usage docs but make the split explicit — add a one-line scope banner at the top of each stating what it is and pointing at the other two: quickstart = the ordered fresh-clone path; first-time-onboarding = mental model + prompt sequence; run-openthrottle-server-developer = the daily native loop. Delete overlapping setup steps from the two non-canonical docs and link to quickstart instead.
2. Relocate `run-locally-oss.md`'s positioning content into `docs/openthrottle/features.md` (or the marketing tree) and delete the doc.
3. `run-locally-oss.md` carries two facts that are cited from code, not marketing — the Ollama/embeddings requirement and the launcher note. Before deleting, rehome those and update the two citing comments: `scripts/verify-openthrottle-mcp-env.ts:90` and `scripts/run-openthrottle-mcp.ts:269`. Also fix the doc's stale reference to `scripts/run-openthrottle-mcp.sh` — scripts moved to tsx in b6a359bf.
4. Update the remaining 6 doc referrers of `run-locally-oss.md` (`docs/README.md`, `monorepo/openthrottle-developer-vite-devtools.md`, `openthrottle/monorepo-architecture.md`, the three getting-started docs, `packages/openthrottle-mcp/README.md`, `packages/openthrottle-mcp/docs/verification-environment.md`, `applications/openthrottle/README.md`).
5. Rewrite `docs/README.md` § Getting started as an ordered path (quickstart first, then onboarding, then daily loop) rather than a flat list of four peers.

**Out of scope:** collapsing the three usage docs into one — the referrer sets are distinct enough (AGENTS.md and skills point at the daily loop; the website points at quickstart) that a merge is a separate call.

description:
## Finding
Found while running the full-workspace test sweep for this plan. **Not caused by this plan's work — `main` is already red.**

```
FAIL packages/openthrottle-skills/src/frontmatter/__tests__/parse-yaml-frontmatter.corpus.test.ts
  > parseYamlFrontmatter corpus regression
  > the current .agents corpus is non-empty (sanity check for the walk itself)

AssertionError: expected 36 to be greater than 40
  at parse-yaml-frontmatter.corpus.test.ts:378
```

## Root cause
`4ceff2ab refactor(monorepo): trim the skill catalog from 44 skills to 20 (#417)` shrank the `.agents` corpus. The corpus walk now finds **36** files (`.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md` + `.agents/rules/**/*.mdc` + `.agents/personas/*.md`), but this sanity check still hardcodes:

```ts
expect(corpusFiles.length).toBeGreaterThan(40);
```

Every other test in the file passes — all 37 per-file parse-equivalence assertions are green. Only the hardcoded floor is stale.

## Confirmed pre-existing
```bash
git merge-base --is-ancestor 4ceff2ab main   # exits 0 — the trim is on main
```
My branch is based on `main` @ `2bf4b614` and touches nothing under `.agents/`, `packages/openthrottle-skills/`, or the skills tooling.

## Why I did not just fix it
The guard's stated purpose is to catch the *walk itself* silently returning nothing. Picking the replacement floor is a judgement call about how much headroom to leave below the current 36 — and whoever owns the trim should confirm 36 is the intended steady state rather than a partially-applied migration. Changing someone's deliberate guard threshold as a drive-by inside a performance PR is the wrong place for that call.

## Proposed fix
Lower the floor to a value that still catches a broken walk but tolerates the trimmed catalog (e.g. `toBeGreaterThan(25)`), or derive it from the count of `skills/*` directories so it cannot go stale again the next time the catalog is resized.

## Acceptance
`pnpm nx run @openthrottle/openthrottle-skills:test --skip-nx-cache` is green, and the guard still fails if the corpus walk returns an empty or near-empty list.
summary: RESOLVED — the fix shipped in PR #422 (696a4740), despite that PR's body stating it was "filed separately rather than adjusting someone else's guard". The diff lowered the floor from `toBeGreaterThan(40)` to `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(36)` in packages/openthrottle-skills/src/frontmatter/__tests__/parse-yaml-frontmatter.corpus.test.ts:378. Verified on main 2026-08-23: @openthrottle/openthrottle-skills:test is green, 238/238 across 16 files. Note the chosen form pins the floor at exactly the current corpus size, so the next catalog resize will make it stale again — deriving it from the skills/* directory count (the task's second proposal) remains the durable fix, but the acceptance criterion as written is met. Closed by reconciliation plan e1b32fde.
title: 13. BUG (pre-existing on main): skill-catalog trim left a stale >40 corpus guard failing

description:

Set up: seed a fixture real directory `.agents/skills/<some-slug>/SKILL.md` whose slug is absent from `skills-lock.json`. Run the developer app against the seeded developer user (admin) per the live-verify recipe; use a built server on an isolated port if the main checkout's dev ports are in use.

Verify on `/skills`:
- the fixture skill renders with the **Custom** badge, not External, and with no origin link.
- the Custom filter segment narrows to it; All still shows everything; a lockfile skill still reads External with its origin URL; a `skills/` skill still reads OpenThrottle; a personal skill still reads Personal.
- opening the fixture skill's detail page allows editing, and a save round-trips to disk.

Verify on `/skills/create`:
- with `FEATURE_BETA_PREVIEW=true`: three destinations; creating a Custom skill writes `.agents/skills/<slug>/SKILL.md` as a real directory, it appears on `/skills` as Custom, and `git status` shows it as an untracked directory (i.e. committable — the `!.agents/skills/*/` rescue works).
- with the flag off: two destinations, and a hand-crafted POST with `destination=openthrottle` is refused inline with nothing written.

Screenshot the four-tier list and both create-form states.

Then run the developer app's four gates sequentially — never in parallel, the Nx cache is shared: `typecheck`, `lint`, `test`, `build`. Clean up the fixture directory afterwards.
requirements: ["A fixture real directory absent from the lockfile renders and filters as Custom in the running app", "A Custom skill is editable and a save round-trips to disk", "A Custom create lands as a real, untracked, committable directory", "Both FEATURE_BETA_PREVIEW states verified, including a refused hand-crafted openthrottle POST", "typecheck, lint, test and build all pass for openthrottle-developer, run sequentially", "Screenshots captured and the fixture removed"]

description:
Branch is a mix of enqueue-time and worker-start-time knowledge, so rather than trying to infer it late, FLIP it: make branch an explicit REQUIRED input supplied at kickoff, so we always have it and can fail fast and loud when it's absent (preferred path).

Enforcement points:
1. GraphQL enqueue input — add a required `branch` field to `EnqueuePlanRunInput` (and the Ralph orchestrator enqueue input) in `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/plans/*`; validate non-empty at the resolver / `plan-enqueue.service.ts` boundary and throw a clear error if missing. Persist to `plan_runs.branch` via `recordQueuedRun`.
2. Skills — thread branch through as an ARG in the agent/Ralph kickoff skills that enqueue runs (e.g. agents-ralph and any `/ot` run-launch skills under `skills/`), so the CLI/agent path always passes it.
3. UI — supply branch from the Developer-app launch surfaces (run-config / launch dialog) so interactive kickoff always sends it.

DB semantics: keep the `plan_runs.branch` COLUMN nullable so legacy/backfilled rows survive; enforcement is at the INPUT boundary, not a DB NOT NULL constraint. New runs must supply branch or fail.

Optional convenience: derive a DEFAULT to pre-fill the UI/skill (worktree name, or `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` of the resolved working dir, reusing cached `repository_checkouts.inspection` where possible) — but the value is still passed explicitly, not silently inferred server-side.

Validate: enqueue without branch → fails loudly; enqueue with branch (via skill arg and via UI) → `plan_runs.branch` populated and matches.
requirements: ["EnqueuePlanRunInput (+ orchestrator input) has a required branch field; missing branch fails fast", "Kickoff skills pass branch as an explicit arg", "Developer-app launch surfaces send branch", "plan_runs.branch column stays nullable (legacy rows); enforcement at input boundary", "Optional default pre-fill (worktree name / HEAD) but value passed explicitly, never silently inferred"]
title: Require branch as an explicit kickoff input (skill args + UI), fail fast if missing

Decide, and if the beat changes, change the episode — not just the flow.

Done when each records identically twice, and no take depends on a model being reachable.

description:
Verify — by reading, and by dispatching where possible — that the CI workflow behaves correctly for a `merge_group` event BEFORE any queue is enabled. Fix what is wrong; leave what is already right alone and say so.

Checklist, each item resolved to verified-correct or changed:

1. **`changes` gate** (`continuous-integration.yml:100-187`): line 124 short-circuits every non-`pull_request` event to `run=true`/`deps=true`/`graph=true`. Confirm a merge-group entry therefore always runs the FULL build, including the two `deps`-gated licence scans and the `graph`-gated circular-dependency check. Expected: already correct, no change.
2. **`build` job `if`** (line 194): `github.event_name != 'pull_request' || draft == false` — merge_group has no PR payload, so it passes. Confirm.
3. **Concurrency** (lines 56-58 and 202-204): merge-queue refs are `refs/heads/gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-N-<sha>`, unique per entry, so `cancel-in-progress` never actually cancels a sibling entry. Confirm that reading, then REWRITE the comment block, which today reasons only about PR-vs-main and will otherwise mislead the next reader.
4. **`nrwl/nx-set-shas`** (line 288) on `merge_group`: determine what `NX_BASE`/`NX_HEAD` resolve to. This is the one item that must be settled empirically, not by reading docs — a base that is too new means the queue build runs a SMALLER affected set than the PR build did, which is silent-passing. If it does not resolve sensibly, pin the base explicitly for `merge_group` (e.g. to `github.event.merge_group.base_sha`).
5. **Prettier format-check** (line 461): the `!= 'pull_request'` branch means merge-group entries do the full-tree sweep. That is correct and intentional (the "everything on main is formatted" guarantee); confirm and leave.
6. **Stale comment** (line 245): "💰 No merge queue on this plan, so the ready PR is the gate" — must be rewritten as part of this plan, not left to rot.
7. **`ci-success`** (line 520): confirm it reports on `merge_group` runs under the exact same context name, since that string is what branch protection requires.

Validate with `pnpm run check:local` where the change touches anything Prettier/actionlint covers. Do not enable the queue in this task.

description:
Close trap 1 permanently rather than relying on the current lucky state.

Today only `ci-success` is required and only `continuous-integration.yml` carries the `merge_group` trigger, so nothing stalls. But `secret-scan.yml`, `openthrottle-docker.yml`, `terraform-validate.yml`, and `vercel-deploy.yml` are all `pull_request`-triggered and none has `merge_group`. The moment someone marks one required, every queue entry waits out `check_response_timeout_minutes` and gets dequeued — with no error message that points at the cause.

Do:

1. Decide per workflow whether it SHOULD run in the queue. Reasoning to apply: `secret-scan` is a correctness gate over content that the queue's rewritten commit could in principle differ on — a strong candidate for `merge_group`. `vercel-deploy` produces preview deployments for PRs — deploying from a throwaway queue ref is almost certainly wrong; document that it is deliberately PR-only. `terraform-validate` and `openthrottle-docker` are path-gated; note that a `merge_group` trigger cannot use the same `pull_request` path filters and decide accordingly.
2. Add `merge_group: types: [checks_requested]` to whichever workflows the step above says should run in the queue, with a header comment explaining why.
3. Write the rule down where it will be seen — `docs/monorepo/ci-cost.md` § "Checklist: before you add a workflow or job" already exists and is the right home: **a check may only be marked required on `main` if its workflow triggers on `merge_group`.**
4. Consider enforcing it mechanically (a small script comparing the required-check list from the GitHub API against workflows carrying a `merge_group` trigger). If you skip the automation, say so explicitly and why — do not leave it implied.

Validate: `pnpm run check:local` plus a manual `workflow_dispatch`/PR run proving nothing regressed on the existing PR path.
title: Required-check hygiene: make merge_group a precondition for requiring any check

description:

Must fail before task 3 lands, with `?? .openthrottle/`.

Assert the distinction the plan rests on, not just the clean status — this is what stops a later change from over-excluding:
- `.openthrottle/workspace-editors.json` is hidden from git;
- the editor config the user asked for (`.mcp.json` or the editor's equivalent) is still present on disk AND still visible to git, i.e. NOT excluded.

Fixture gotcha carried from OT b409da6e: build the repo layout and commit it BEFORE applying config. A layout created after the initial commit leaves the baseline dirty, and the test then passes or fails for the wrong reason. Assert the baseline is clean before acting.

Note the service writes MCP config only when `scripts/run-openthrottle-mcp.sh` exists in the repo (otherwise it warns and skips), so the fixture needs that file for the not-excluded assertion to mean anything.
requirements: ["Test fails before the fix with `?? .openthrottle/`", "Asserts the clean baseline before applying, so the result is meaningful", "Asserts the user's MCP config is present and NOT excluded", "Fixture cleans up its temp repo"]
summary: 2 tests landed (a90f17fc); the manifest one fails as intended. CORRECTED this task's stated requirement: "git status --porcelain stays EMPTY" is the wrong goal — applying also writes .cursor/mcp.json, a legitimate new untracked file the user asked for. Implementing the requirement literally would have invited excluding everything the apply writes, hiding the user's own config. Real invariant, now asserted per-path via check-ignore: OT bookkeeping is ignored, user-requested files stay visible.
title: Add a failing test: applying editor config leaves a foreign repo dirty

Everything above is a one-time scrub; without a guard the same drift returns, because nothing today connects the env-var docs to the code that reads them. Two knobs were documented into existence and nothing caught it.

There is already a precedent to extend rather than a new harness to build: `applications/openthrottle-server/src/services/worktree-root/worktree-root-default.test.ts` asserts that `skills/ot-worktree/scripts/root.sh` contains the expected default, i.e. it already reads a file across the repo boundary to pin a cross-surface fact.

Add an assertion in the same spirit: every `OPENTHROTTLE_WORKTREE_*` name appearing in `docs/monorepo/environment-variables.md` and `skills/ot-worktree/references/contract.md` must appear in `skills/ot-worktree/scripts/root.sh` or under `applications/openthrottle-server/src`. description:
Two script edits.

**There is no note title.** Beat 0:08 is "type a title" and 0:18 is "type two sentences of body text". `NoteForm.tsx` renders a single `Label htmlFor="content"` over one `content` field. `notes.create.tsx` submits `{ input: { content: parsed.data.content } }`. `CreateNoteInput` in `notes.create.tsx.graphql` is `{ content: String!, author: String }`. `NotesTable` derives its row label from the content via `notePreviewLabel`. Two beats and about ten seconds of runtime collapse into one action.

That is not purely a loss - "a note is just the thing you would have put in a Slack message and lost" is a *better* line over a single free-text box than over a titled form, so the collapse can be spent on the narration rather than backfilled with a new beat.

**`blockedOn: []` is wrong.** Set it to name the dependency task 1 settles on. This matters beyond bookkeeping: `docs/marketing/publishing.md` and `docs/marketing/catalogue-rebuild.md` read script frontmatter to decide what is producible, so a script that lies about being unblocked gets picked up by a scheduled rebuild and fails late instead of early.

Re-run `pnpm exec tsx scripts/validate-video-scripts.ts` after both edits - the frontmatter budget is 68 spoken words.
summary: Notes have one content field, not a title and a body; and the script claims blockedOn: [] while being blocked.
title: Collapse the title beat and fix the blockedOn frontmatter

DECISION LOCKED (owner, 2026-08-13): Auto-rotate.

When `bootstrap-service-account-credentials.ts` runs with the env var unset, an active credential already existing, AND the key absent from `.demo-workstation.local`, self-heal by rotating: revoke the existing active credential(s) for that bootstrap account, mint a fresh one, and write the new token to the file. Setup always ends with a complete six-field file.

Guardrails for the implementation (task 3):
- Rotation is restricted to the two known BOOTSTRAP_ACCOUNTS (openthrottle-mcp, workflow-ralph) ONLY — never a generalized revoke of arbitrary service accounts.
- Rotate only when the file key is genuinely ABSENT (not merely when a credential exists) — a complete file + matching credentials must stay a clean no-op.
- Accept that any already-distributed copy of the old token stops working; that is fine for local bootstrap accounts.

Acceptance: decision recorded (done); task 3 implements auto-rotate per these guardrails.
title: Lock design: rotate-vs-warn for the skip branch

description:
## The problem
Chat, /schedule, and Ralph each grew their own answer to the same questions — which checkout, which cwd, which worktree, which MCP servers, which concurrency key — and the last week made the split undeniable. Schedule now has `ScheduledAgentJobCheckoutPathService` + `repository_checkout_id` + `resolved_cwd` on job/run rows (`e199f3ae` / PR #399; entity columns in `scheduled-agent-job(-run).entity.ts`). Ralph still resolves cwd on a separate path, which is why plan [`18fb4027`](18fb4027-3849-43cc-844c-899a9992e6f0) exists as an explicit follow-up that says "do NOT add a third inline copy." Open PRs then pile on more one-surface fixes: default plan-run worktrees (#414), schedule concurrency keyed on the resolved directory (#415), MCP for headless/scheduled runs (`e22c613f` / #394 / open #395), agentic-hooks overlay into child repos (#416), plus in-flight schedule stats (`ee622b86` / #420) and live plan output (`7d9ff9f4` / #408). Parallel plans [`96bfd217`](96bfd217-cc2b-47a3-a9b2-5225887d5a5d) (harness lifecycle hooks) and [`69f47e25`](69f47e25-67c9-4687-8fed-c2286b15a6ed) (infra isolation for K>1) assume a coherent run identity that does not exist yet. This is one missing abstraction wearing five open tickets.

## The proposed change
Introduce a single typed **RunExecutionContext** (name flexible) owned in a shared package (likely generalize `ScheduledAgentJobCheckoutPathService` out of the schedule module into something like `@openthrottle/openthrottle-plan-config` or a small `nestjs-repositories` run-context module) with: `checkoutId`, fire-time `resolvedCwd`, worktree provisioning policy, MCP server set, concurrency key, model/provider, and provenance fields already on `plan_runs` from #280. Make the three launchers — conversation-stream / chat turn, scheduled-agent-jobs processor, agentic-ralph orchestrator — *callers* of that resolver, not owners of their own. Land mid-flight PRs (#414/#415) and plan 18fb4027 as migration steps onto the shared type rather than as permanent parallel paths. Document one cwd precedence ladder for all three surfaces.

## What it unlocks
Ends the fix-schedule-then-Ralph-then-chat cycle that produced this week's PR burst; gives Orchestration Engine (roadmap [`ce7e2773`](ce7e2773-3c71-4e8f-8229-11355d021723)) a real substrate so bounded-parallel orchestration (69f47e25) and harness hooks (96bfd217) have one run identity to bind to; makes "where did this run actually execute?" answerable the same way in the UI for chat, schedule, and plan runs.

## Rough size
6–10 days including migrating the three launchers and deleting the schedule-only service name. Touches `packages/nestjs-repositories` (checkout path service + plan-runs/scheduled-agent-jobs entities), `applications/openthrottle-server` (conversation-stream, scheduled-agent-jobs queue, agentic-ralph orchestrator), `packages/openthrottle-plan-config`, `packages/openthrottle-agentic-ralph`, `openthrottle-developer` (run provenance UI on plan + schedule detail).

## Migration risk
Medium — three production launch paths change. Mitigate: keep the shared resolver additive and nullable; migrate schedule first (already closest), then Ralph (18fb4027), then chat; feature-flag or env-gate worktree-default behavior from #414. Rollback: per-launcher flag to restore the previous resolution function; no forced data backfill if new columns stay nullable.

## The strongest argument against
The open PRs and plan 18fb4027 may *already* be the right decomposition — finishing them as scoped follow-ups could close the gap without inventing a new shared type that itself becomes a fourth thing to maintain. If schedule and Ralph converge on one service via 18fb4027 alone, and chat genuinely needs different semantics (interactive vs headless), a forced RunExecutionContext is architectural vanity. Wait until #414/#415/18fb4027 merge, then re-judge whether a third cwd bug still appears.
summary: Replace the parallel checkout/cwd/worktree/MCP/concurrency paths across chat, /schedule, and Ralph with one shared RunExecutionContext; treat mid-flight PRs as migration steps onto it.
title: Unify RunExecutionContext across chat, /schedule, and Ralph

description:
Carried from task `4d1be2e6` of plan `7aead6c5` (closed COMPLETED by `e1b32fde`).

## Measured composition of the 310.1 KB `calendar._index-*.js`
Established by ablation — stubbing `import 'temporal-polyfill/global'` in both `temporal-bootstrap.ts` and `datetime.ts` and rebuilding:

| Component | KB |
|---|---:|
| Temporal polyfill (Vite resolves `global.min.js`, 55.4 KB — exact match) | 55.7 |
| schedule-x engine + preact + calendar UI | 254.4 |
| **Total** | **310.1** |

The original ≤100 KB target was disproved: 254.4 KB remains after deleting Temporal outright. The `rrule` premise was also false — the library is not installed in the workspace at all.

## The decision
**A. Conditional polyfill.** Load `temporal-polyfill/global` only when `globalThis.Temporal === undefined`. Saves 55.7 KB on Temporal-native browsers. Cost: an async gate before calendar construction, because schedule-x v4 reads the global directly — so this is a load-order change, not a one-line guard. Check current baseline browser support before assuming the saving is real for most users.

**B. Accept ~310 KB** as the floor for a full-featured calendar and close this out.

## Already rejected — do not re-propose
- Splitting the optional schedule-x plugins: breaking change to `createSchedulingPlugins`, and no win on this route (it uses the all-enabled `DEFAULT_PLUGINS`).
- `React.lazy` on the calendar itself: defers bytes rather than removing them, and the calendar *is* the page content — trades a measured number for a blank-then-pop render.

## First step
Re-measure `calendar._index-*.js` on current `main` before deciding — #422's `sideEffects` work may have moved it.

## Acceptance
A decision is recorded (A or B). If A, the polyfill is conditional and the re-measured chunk is ~255 KB with the calendar rendering correctly on a browser without native Temporal.
title: DECIDE: load the Temporal polyfill conditionally on the calendar route?

description:
The generator templates are the source of truth for the shape, but a survey found them contradicting each other — so the SSOT would fail its own contract test (task 10) and generated modals/forms would fail the R3 marker rule. Normalize them BEFORE the contract test (ideally before the ESLint rule so it's authored against canonical templates). All under tools/generators/src/generators/:

Fixes:
- Modal + form templates emit `// 🔌 Short Circuits` (PLURAL); every other template is singular `// 🔌 Short Circuit`. Make all templates use the single canonical marker string (react-router/files/modal/__name__.tsx, react-router/files/form/components/__name__.tsx).
- `react` hook template uses `any` (`onCopy = (value: any)`, react/files/hook/__name__.tsx) — type it (`string`) to match the RR hook and the repo no-`any` rule.
- Hook import style diverges: RR hook uses `import * as React` + `React.useState`; `react` hook uses named `useState` import. Pick one (align to `import * as React` per the component templates) across both hook templates.
- `rest-service` module class is literally `class Module` with a decorator alias (nestjs/files/rest-service/__name__.module.ts) instead of `<namePascal>Module` — rename to match every other nestjs module.
- Static `.id` casing differs: modal uses `nameKebab`, form uses `name`. Pick one convention for component `.id` and apply to both.

Validation: run the generators (or the generator unit tests + tools/generators/.../template-conventions.test.ts) to confirm output still scaffolds and passes existing guards. Extend template-conventions.test.ts to assert the canonical singular Short Circuit marker + no `any` in hook templates so this drift can't recur. This task makes the generator↔enforcer contract test (task 10) achievable.
title: Normalize generator template drift so the SSOT is self-consistent

description:
Make OT-orchestrated runs in foreign repos carry the hooks without the user having installed anything.

`packages/openthrottle-drivers/src/drivers/claude.ts` builds a **shell command string**, not an argv array, so the flag has to be appended and escaped the same way everything else is. Follow the existing precedent exactly: `appendWorktreeShellFlags(base, capabilities, config.worktree)` plus `escapeShellArg` / `escapeForShellDoubleQuoted` from `../utils/shell.ts`. Do not hand-concatenate an unescaped path — the payload path can contain spaces.

Requirements:

- Resolve the payload path from task 2's artifact. Server-side resolution must survive the container bridge — reuse `getWorkspacePathMapping` (`packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/workspace-paths.ts`), which the skill materializer already relies on for exactly this.
- **Fail open.** If the payload is missing or unresolvable, emit the command without the flag and warn once. A telemetry overlay must never be able to break a run — this matches the hook core's own fail-open stance.
- Gate it: an env var and/or a run-config knob to disable injection. Default on is fine for OT-owned repos; the switch has to exist for repos the operator does not own (see the privacy-contract task).
- Do **not** add `--strict-mcp-config` or `--mcp-config` while in here. The driver comments call out that `--strict-mcp-config` would actively suppress the project `.mcp.json`; that warning still applies.
- Unit tests in `src/drivers/__tests__/` asserting the flag's presence, absence when gated off, and correct escaping.

After this lands, leg B is complete: orchestrated runs in any foreign repo get hooks, with nothing written to the target checkout.
summary: Leg B complete. Split ACROSS the existing package boundary rather than through it: `openthrottle-drivers` is documented as a dep-free leaf of pure descriptors that never touches the filesystem, and `agentic-utils` already depends on it, so importing `getWorkspacePathMapping` into the driver (as the task sketched) would have been a dependency cycle. The leaf gets a `pluginDir` capability, a `pluginDirs` invocation field, and `appendPluginDirShellFlags` (mirroring appendWorktreeShellFlags/appendMcpShellFlags, escaping every path via escapeShellArg since these are caller input, unlike the MCP flags); the impure resolver `resolveHookPluginDirs` lands in agentic-utils and is wired through tools/workflows' `toDriverConfig`. CORRECTION TO THE TASK'S ASSUMPTION: the container path bridge does NOT apply here. `toContainerPath` exists for host-recorded paths read out of the database (WorkspaceLocalRepository.filesystemPath, plan workingDirectory); the payload path is derived from this process's own filesystem via the existing `getOpenThrottleRoot`, so it is already in the same view the CLI is spawned into — translating it would break the containerized case rather than fix it. This is documented in the resolver's JSDoc so the next reader doesn't "fix" it. Fail-open throughout: gated off, unfindable OT root, missing payload, or a directory with no `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` all resolve to an empty list → no flag → an ordinary run. Warnings latch once per process, not once per iteration. Gate is `OPENTHROTTLE_HOOK_PLUGIN_ENABLED` (default ON, explicit falsy disables) plus `OPENTHROTTLE_HOOK_PLUGIN_DIR` to relocate the payload. Existence is checked via the plugin MANIFEST rather than the directory, so a half-staged payload degrades instead of handing the CLI something it rejects. Did not touch --mcp-config/--strict-mcp-config. 21 new tests across both packages cover presence, absence, blank-entry filtering, space quoting, metacharacter neutralization, repeated flags, flag ORDER (after --model, before worktree), that the other four drivers ignore pluginDirs, that --bare is never emitted, and every resolver failure mode including warn-once. All five drivers' capability fixtures updated (typecheck over test files caught four I would otherwise have missed). lint + typecheck + test green across drivers, agentic-utils (554 tests), and @tools/workflows.
title: Leg B — append --plugin-dir to the Claude driver's spawn command

Port `scripts/create_worktree.sh` → `skills/ot-worktree/scripts/create.sh` and `scripts/ensure_worktree.sh` → `skills/ot-worktree/scripts/heal.sh`, sourcing `common.sh`, `root.sh`, `provision.sh`.

`create.sh` keeps all three modes exactly as they behave today:
1. Name as `$1` (CLI / `pnpm worktree:new <name>`) — never reads stdin.
2. No name + piped stdin — Claude `WorktreeCreate` hook JSON payload; parse `.name // .worktree_name // .worktreeName // .worktree // .branch // .slug`, fall back to `wt-<first 8 of session_id>`, log the payload to `$TMPDIR`. Keep the `[ ! -t 0 ]` guard so an interactive TTY never blocks on `cat`.

Branch naming: today it is hardcoded `openthrottle/<name>`. Make the prefix configurable via `OT_WORKTREE_BRANCH_PREFIX` (default `openthrottle/`) so the skill is not OT-branded in a foreign repo; existing OT behavior must be unchanged by default. Keep the existing-branch checkout fallback.

Stdout contract is absolute: create.sh prints ONLY the worktree's absolute path.

description:
Design gate — do this before writing code. Pick between:

**A — resolve then exclude the real path.** realpath the target dir before materializing; record and exclude the resolved repo-relative path. Keeps injection working in symlinked layouts.

**B — refuse to inject through a symlinked target dir.** Skip it with a warning pointing at ot-skill-sync.

Recommendation from the investigation: A, with B as the fallback when the resolved path escapes the repo (git exclude cannot cover a path outside the worktree, so injecting there can never be made clean).

Things the decision must account for:
- A target dir symlinked to somewhere OUTSIDE the repo (exclude is powerless; must refuse).
- Two target dirs resolving to the SAME real directory (e.g. .claude/skills -> ../.agents/skills). Materializing both would collide on identical names; the ledger must not record the same real path twice.
- Target-owned name detection (scanTargetOwnedSkillNames) reads the same dirs and must see the resolved location, or a repo's own skills could be masked.

Record the decision in docs/monorepo/foreign-workspace-skill-injection.md §4 as part of task 5.
requirements: ["A written decision (A, B, or A-with-B-fallback) with the reasoning, recorded on the plan", "Explicit answer for the escapes-the-repo case", "Explicit answer for two target dirs resolving to the same real dir"]
summary: DECISION: option A with a B fallback — resolve the target dir, record and exclude the resolved repo-relative path; refuse only when it escapes the repo. Verified that git exclude can hide untracked entries inside a tracked dir (the load-bearing assumption). Key trap for task 3: scanTargetOwnedSkillNames builds keys from the un-resolved dir, and today only works because the ledger does too — both must move together or the fix silently uninjects the repo.
title: Decide the direction: resolve-and-exclude vs refuse-to-inject

Three small, independent repo-config defects found while auditing driver MCP attachment for plan a08e7d24. None are driver-contract issues, which is why they were not fixed there.

**1. `openthrottle-mcp-docker` is skipped entirely by Claude Code.** `claude mcp list` reports: *MCP server "openthrottle-mcp-docker" has a "url" but no "type"; add "type": "http"*. **2. The `openthrottle-mcp` `env` block is decorative and misleading.** `claude mcp list` warns *Missing environment variables: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENTHROTTLE_DEVELOPER_API_URL_EXTERNAL, OPENTHROTTLE_DEVELOPER_API_URL_INTERNAL, OPENTHROTTLE_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN*. **3. grok has no project MCP config.** `grok mcp list` reports "No MCP servers configured", so grok runs have no OT tools. Grok supports a project scope at `./.grok/config.toml` (`grok mcp add --scope project`). Consider committing one mirroring `.mcp.json`. Check `/skill-sync` and the agent/editor-folders docs first — adding a new agent config directory has fan-out implications, and `.grok/` may need a gitignore/SSOT decision.

Verify each with the CLI's own doctor/list command from a FRESH worktree, not the main checkout — per-path state makes the main checkout an unreliable witness.

description:
Document and decide the GraphQL evaluation contract the client SDK will call.

## Context
Today myFeatureFlags requires flags:read and AuthPrincipal. Product decision: evaluation must work for authenticated AND unauthenticated users; auth is enrichment for targeting/bucketing only. Admin CRUD stays behind flags:read / flags:write.

## Work
1. Compare rename/keep of myFeatureFlags vs new query (e.g. evaluateFeatureFlags / rolloutEvaluations) that is callable without FLAGS_READ.
2. Specify anonymous principal / bucketing strategy when no JWT (cookie/device anon id vs ephemeral request id). Prefer stable-enough client id so percentage split is not random on every refresh; sticky hashing remains out of scope for nestjs-rollout.
3. Decide how applicationKey (APP_NAME) is passed: GraphQL arg now (filter/log) vs client-only until server scoping exists. Prefer accepting applicationKey as an optional query arg early so clients can send APP_NAME without waiting for UUID mapping.
4. Write the accepted contract in the plan output / task summary (operation name, args, auth gate, response shape reuse of FeatureFlagObject).

## Acceptance criteria
- Chosen query name + auth gate (any authenticated OR anonymous) recorded
- Anonymous bucketing/id strategy recorded

description:
We pay GCS egress on every cache read while `.github/actions/node-setup` **already** caches `.nx/cache` through `actions/cache` — a free layer duplicating a paid one. On a public repo, GitHub Actions cache is free (10 GB/repo, LRU eviction).

**The security model survives for free.** GitHub Actions cache scoping already enforces exactly what the current setup achieves with `NX_POWERPACK_CACHE_MODE`: a PR branch can *read* caches from its base branch but cannot *write* into them, and branch caches are isolated from each other. That is the CREEP-safe (CVE-2025-36852) trusted-`main`-writes / PRs-read-only model, by construction, with no env override to maintain.

Work:
1. Strengthen the existing `actions/cache` step — the key is `hashFiles('nx.json','pnpm-lock.yaml')` with a loose `restore-keys` prefix, which is right for an Nx local cache. Verify `main` populates it and PRs restore from it.
2. Remove from `continuous-integration.yml`: the `🪣 NX Setup Cache` sed step, the `🌥️ Google Cloud Provider (GCP)` step, `NX_POWERPACK_CACHE_MODE`, `NX_GCS_BUCKET`, `GOOGLE_CREDENTIALS`, `GOOGLE_PROJECT_ID`. Same in `vercel-deploy.yml`.
3. Remove the `gcs` block from `nx.json` and drop `@nx/gcs-cache`. Confirm whether `NX_KEY` is still needed for anything else before removing it.
4. Keep the bucket for a couple of weeks, then delete it (90-day lifecycle otherwise pays storage for dead entries).

**Watch out:** `poisoned-gcs-nx-remote-cache` documents that gitignored `__generated__` output is invisible to Nx hashing. That hazard follows the cache, not the backend — it applies to the GitHub cache too, so keep the runbook and keep the codegen-before-affected ordering intact.

**Trade-off to state plainly:** 10 GB with LRU eviction is smaller than the 2.19 GB currently used but shared across all branches and workflows, so eviction pressure is higher; cross-branch hit rate may drop slightly. Measure hit rate before and after.
requirements: ["actions/cache verified populating on main and restoring on PRs", "All GCS/Powerpack cache wiring removed from both workflows and nx.json", "Nx cache hit rate before/after recorded", "Bucket scheduled for deletion after a soak period", "Poisoned-cache runbook retained and retargeted at the GitHub cache"]
title: Retire the paid GCS Nx remote cache in favour of the free GitHub Actions cache

description:
Not a pruning task — a quality signal the outcome data surfaced, worth its own plan.

From `skill_usage_outcomes`:

| skill | success | abandoned | abandon rate | avg duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ot-claude-loop | 43 | **4** | 8.5% | **2190s (36 min)** |
| github-squash | 46 | **3** | 6.1% | 147s |
| github-commit | 8 | 1 | 11% | 116s |
| skill-sync | 1 | **1** | **50%** | 35s |
| loop | 18 | 1 | 5.3% | 899s |
| ot-plan-loop | 18 | 0 | 0% | 1849s |

Abandoned rows carry no `duration_ms`, so the schema cannot currently say *how far in* a run died.

**Questions worth answering:**
1. The 4 abandoned `ot-claude-loop` runs — mid-task failure, worktree reaping (memory records session worktrees being deleted mid-run), or the human stopping it? A 36-minute average means an abandonment is expensive.
2. `skill-sync` at 1-of-2 abandoned on a 35-second skill is a small n but an ugly ratio — a fast skill dying half the time suggests it errors on a common path.
3. The 3 abandoned `github-squash` runs — is this the force-push confirmation gate being declined (a *healthy* abandon) or a real failure? If declining a confirmation records as `abandoned`, the metric is conflating user choice with breakage and needs a fourth outcome value.
4. Consider recording `duration_ms` on abandoned rows too, so partial progress is measurable.

**Do:** query the abandoned rows for `session_id`, correlate with the sessions, classify each, and fix whichever of the above turns out to be real.

**Done when:** every abandoned outcome is classified, and either the skill is fixed or the outcome vocabulary is corrected.

description:
Write down the decisions the rest of the plan implements. No config changes in this task.

**1. Which surface owns the queue.** `main` is protected TWICE today: classic branch protection (holds the only required check, `ci-success`) and ruleset id 14604876 (holds `required_linear_history`, `non_fast_forward`, `deletion`, and `pull_request` with `allowed_merge_methods: ["rebase"]`). Rulesets support a `merge_queue` rule; classic protection has its own "Require merge queue" toggle. Pick ONE and say why. Recommendation: put the `merge_queue` rule in the ruleset (it is already the richer, API-manageable surface) and, in a follow-up, move `required_status_checks: [ci-success]` there too so there is a single place to read — but do NOT move the required check in the same change as enabling the queue, so a stall has one candidate cause, not two.

**2. Queue merge method.** `MERGE` is ruled out by `required_linear_history`. Choose `SQUASH` or `REBASE` and state the consequence for commit shape. The repo's conventional-commit + `Plan-Id:`/`Task-Id:` footer convention (CLAUDE.md § Git and agent behavior) is the constraint: with `SQUASH`, repo settings `squash_merge_commit_title: PR_TITLE` + `squash_merge_commit_message: COMMIT_MESSAGES` decide what survives; with `REBASE`, every individual commit lands and each must already be conventional. Note the tension: the ruleset's `pull_request.allowed_merge_methods` is currently `["rebase"]` only, which constrains the non-queue path, and the queue's method is configured independently — say explicitly whether the two should agree.

**3. Tuning knobs**, with a number and a reason for each:
- `merge_method`
- `max_entries_to_build` (how many entries build speculatively in parallel)
- `min_entries_to_merge` / `max_entries_to_merge` (batch size)
- `min_entries_to_merge_wait_minutes`
- `check_response_timeout_minutes` — must exceed the CI worst case. The build job's own ceiling is `timeout-minutes: 30` per shard (`continuous-integration.yml:258`) and the measured fat-`main` worst case pre-sharding was 28m24s; the 3-way shard projects ~10.6 min. Set this with real headroom or the queue will dequeue healthy PRs.
- `grouping_strategy` (`ALLGREEN` vs `HEADGREEN`)

**4. Rollback.** The exact command/steps to turn the queue back off, and the symptom that should trigger it.

Deliverable: the decisions recorded on this plan (`append_plan_output`) or in `docs/monorepo/ci-cost.md` § merge queue — whichever the next task consumes. This task ends with a human confirming the merge-method choice; it changes commit history shape for every future merge and is not an agent's call.
summary: Human confirmed SQUASH. Queue lives on ruleset 14604876 (classic protection keeps ci-success). Knobs: SQUASH / max_build=5 / min_merge=1 / max_merge=5 / wait=5m / check_timeout=45m / ALLGREEN. Enable task must also add squash to allowed_merge_methods. SSOT: docs/monorepo/ci-cost.md § Merge queue.
title: Decide the queue's config surface, merge method, and tuning knobs (human gate)

description:
## Rule
From `packages/AGENTS.md` (Import and export rules): “No deep imports between workspace packages: consume via the main entry (`import { X } from '@openthrottle/foo'`) and re-export new symbols from the package's `index.ts`. Do not add subpath exports just to expose one symbol.”

## Violating files (with lines)
1. `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/settings/components/SettingsFeatureFlags.tsx:2` — `import * as FEATURE_FLAGS from '@openthrottle/react-router-utils/src/config/features'`
2. `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/settings/components/__tests__/SettingsFeatureFlags.test.tsx:4` — same deep path
3. NestJS generator templates (seed future violations; `@openthrottle/nestjs-core` is not a live workspace package):
   - `tools/generators/src/generators/nestjs/files/graphql-service/__name__/__name__.resolver.ts:5-8` (`…/src/entities/result.entity`, `…/src/policies/types`, `…/src/policies/policies.guard`, `…/src/policies/policies.decorator`)
   - `tools/generators/src/generators/nestjs/files/graphql-service/__name__/entities/__singular__.entity.ts:3` (`…/src/entities/base.entity`)
   - `tools/generators/src/generators/nestjs/files/graphql-service/__name__/dto/get-__name__.args.ts:3` (`…/src/dto/pagination.args`)
   - `tools/generators/src/generators/nestjs/files/graphql-service/__name__/__name__.service.ts:3` (`…/src/repositories/certs/roles.repository`)
   - `tools/generators/src/generators/nestjs/files/graphql-service/__name__/__name__.module.ts:4` and `…/simple-service/__name__/__name__.module.ts:3` (`…/src/repositories/certs/certs.module`)

## Mechanical fix
- SettingsFeatureFlags*: change to `import * as FEATURE_FLAGS from '@openthrottle/react-router-utils'` (already re-exported via `packages/react-router-utils/src/index.ts` → `./config/features`).
- NestJS templates: replace each `@openthrottle/nestjs-core/src/…` deep import with the current package’s **main entry** that actually exports that symbol (discover via `rg` / package `index.ts`; re-export from that package’s `index.ts` if missing). Do not add a one-off subpath export.

## Deliberate exceptions
None.

## Acceptance
- No `@openthrottle/*/src/` imports remain in the listed files.
- `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:test -- applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/settings/components/__tests__/SettingsFeatureFlags.test.tsx` green.
- `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:lint` green for touched files.
- Generator template paths no longer reference a non-existent `@openthrottle/nestjs-core` package.

description:
Two independent root package.json cleanups:

1. `tailwindcss` — **fix duplicate listing**, not a deletion. Appears under both `dependencies` (~line 227) and `devDependencies` (~line 347) in root `package.json`. The package itself is genuinely used (every React Router app's `vite.config.ts`/`styles.css` references it via root's hoisted copy — none of the apps declare it directly), so dedupe to a single section (`devDependencies`, since it's a build-time CSS tool) rather than removing it entirely.
2. `@swc/cli` — **delete**, pending one more check. `package.json:275:6` (devDependencies). Grep found no `npx swc`/CLI invocation anywhere in root `package.json` scripts, `tools/`, or `scripts/`. Sibling tools `@swc/core`, `@swc-node/register`, `swc-loader`, `unplugin-swc` are all confirmed in active use elsewhere (e.g. `tools/dotfiles/src/vitest-config.ts` imports `unplugin-swc`) — only the CLI binary itself looks dead. Before deleting, check for any Nx executor config that might shell out to `swc` directly.

Acceptance criteria: root `package.json` lists `tailwindcss` exactly once (devDependencies); `@swc/cli` removed if the executor-config check comes back clean; `pnpm install` updates the lockfile; `pnpm nx run monorepo:knip` no longer flags either; a representative RR app build (e.g. `openthrottle-developer:build`) stays green.

---

## RESOLUTION 2026-08-20 (/ot-claude-loop)

**Item 1 (tailwindcss) — done as specified.** Removed the `dependencies` copy, kept `devDependencies`. Confirmed safe for containers first: `Dockerfile.ReactRouter:135` runs a full `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and only prunes with `--prod deploy` at line 144, *after* the Nx build — so a build-time-only devDependency is available when the CSS is compiled. Verified with an **uncached** `openthrottle-developer:build --skip-nx-cache` (the cached run proved nothing, since it was a 12/12 cache hit).

**Item 2 (@swc/cli) — DO NOT DELETE. The verdict is refuted; the required executor check is what caught it.**

`@swc/cli` is load-bearing for `openthrottle-server`:

- `applications/openthrottle-server/nest-cli.json` sets `compilerOptions.builder.type: "swc"`.
- The server's `build`, `dev`, and `start` targets all shell out to `nest build` / `nest start`.
- `node_modules/@nestjs/cli/lib/compiler/swc/swc-compiler.js:137` does `require('@swc/cli/lib/swc/dir')`, and line 141 throws *"Failed to load \"@swc/cli\" and/or \"@swc/core\" required packages. Please, make sure to install them as development dependencies."*

So the CLI is consumed through the Nest CLI's swc compiler, not via a `swc` shell invocation — which is exactly why grepping for `npx swc` found nothing. Deleting it would have broken the server's build, dev and start. Confirmed the server still builds with an uncached `openthrottle-server:build --skip-nx-cache`.

`@swc/cli` left in root `devDependencies` unchanged. Not re-scoped into `openthrottle-server` either: `@nestjs/cli` resolves `@swc/cli` from its own location (hoisted root `node_modules`), so moving the declaration down is not obviously safe and was out of scope for a dedupe task. Recorded on the knip-config follow-up task instead.

**Bonus item — same duplicate-listing bug, found via task `66b2c5b2`.** Root `package.json` also declared `@faker-js/faker` twice (`dependencies` *and* `devDependencies`). Deduped to `devDependencies`, matching how its actual consumer declares it (`packages/nestjs-repositories/package.json` lists faker under `devDependencies`, used by its 16 `*.factory.ts` fishery factories).

Noted for a future sweep, not fixed here: those `*.factory.ts` files are exported from `nestjs-repositories/src/index.ts` while faker is only a devDependency there — dev-dep-used-by-exported-code is a latent packaging smell, but it is the existing deliberate arrangement and outside this task.
summary: tailwindcss is accidentally declared in both dependencies and devDependencies at root (should be one), and @swc/cli has no found invocation anywhere despite sibling swc tooling (@swc/core, @swc-node/register, swc-loader, unplugin-swc) being actively used.
title: root package.json: dedupe tailwindcss listing + resolve unused @swc/cli

description:
In `scheduled-agent-jobs.processor.ts`:

- Swap the `@Processor` `concurrency: SCHEDULED_AGENT_JOBS_CONCURRENCY` for `resolveScheduledAgentJobsConcurrency()`.
- After `resolveRunTarget` (which already runs before the run row is claimed, so the key is available early) compute the concurrency key from the resolved cwd plus the run's `settings.worktree` and the driver's worktree capability.
- Acquire the lock inside the existing `try`, before `assertUsableCwd`/`runner.run`, and release it in a `finally` nested so it is freed before the outer bookkeeping. The acquisition wait is bounded by the run's own resolved timeout; exceeding it fails the run in-band with a message naming the directory rather than hanging a worker slot forever.
- Log at info when a run waits on a directory, so contention is visible in the run log rather than looking like a slow agent.
- Register the service in `scheduled-agent-jobs-queue.module.ts` and add `NestjsRedisModule` to its imports.

Extend `scheduled-agent-jobs.processor.test.ts`: a run acquires and releases for its resolved cwd; a flag-only worktree run acquires nothing; the lock is released even when `runner.run` throws; an acquisition timeout marks the run failed with a directory-naming message.
requirements: ["Worker concurrency comes from resolveScheduledAgentJobsConcurrency()", "The lock is keyed on the resolved cwd and acquired before the agent CLI spawns", "The lock is released on every exit path including runner.run throwing", "An acquisition timeout fails the run in-band with a message naming the directory", "Processor tests cover acquire/release, the no-lock worktree path, release-on-throw, and timeout"]
summary: Wire ScheduledAgentJobDirectoryLockService into ScheduledAgentJobsProcessor around runner.run, keyed on the resolved cwd, and switch the @Processor concurrency to resolveScheduledAgentJobsConcurrency().
title: Gate the processor run on the directory lock and raise worker concurrency

description:
Traps 3 and 4. With a queue on, `gh pr merge` enqueues instead of merging, and the SHA that lands on `main` is not the SHA that was pushed. Anything automated that assumes otherwise is now wrong.

Audit and update:

1. **Work-ledger recording.** The OT convention is `attach_session_subject` then `record_artifact` (type `git_commit`, payload `{repo, sha}`) for the MERGED squash commit. Any flow capturing that SHA from the local branch or the PR head now records a commit that does not exist on `main`. Fix it to resolve the SHA from `main` after the merge actually lands (e.g. the PR's `mergeCommitSha` via `gh pr view --json mergeCommitSha`, polled until non-null).
2. **`skills/github-pull-request`** and any `/github/*` command that merges or waits on merge: make enqueue-vs-merged an explicit distinction in the output, so an agent does not report "merged" when it means "queued".
3. **Ralph / `/loop` / workflow-ralph task loops** that commit → PR → merge → next task: a queued PR can sit for minutes and can be REJECTED from the queue. Decide whether these loops wait for the merge, or enqueue and move on and reconcile the ledger later. Either is defensible; leaving it unstated is not.
4. **`monitor-ci` skill** — note that it depends on Nx Cloud and is already inoperable here (`docs/monorepo/NX.md`); do not build queue monitoring on top of it.

Search broadly (`gh pr merge`, `mergeCommitSha`, `--auto`, `link_commit`, `record_artifact`) rather than trusting this list to be complete. Validate with `pnpm run check:local` and, for any changed skill, `/skill-sync` per the repo's skill architecture.
title: Fix the agent workflows that assume merges are instant and SHAs are stable

description:
Split out of task 1137b619 (Phase C) during the /grilling gate, and moved AHEAD of Phase B.

Rationale: task 1137b619 itself says the baseline "cannot be reconstructed afterwards" — it must be captured at or near the base commit, before tasks 00b5a4ad / c2335c92 move anything. It is also the input that decides whether Phase B is worth doing at all, so running it last inverted the dependency.

## Measure

1. Record the pre-split baseline from a full-affected CI run at the base commit: heaviest-shard wall-clock, **broken down per target — `lint` vs `typecheck` vs `test`**. The breakdown is the point, not the total.
2. Record what a config-only **Vitest `--shard`** split inside the single `openthrottle-developer` project would buy for the `test` slice. No code movement; `--shard` can cut `test` at arbitrary granularity.
3. Isolate the delta only Phase B can deliver: `lint` + `typecheck` are whole-project and `--shard` cannot touch them. That slice IS Phase B's unique value.
4. Feed in task d4d987ab's partitioner verdict — if `developer-routing` would co-locate with `openthrottle-developer`, the projected Phase B win is zero regardless of the above.

## Decide

Present to the owner: baseline breakdown, `--shard` projection, Phase-B-only delta, partitioner verdict. **No pre-committed threshold** — owner calls go/no-go with the numbers (decided during grilling).

Done when: all four numbers are in plan output and the owner has been given the go/no-go call. Tasks 00b5a4ad and c2335c92 stay PENDING until that call is GO.

description:
Design-first gate. Produce a short design decision (record in this plan's output / a design note in OT, not a Markdown file) before any code changes.

Measure the as-is cost:
- Cold vs warm latency for `discoverLocalModels` and `discoverAgentClis` (time a cache-miss scan vs a cache hit). Cold agent-CLI = up to 5 `--version` + 3 `<cli> models` child spawns at 3s/5s timeouts; cold local = ~48 HTTP probes.
- Confirm the home-load amplification: one load of `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/_index.tsx` should currently trigger `discoverLocalModels` x2 and `discoverAgentClis` x2 (via `loadDriverEndpointModels` in `models.server.ts` re-issuing both queries) plus the header chat's `/resources/chat-options` fetch.

Decide and record:
- Which levers ship in this plan (in-flight coalescing, stale-while-revalidate/background refresh, home-loader dedupe, client-side caching, optional Redis) and in what order.
- Target: repeat loads within the TTL should never pay a cold scan; first-load-after-expiry should serve stale + refresh in background rather than block.
- Whether TTL stays 60s or lengthens once SWR is in place; whether Redis is in scope now or deferred.

Output: a concrete decision the remaining tasks implement. No source changes in this task.
summary: Baseline the current repeat-load latency and decide which levers to ship before writing code.
title: Design: measure repeat-load cost + lock the caching levers

description:
UI half — make the disabled state reachable and self-explanatory, so a user never types an edit that the server will reject.

`useSkillDetail` (`app/routing/skills/hooks/useSkillDetail.tsx`) already computes `isOpenThrottle` from `entry.source`. Take the loader's `editable` as an input and return two derived values:
- `canEdit = editable && isOpenThrottle`
- `editDisabledTooltip` — `SKILL_DETAIL_COPY.editDisabledTooltip` when the blocker is the missing checkout, and a new `SKILL_DETAIL_COPY.editExternalTooltip` when the blocker is provenance. Provenance wins when both apply (it is the more specific reason).

New copy in `data.copy.ts` `SKILL_DETAIL_COPY`:
`editExternalTooltip: \`This skill is installed from an external source. Editing it here would fork it from upstream — change it upstream and re-sync.\``

`SkillDetailEditControls.tsx`: keep the `editable` prop as the single "can the user edit" boolean (now fed `canEdit`) and add a required `disabledTooltip: string` prop replacing the hard-coded `SKILL_DETAIL_COPY.editDisabledTooltip` in the tooltip content. Thread `canEdit` / `editDisabledTooltip` through `SkillDetailTabs.tsx` → `SkillIntroduction.tsx` in place of the raw `editable`. Also harden `handleEdit` in the hook to no-op when `canEdit` is false, so edit mode cannot be entered even if a caller passes the wrong prop.

Tests (`components/__tests__/SkillDetailEditControls.test.tsx`, `SkillIntroduction.test.tsx`, `SkillDetailTabs.test.tsx`): an `external` entry renders `skill-edit-disabled` with the external tooltip and no `skill-edit-button`; an `openthrottle` entry with `editable` renders the enabled Edit button; a no-checkout `openthrottle` entry keeps today's checkout tooltip. Add a hook test that `handleEdit` leaves `isEditing` false for an external entry.

Do not touch the tag chips, orphan removal, run control, or availability controls — those stay live for external skills.

Validate: `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:test -- app/routing/skills`, then `:typecheck` and `:lint`.

description:
BLOCKING HUMAN GATE — this task blocks the install/update tasks (2, 3, 4, 6) and needs owner sign-off before any install code runs on the server host. It does NOT block task 5 (the read-only status view, which uses only the existing SETTINGS_READ discoverAgentClis query).

Decide and write down (as this task's requirements/summary, not a docs/ file):

1. **Install descriptor shape** on the driver registry. Propose adding optional `install` (and `update`) to `AgentDriver` in packages/openthrottle-drivers/src/types/index.ts, e.g. `install?: { method: 'curl-shell'; url: string; installerShell: 'bash' | 'sh' }` and `update?: { method: 'curl-shell' } | { method: 'command'; argv: readonly string[] }`. Keep the package a dep-free leaf.
2. **Per-CLI install + update commands.** Install URLs are known from scripts/setup_software.sh: claude=https://claude.ai/install.sh (bash), cursor-agent=https://cursor.com/install (bash), codex=https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh (sh), grok=https://x.ai/cli/install.sh (bash), opencode=https://opencode.ai/install (bash). RESEARCH each CLI's real self-update path (is it `claude update`? re-run installer? `npm i -g`?) and record the decision per CLI. Where no distinct update exists, update == re-run installer.
3. **Permission model.** New WRITE permission (reuse SETTINGS_WRITE or add a dedicated `AGENT_SETUP_MANAGE` in nestjs-rbac) — NOT SETTINGS_READ. Decide which.
4. **Env/feature flag** to enable server-side install, DEFAULT-OFF (hosted/multi-tenant must not allow curl|bash on the box). Name it (e.g. `AGENT_SETUP_INSTALL_ENABLED`) and decide where it's read + how the UI reflects disabled state.
5. **Execution/streaming model.** Sync mutation returns a runId + graphql-ws subscription for streamed stdout/stderr (mirror resources.conversation-stream.tsx), vs a BullMQ job. Pick one; note timeout/abort + the PATH gotcha (installer target dir must be on the server process PATH or post-install discovery won't see the binary) + discovery-cache invalidation on success.

Deliverable: a short decision record captured on this task so the downstream tasks have unambiguous inputs.
requirements: ["Owner sign-off on running installers on the server host (security surface)", "Install descriptor shape approved", "Per-CLI update mechanism researched and recorded", "Permission + env-flag names decided", "Execution/streaming model chosen"]
summary:
DECISION RECORD (task-1 gate).

1) Install descriptor shape on AgentDriver (packages/openthrottle-drivers/src/types/index.ts, keep leaf dep-free):
   install?: { method: 'curl-shell'; url: string; installerShell: 'bash' | 'sh' }
   update?:  { method: 'curl-shell' } | { method: 'command'; argv: readonly string[] }   // argv = args AFTER the binary; command runs `<binary> <argv...>`

2) Per-CLI install URL/shell (from setup_software.sh) + researched update:
   claude   install https://claude.ai/install.sh (bash)      update: command ['update']   (`claude update`, native updater)
   cursor   install https://cursor.com/install (bash)         update: curl-shell (re-run installer; auto-updates by default, `cursor-agent update` ambiguous — re-run is robust & idempotent)
   codex    install https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh (sh) update: command ['update']   (`codex update`, confirmed 2026)
   grok     install https://x.ai/cli/install.sh (bash)        update: command ['update']   (`grok update`)
   opencode install https://opencode.ai/install (bash)        update: command ['upgrade']  (`opencode upgrade`)

3) Permission: REUSE existing SETTINGS_WRITE ('settings:write') from @openthrottle/nestjs-rbac — it already exists and is DB-seeded (migration 034); ADMIN has it. No new permission / no new seed migration. (Read-only status view keeps SETTINGS_READ.) Note drift: migration 034 grants settings:write only to admin, not the `user` role — acceptable, install is admin+env-gated.

4) Env flag: OT_AGENT_CLI_INSTALL_ENABLED, DEFAULT-OFF. Read via ConfigService.get<string>()?.trim().toLowerCase(), enabled only for 'true'|'1'|'yes' (mirror readAgentsChatMutationsEnabledFromConfig). When disabled the mutation resolves a typed { ok:false, disabled:true } result and NEVER spawns. UI shows controls disabled + reason. Read-only view ignores the flag.

5) Execution/streaming: sync mutation returns a runId, live stdout/stderr via graphql-ws @Subscription mirroring conversation-stream (pubSub topic agent-setup:<runId>:stream, chunk @ObjectType, buffered replay). NOT BullMQ. Bounded timeout (~10min) + AbortSignal; v1 may skip a cancel mutation. PATH gotcha: executor must augment child env PATH with common install target dirs (~/.local/bin, ~/.bun/bin, ~/.opencode/bin, ~/.cursor/bin, etc.) so post-install discovery sees the new binary. On success call AgentDiscoveryService cache.invalidate() so next discoverAgentClis re-scans.

Placement: descriptors in openthrottle-drivers (task 2, pure data); executor as new file in agentic-utils conversation-backend with an injectable spawn seam (task 3); server mutations+subscription in a NEW sibling `agent-setup` GraphQL module, leaving agent-discovery read-only (task 4).

GATE STATUS: security sign-off (running registry-locked curl|bash on the server host) pending owner approval; blocks tasks 2/3/4/6, not task 5.
title: 🚧 GATE — Design & decisions: security gating, install descriptor shape, per-CLI install/update commands, execution model

description:
Design gate. Pick between the three sketches in the plan description — consumer-side lint, producer-side lint on client-safe packages, or a build-time check — informed by task 1's matrix.

The decision must answer:

- **Transitivity.** The bug was `isRecord` -> barrel -> `node:os`. A rule that only catches direct imports would not have caught it. Say plainly whether the chosen mechanism is transitive, and if not, why that is still worth shipping.
- **How client-safe is determined.** A hand-maintained list will rot. Check whether Nx tags (`type:`, `technology:`) or `package.json` fields already distinguish client-consumable packages from server-side ones, and prefer deriving from those.
- **False positives.** `openthrottle-agentic-utils` (38 files), `openthrottle-ide` (20) and `openthrottle-skills` (8) legitimately use node builtins and must not be flagged. A rule that fires on them is wrong, not a finding.
- **Test files.** `*.server.test.ts` imports node-heavy packages and runs under Node, so it must not trip the rule.

Record the decision on the plan before implementing.
requirements: ["A written decision with reasoning, recorded on the plan", "Explicit answer on transitivity", "Explicit answer on how client-safe packages are identified, preferring existing metadata over a new list"]
title: Decide the mechanism
