description:
Scaffold first — do not hand-write the file:

```
NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:react-router --subGenerator=component --application=openthrottle-developer --folder=app/routing/settings/components --name=WorkspaceEditorCard
```

(`--folder` takes the full path — see the appearance-regroup gotcha.)

Props (alphabetized, explicit types, `import type` for type-only):

- `affiliateUrl?: string | null`
- `editor: WorkspaceEditorId`
- `enabled: boolean`
- `onToggle: (editor: WorkspaceEditorId, next: boolean) => void`
- `presence?: EditorPresenceState | null` — `null`/absent and `UNKNOWN` both render **no badge at all**

Composition, using `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn`:

- `Card` as the shell. Enabled state reads as selected: `ring-1 ring-primary` / `border-primary` plus a subtle `bg-accent/40`, not just a checked switch. Unenabled cards stay quiet, never disabled-looking.
- Header row: `icon` from the editor config + `label`, with the presence `Badge` right-aligned. Detected → a positive-but-calm variant; not detected → `variant="outline"`/muted. Check `Badge.tsx` for the variants that actually exist before inventing one; if a suitable variant is missing, use an existing one rather than adding to the shared package in this task.
- Body: the one-line `description` from the config, `text-muted-foreground text-sm`.
- Footer: the `Switch` (accessible name from copy, `data-testid={`WorkspaceEditorCard-switch-${editor}`}`) and, when `affiliateUrl` is non-null, the `Get {label}` link — keep the existing `rel="noopener noreferrer sponsored"`, `target="_blank"`, and the aria-label that discloses it is an affiliate link opening in a new tab.
- Wrap the not-detected badge in a `Tooltip` carrying `presenceNotDetectedTooltip` so the reassurance survives the move from prose to badge.

Hard requirements:

- **Never** disable the switch, the card, or anything else because `presence` is `NOT_FOUND`. Detection is advisory, full stop.
- Card must be keyboard-operable: the switch is the control; if the whole card is clickable, it must not create a second tab stop or a nested-interactive a11y violation (a `label` wrapping the switch is the safe pattern — the affiliate anchor must stay outside it so clicking the link never toggles the switch).
- `data-testid="WorkspaceEditorCard"` on the root plus `data-editor={editor}` and `data-presence` so tests can target a specific card.
- Keep the generated section comments (`// Hooks`, `// Setup`, `// Handlers`, `// Markup`, `// Life Cycle`, `// 🔌 Short Circuit`) even where empty.
- Presentational only — no fetcher, no form state, no `useState` for enablement. The parent owns selection.

Done when: the component typechecks and lints in isolation, and its own test file (next task) can render it standalone.
summary: One card per editor carrying label, description, presence badge, enable switch, and inline affiliate link.
title: Generate and build the WorkspaceEditorCard component

description:
Primary fix. Stop awaiting createCursorAgentSession inside startConversationStream so the mutation returns the assistant id immediately (as claude/codex/grok/opencode do).

Approach options (pick during impl, keep server contract intact):
- Lazily mint the cursor session inside the fire-and-forget runStream (conversation-stream.service.ts, before first cursor spawn) rather than in resolveCliSession, persisting the id to conversation.metadata once obtained. Mirror how opencode records its surfaced session id mid-stream.
- OR return from the mutation immediately and perform the create-chat as the first step of the stream, emitting a 'starting' chunk so the client has activity.

Constraints: preserve --resume <sessionId> requirement in argv; keep persistence + reuse behavior (later turns still skip the mint); private mode (persist=false) still runs a fresh session; surface create-chat failures as a stream error the client can display/retry, not a silent hang.

description:
## Problem

On the plan detail route ([`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/plans.$planId._index.tsx`](applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/plans.$planId._index.tsx)), clicking a tab (`overview` / `tasks` / `output` / `configuration`) shifts the page scroll position. The tabs are URL-linked, so navigation is expected to preserve scroll — it does not.

## Root cause is NOT the obvious one

These tabs are **not** React Router `<Link>`/`<NavLink>` elements — they are Radix/shadcn `TabsTrigger` buttons whose selection is synced to a search param. The `setSearchParams` call **already** passes `{ preventScrollReset: true }`, so the router-scroll-reset is already suppressed:

- Tabs component: [`PlanDetailRoute.tsx:113-158`](applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/plans/components/PlanDetailRoute.tsx) → `OpenThrottleTabs` (`packages/react-router-ui/src/components/OpenThrottleTabs.tsx`) → `OpenThrottleTabsWithUrlSync.tsx`.
- Navigation call: [`packages/react-router-ui/src/hooks/useUrlSyncedTabValue.ts:56`](packages/react-router-ui/src/hooks/useUrlSyncedTabValue.ts) — `setSearchParams(nextParams, { preventScrollReset: true })`.

So adding `preventScrollReset` is a no-op — it's there. The remaining scroll shift comes from something else. Likely candidates to verify:

1. **Radix focus-on-select**: when a tab is activated, Radix moves focus to the selected `TabsTrigger` (or the panel), and the browser scrolls that element into view. Check whether `focus({ preventScroll: true })` or `scroll-margin`/focus handling is needed.
2. **Layout/height change between panels**: the four panels have different heights; switching to a shorter panel can shrink the document and reflow scroll. Confirm by measuring `document.scrollingElement.scrollTop` before/after a tab click across panels of differing heights.

## Desired behavior

Clicking any plan-detail tab updates the active panel (and the URL param) **without** changing the window scroll position — the toolbar/tab strip stays exactly where it was.

## Scope note

The tab wiring is shared (`OpenThrottleTabsWithUrlSync` / `useUrlSyncedTabValue` in `@openthrottle/react-router-ui`), so a fix here benefits every URL-synced tab surface. Prefer a fix in the shared hook/component over a route-local patch, and keep the existing `preventScrollReset: true`.

## Verification

- Reproduce on `plans.$planId._index.tsx` with the window scrolled partway down, then click across all four tabs; scroll offset must not change.
- Diagnose which of the two causes applies (add a temporary `scrollTop` log or inspect focus target) before committing a fix, so the change targets the actual mechanism.
- Update/extend the `useUrlSyncedTabValue` / `OpenThrottleTabs` tests if the fix changes their behavior.
summary: On applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/plans.$planId._index.tsx the URL-synced tabs jump the scroll position when a tab is clicked. Note: the setSearchParams call already passes { preventScrollReset: true } (useUrlSyncedTabValue.ts:56), so the router is NOT the cause — investigate the real culprit (Radix focus-scroll on the newly-shown TabsTrigger/panel, or layout/height change between panels) and stop the jump.
title: Plan-detail tabs: stop scroll position shifting on tab change

description:
Add pagination to `app/routes/skills._index.tsx` wired to the skills `DataTable`. Client-side (list is disk-backed and fully in memory) but URL-driven, matching the sibling-route convention.

## Do
- Parse `page` and `limit` from `searchParams` (sane defaults, e.g. page 1 / limit 25/50; mirror parsing in `plans._index.tsx`). Clamp to valid bounds.
- Apply pagination AFTER the existing `filterSkillsBySource` step: compute `offset = (page - 1) * limit`, slice the filtered array, pass the page slice to `SkillsTable`.
- Render `OpenThrottlePagination` (from `@openthrottle/react-router-ui`) below the table with `page`, `limit`, `totalCount = filteredEntries.length`, and a suitable `resultLabel` (e.g. "skills").
- When the source filter changes, reset to page 1 (drop/clear the `page` param) so the user isn't stranded on an out-of-range page.
- Keep `DataTable` unchanged — do NOT add `getPaginationRowModel`. The external pager drives the slice.

## Gotchas
- `DataTable` (react-router-shadcn) has no built-in pagination props; it renders whatever `data` it's given, so slicing upstream is the mechanism.
- Preserve other query params (e.g. the tab/source filter) when navigating pages — `OpenThrottlePagination` preserves the query string; confirm the filter state survives page nav.

## Verify
- Vitest: render the route/component with > `limit` entries, assert only one page renders, pager shows correct count, navigating changes the slice, and changing the filter resets to page 1.
- `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:{lint,typecheck,test}`; visually confirm via dev server.
title: Add URL-driven pagination to the /skills index Table

description:
## Finding
Website landing first-load JS is dominated by a single shared chunk that contains `GlobalAnimationMesh` / `GlobalAnimationWaves` (WebGL/canvas shaders).

## Paths
- `applications/openthrottle-website/app/routes/_index.tsx`
- `applications/openthrottle-website/app/routing/home/demo/LandingHero.tsx` (imports `GlobalAnimationMesh`)
- `applications/openthrottle-website/app/routing/home/demo/LandingFlow.tsx` (`GlobalAnimationWaves`)
- `packages/react-router-ui-global/src/components/GlobalAnimationMesh.tsx`
- `packages/react-router-ui-global/src/components/GlobalAnimationWaves.tsx`
- Built asset: `applications/openthrottle-website/build/client/assets/settings-*.js` (Rolldown name; not a settings route)

## Measured before
After `pnpm nx run openthrottle-website:build`:
- `settings-*.js` = **1229.7 KB raw / 356.9 KB gzip-9**
- Estimated landing JS (entry+jsx+root+runtime+rollbar+settings+_index) = **1815.2 KB raw**
- `_index-*.js` itself is only 12.6 KB; the animation chunk is referenced from `_index`, `root`, and `download`

Re-measure:
```bash
pnpm nx run openthrottle-website:build
python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import gzip
w=Path('applications/openthrottle-website/build/client/assets')
p=next(w.glob('settings-*.js'))
print(p.name, p.stat().st_size, len(gzip.compress(p.read_bytes(),9)))
PY
```

## Suspected cause / intro
This week's landing work: `4454472a` (promote GlobalAnimationMesh/Waves), `89c6bb4a` (snap-scroll landing), `d2be5590` (rebuild landing). Eager import of animation components (and likely the `@openthrottle/react-router-ui-global` barrel) into the landing graph.

## Proposed fix
Dynamic-import / `React.lazy` the mesh+waves so the hero paints without the shader stack; keep a CSS/static fallback for reduced-motion and first paint. Avoid pulling `GradientMesh` / `@paper-design/shaders-react` into the critical path via barrel re-exports.

## Expected after
- Landing critical JS (everything needed for first paint excluding deferred animation) **≤ 500 KB raw** (ideally ≤ 150 KB gzip for the deferred animation chunk alone)
- `settings-*.js` either gone from the `_index` import graph or loaded only after idle/`requestIdleCallback`

## Acceptance
Re-run the measure command above on a production build: landing estimated JS **< 900 KB raw**, and the animation chunk is **not** in the initial module graph of `_index` (no static import edge).
title: 1. Website landing: defer GlobalAnimationMesh/Waves (1229.7 KB chunk)

description:
**No production code in this task.** It exists because getting the boundary wrong makes the whole plan a net negative — a hand-written vocabulary sitting next to a generated enum is a fifth copy of the same list.

Answer, in writing, on the plan output stream:

1. **Who owns a GraphQL-backed union?** Today: `WORKSPACE_EDITOR_IDS` (nestjs-repositories) → server enum → `schema.gql` → generated `WorkspaceEditorId` (developer app). Four representations already. The package must NOT add a fifth. Proposal to validate: `vocabularyFromEnum(GeneratedEnum)` wraps the generated enum on the client; `vocabulary([...])` is the source only for unions with no GraphQL representation. Confirm `vocabularyFromEnum` can recover a literal union type from a codegen'd TS enum — codegen emits `enum WorkspaceEditorId { Claude = 'CLAUDE', … }`, so check whether `Record<WorkspaceEditorId, T>` keys off the member names or the values, and which one consumers actually index by. Write a throwaway .ts file and read the inferred types; do not assume.

2. **What is the minimum helper set?** Candidates: `vocabulary()`, `.is()`, `.labelled()`, `.subsetOf()`, `.map()`. Justify each with a real call site from the migration targets. Drop anything without one — an unused helper is another thing to keep in sync.

3. **Does `subsetOf` return a Set, an array, or a predicate?** Call sites differ: `PROMPT_ROLES` does `.has()`, `TERMINAL_TASK_STATUSES` is used in a comparison. Pick one return shape that serves both.

4. **Where does the package live and what may it import?** `packages/nodejs-parts-department` (`@openthrottle/nodejs-parts-department`), source-first (no `build` target; `main`/`types` → `./src/index.ts`) so React Router apps transpile it via Vite. Verify against `packages/AGENTS.md` and the `__build` placeholder discriminator. It must be dependency-free: `openthrottle-server`, `openthrottle-drivers`, the developer app, and `@tools/generators` all need it, and a package consumed by the server needs top-level exports (see the server-consumed-packages note in MONOREPO.md).

Deliverable: a decision record in the plan output covering all four, plus a one-file API sketch. Do not start task 2 until this is settled.
summary: Decision record on the plan output stream. Verified by tsc probes: generated enum values are UPPERCASE (server ids are lowercase — two distinct string sets bridged by GraphQL); Record<Enum,T> keys off the nominal enum type, so consumers must index with WorkspaceEditorId.Claude; vocabularyFromEnum recovers the union cast-free by constraining Record<string,TMember> rather than Record<string,string>. Helper set trimmed to vocabulary/vocabularyFromEnum/.values/.is/.labelled/.subsetOf — .has and .map dropped for lack of a call site. subsetOf returns ReadonlySet<TMember>, parameter Record<TMember,boolean>. Package follows the nodejs-utils source-first precedent (__build placeholders, publishConfig.exports, zero deps).
title: Design spike: settle the codegen boundary and the helper API

description:

Behavior:
1. Resolve the Postgres connection the same way the server does (`getPostgresUrl()` from `@openthrottle/openthrottle-agentic-utils`, matching `scripts/openthrottle-database-migrations.ts`). See Task 'env/DB parity' for making this resolve the server's DB, not a divergent root one.
2. Retry-connect loop with bounded backoff — poll for readiness for a short window (default ~5s, a handful of attempts) to cover the race where `pnpm run database:start` was just issued and the container isn't accepting connections yet.
3. On successful connect: import and call the EXISTING exported `runMigrations(store, source)` + `PgMigrationStore` from `scripts/openthrottle-database-migrations.ts` (do NOT reimplement migration logic). Use the same fs-backed `MigrationSource` (readdir/readFile over `databases/migrations`).
4. On timeout / unreachable after the window: print a clear, actionable message ('Postgres is not reachable — start it with: pnpm run database:start') and `process.exit(1)`.

Structure for testability: extract the wait/backoff logic into a pure, injectable function (inject a `connect` attempt fn + a `sleep`/clock fn + attempt budget) so the retry policy can be unit-tested without pg or real timers — mirror the ports style already used in the runner. Keep the `main()`/direct-invoke guard pattern used by the runner so it is importable by tests without executing.

Match existing code style: `import type` for types, explicit return types, no `as`/`any`, async/await. Refactor the runner's shared bits into small exports rather than duplicating if that reads cleaner (the runner already exports `runMigrations`, `PgMigrationStore`, `MigrationStore`, `MigrationSource`, `LEDGER_TABLE`).

description:

Model it on `scripts/audit-component-shape.ts` — read it first. It already runs in the pre-commit hook, scans with ts-morph, prints a per-rule/per-project violation table, and supports `--strict`. Match that output shape; the console format is what makes it usable.

**What to report:**
1. Duplicate exported symbol names across files that look like vocabulary guards (`is<Name>`, `<NAME>_VALUES`, `<NAME>_IDS`) — the exact shape of the original bug.
2. Array/Set literals enumerating ≥2 members of a known vocabulary outside its SSOT (belt-and-braces with the lint rule, which may be suppressed).
3. `Partial<Record<…>>` over a known vocabulary — flags the `DriverRegistry` class of gap.
4. **The backlog:** every union in the repo not yet on the package, so the fan-out beyond the three pilots is a list rather than another audit.

Start in **warn mode**, mirroring the test-coverage guard-rail precedent (OT 2e227f88). Report item 4 as informational from day one — it is the deliverable that makes the rest of the migration schedulable.

summary: Audit script modelled on audit-component-shape.ts (same flags, same table format), scanning 2884 files. V1 found 3 duplicate guards — including isRolloutFlagKind, structurally identical to the isWorkspaceEditorId bug this plan exists to fix, in the same file the ESLint rule flagged for the array half. V2 30 sites, informational (value-based matching without a type checker; smallest-superset wins). V3 4 sites — including the named DriverId/DriverRegistry case, which my first version MISSED because it matched the Partial key against union consts rather than the type alias; now collects union-derived type aliases and enum names. V4 backlog needed two discriminators to be usable (308→153): identifier-like members, and enum-map-only objects so label maps aren't reported as needing migration — a label map is already a derivation. Wired as monorepo:audit-vocabularies (nx.json targetDefaults + the required {} placeholder on the root project) plus audit:vocabularies[:strict] and check:local:vocabularies; check:local exits 0. Excluded from the strict sweep exactly as test-coverage is. description:
## Finding
`/calendar` route module alone is **310.1 KB** (gzip **82.0 KB**), the heaviest per-route chunk in the developer app. Fingerprints: `rrule` + `Temporal` from `@openthrottle/react-router-scheduling`.

## Paths
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/calendar._index.tsx` (+ related calendar routes)
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/calendar/**`
- `packages/react-router-scheduling` (rrule helpers)
- Built: `calendar._index-*.js` = 310.1 KB

## Measured before
```bash
pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:build
# calendar._index-*.js = 310.1 KB raw / 82.0 KB gzip
# With base shell: ≈ 2563 KB total JS for that navigation
```

## Suspected cause
Full recurrence/Temporal stack eagerly bundled into the calendar index route rather than lazy-loaded for create/edit flows that need rrule.

## Proposed fix
Code-split recurrence expansion / rrule to the event create/edit paths; keep the month grid lean. Audit whether Temporal polyfill is required for target browsers.

## Expected after
`calendar._index-*.js` **≤ 100 KB raw** (≤ ~30 KB gzip).

## Acceptance
Production build re-measure of `calendar._index-*.js` ≤ 100 KB raw.
summary:
CLOSED with the ≤100 KB acceptance re-baselined — the target was disproved by measurement, not left undone.

SHIPPED (on main, in PR #422 / 696a4740, which lists this Task-Id in its footers): a precise sideEffects list on packages/react-router-scheduling/package.json — ["**/*.css", "**/datetime.ts", "**/temporal-bootstrap.ts"]. This package was deliberately excluded from the blanket `sideEffects: false` sweep because it installs the Temporal global polyfill and imports CSS; enumerating its real side effects instead lets the rest of the barrel tree-shake and stops scheduling internals leaking into unrelated routes. Verified present on main 2026-08-23.

WHY THE ACCEPTANCE IS VOID — two independent reasons:
1. The rrule premise is false. `rrule` is not installed anywhere in the workspace (no node_modules/.pnpm/rrule@* entry, confirmed 2026-08-23). The 43 lowercase `rrule` hits are a property name on schedule-x event objects. recurrence.ts:7 states buildRRule is hand-rolled "rather than pulling the full `rrule` library". There is no recurrence library to split out.
2. Ablation decomposed the 310.1 KB as 55.7 KB Temporal polyfill + 254.4 KB schedule-x engine + preact + calendar UI. Deleting Temporal outright still leaves 254.4 KB, so ≤100 KB is unreachable. All seven schedule-x plugins are statically imported and selected by runtime flags with DEFAULT_PLUGINS enabling all of them, so the bundler cannot shake them.

STILL OPEN, CARRIED FORWARD — successor plan 2d8b7293-742b-4395-bb54-80f24229685d, task 31e85909-1858-4d55-84d8-a5404cdf249e: whether to load the Temporal polyfill conditionally on `globalThis.Temporal === undefined` for 55.7 KB on Temporal-native browsers, which needs an async gate since schedule-x v4 reads the global directly. Explicitly rejected already: React.lazy on the calendar (defers rather than removes, and the calendar IS the page content) and splitting the optional plugins (breaking API change, no win on this route).

Closed by reconciliation plan e1b32fde.
title: 5. Calendar route: cut 310.1 KB chunk (rrule/Temporal)

description:
Implement the shape decided in the design task, inside `packages/openthrottle-showroom`, standing alone so the migration and the consumer rewiring stay reviewable separately.

## Ship

- The type definitions (`VideoEpisode`, `Variant`, `Beat`, the `as const` value sets for format/status/recording/playlist).
- A **registry**: `episodes` keyed by id, plus `getEpisode(id)` and `getVariant(episodeId, variantId?)` where an omitted variant id resolves `selectedVariant`. Unknown ids throw with the list of known ids — this replaces four different "missing front matter" error paths.
- **Derived helpers**, each a pure function over beats: `spokenWords`, `estimatedSpokenSeconds` (145 wpm, the constant currently living in `scripts/validate-video-scripts.ts`), `budgetWords(format)` derived from `docs/marketing/format.json` exactly as today, and `sentences(variant)` producing the `NarrationSentence[]` shape `narrate/parse-script.ts` returns — same naive sentence split, same lexicon application, so the TTS path is a drop-in later.

Everything reachable from the package's single entry point per the no-deep-imports rule. Public API exports need a JSDoc `@public` tag so Knip keeps them.

## Tests

Vitest, colocated per repo convention. Cover: word counting matches what `validate-video-scripts.ts` produces for a known script (the migration must not silently change counts), sentence splitting matches `parse-script.ts` on the same input, budget derivation matches the current 132-word short budget, unknown id/variant errors, and description composition against a fixture.

description:
The largest multiplier on every other number in this plan. 100 workflow runs in an 8-hour overnight window; ~78 CI runs/day. The cause is structural, not accidental: `agents-ralph` and the OT plan loop commit **after each task** with `Plan-Id:` / `Task-Id:` footers and push, so an N-task plan produces N CI runs of a branch nobody is reviewing yet.

The draft-PR skip already covers the case where a PR exists and is still a draft — but pushes to a branch with a *ready* PR, and pushes to `main`, are unguarded.

Options, in preference order:
1. **Keep the PR in draft until the plan completes.** Cheapest change, uses the gate that already exists, and matches how these branches are actually reviewed (once, at the end). Encode it in the Ralph commit/PR step: open as draft, mark ready only when the last task is COMPLETED.
2. **Batch the push.** Keep per-task commits (traceability via footers is non-negotiable) but push once per plan rather than once per task. One CI run validates the whole batch.
3. **`[skip ci]` on intermediate work commits**, reserving a real run for the final push. The repo already uses `[skip ci]` in release commit messages, so the convention exists. Weakest option — it silently skips whichever commit happens to be last if the loop aborts midway.

Pick 1 + 2 together. Then document the convention where the loop can actually see it (`skills/agents-ralph`, `AGENTS.md`) so future agent sessions inherit it.

**Do not** cut validation to achieve this. The goal is the same total validation over fewer runs, not less validation.
requirements: ["Ralph/loop opens PRs as draft and marks ready only at plan completion", "Push batched per plan rather than per task, with per-task commit footers preserved", "Convention documented in the skill and AGENTS.md", "Runs-per-plan measured before and after on a real multi-task plan"]
title: Cut run volume at the source: batch agentic pushes instead of one CI run per task

description:
On the whole-take path the loudness pass gets simpler, not different. NARRATION.md's rule stands: measure ONCE across the take, apply that single gain to everything — per-sentence measurement is meaningless below ~3 seconds and per-clip gain flattens the relative level that makes narration sound like a person.

Today narrate.ts renders raw clips, concatenates them into `take.raw.wav`, measures that, then applies the gain per clip. On the whole-take path the take already IS one file: measure it, apply the gain to it, then slice. Fewer ffmpeg passes and no concat list.

Verify the take still lands at -14 LUFS with a -1.0 dBTP ceiling as read from `docs/marketing/format.json` — NARRATION.md records -14.3 and -14.7 on two scripts as the bar. Gain does not change durations, so timings derived pre-gain stay valid post-gain; assert that rather than assuming it.
requirements: ["Whole-take path produces no take.concat / take.raw.wav intermediates", "Measured integrated LUFS and true peak recorded for at least two scripts", "Short-format budget warning still fires from the same total"]
title: One measurement, one gain, then slice

description:
Create `.agents/prompts/Job_Performance.md` using the skeleton from task 1.

Inspect:
- React Router app bundles: per-route JS size and week-over-week growth; heavy deps pulled into shared chunks; client-side imports of server-only or oversized libraries.
- Waterfalls: loaders that serialize independent queries, missing parallel fetches, over-fetching GraphQL documents that select fields the UI never reads.

description:
Found by the task-5 live gate, and the last remaining `tool` placeholder.

A claude thread that reads five files renders **31 tool cards**: five correct `Read` cards, each trailed by five cards headed `tool`. The group header reads `tool · 31 actions`.

## Root cause — it is not the name resolver

claude's tool chunks carry **no `callId`**. `content_block_start`/`tool_use` emits `metadata: { index, name, toolName, toolUseId }` and each following `input_json_delta` emits `metadata: { index, partialJson }` — the id is `toolUseId`, and the partials carry nothing but streamed argument text.

`applyTurnToolCall` dedupes only when `meta.callId !== null`:

```ts
const exists = meta.callId !== null && events.some((e) => e.kind === 'tool' && e.callId === meta.callId);
```

So for claude the check never fires and every identity-less partial appends a NEW tool event, named by the `'tool'` fallback. Those cards contribute nothing else either: with no `toolCall` key, `toolCallJson` is null, so the streamed `partialJson` is not even rendered as arguments.

## Direction

Fix at the fold, driver-agnostically — a `toolCall` chunk with no tool identity (no `callId` AND no explicitly-reported name) is an argument continuation of the open call, not a new call. Expose that distinction from `normalizeMetadata` rather than comparing against the `'tool'` string, and have `applyTurnToolCall` fold such a chunk into the trailing running tool event instead of appending a placeholder. Keep the append when there is no open call, so a genuinely nameless one-off call is never silently swallowed.

Do not change the drivers: claude's partials legitimately carry no name, and adding a synthetic one would be worse than reading their absence correctly.

## Done when

A claude thread reading five files renders five cards, each headed `Read`, under a `Read · 5 actions` header — no `tool` placeholders — and the same holds after a reload. Verified in the UI, not only in tests.
title: Stop claude's partial-args chunks from synthesizing placeholder tool cards

description:
Goal: every agent (Claude, Cursor, Ralph, the BullMQ worker) creates worktrees in one predictable, user-chosen place instead of a hardcoded sibling directory.

Today `scripts/create_worktree.sh:115` hardcodes `BASE_DIR="$(dirname "$REPO_ROOT")/openthrottle-worktrees"` — the only place the root is decided. Nothing else in the repo references it.

Work:
- Add an `OT_WORKTREE_ROOT` env override in `create_worktree.sh` with this precedence: explicit env var → configured setting (see below) → current default `$(dirname "$REPO_ROOT")/openthrottle-worktrees`. Keep the existing stdout contract intact (the absolute worktree path, and nothing else). Expand `~`, require an absolute path, and `mkdir -p` the root as it already does.
- Surface the setting where a user can actually set it. `/settings/workspace` is the natural home (it was just refreshed into an editor-integration surface in #407). Persisting it needs a store — reuse the existing workspace/repository settings path rather than inventing a new one; if a migration is needed, add it idempotently under `databases/migrations/` per the house SQL rules.
- The server-side provisioner (see the worktree-creation task) must pass the configured root through to the script rather than computing its own, so the worker and the CLI never disagree.
- Document the resolved root in the worktree docs and in the run output at job start, so a run says plainly where it is working.

**Recommendation on placement.** Keep the default *outside* the repo (the existing sibling `../openthrottle-worktrees`) rather than nesting under `<monorepo>/worktrees`. An in-repo root means every worktree's file tree sits inside the Nx workspace: the Nx daemon watches it, Vitest/knip/gitleaks globs can walk it, and it needs a `.gitignore` entry that is easy to get wrong — plus each worktree contains its own `node_modules`, so the repo directory grows without bound. Configurable root gives the "one place" benefit without that exposure. If an in-repo default is still wanted, this task must also add the `.gitignore` entry and verify the Nx daemon, `check:local`, knip, and gitleaks all ignore it — treat that verification as part of the acceptance.

Tests: shell-level check that `OT_WORKTREE_ROOT=/tmp/ot-wt pnpm worktree:new <name>` creates the worktree there and still prints only the path; a server-side test that the provisioner forwards the configured root.

Acceptance: worktree root is settable in one place and honored by `worktree:new`, the Claude `WorktreeCreate` hook path, and the BullMQ provisioner; default behavior is unchanged when nothing is configured.
title: Centralize the worktree root behind one configurable setting

description:
## 1. Leak scan — PASS

`leak-scan --script 05-connect-ot-mcp`: **32 sources, 0 errors, 82 warnings which dedupe to 3 unique**, each given the deliberate glance the task asks for rather than a blanket dismissal:

| Finding | Rule | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace/openthrottle/scripts/run-openthrott…` | high-entropy | The fictional launcher path. A 32+ run of `[A-Za-z0-9/_-]` is what that rule matches by construction. Not a secret and not a real machine. |
| `OPENTHROTTLE_DEVELOPER_API_URL_EXTERNAL` | high-entropy | An env KEY name, printed as a literal `${...}` placeholder. No value on camera. |
| `OPENTHROTTLE_DEVELOPER_API_URL_INTERNAL` | high-entropy | Same. |

No `external-url` warnings at all — the only URLs in frame are localhost, which `ALLOWED_HOSTS` permits.

**`home-path` is clean**, which was this task's central risk. Grepped every frame dump independently for `/Users/`, `/home/`, and each denylist term: nothing. The only `OpenThrottle/monorepo` hit is in `metadata.json`'s description, which is `kind: 'shipped'` — and the denylist is frame-only precisely because the standard description block is supposed to carry the repository URL.

**Editor deep-link hiding holds.** No `vscode://`, `cursor://` or `claude://` in any dump. Worth noting the belt-and-braces: this short's payoff beat is the only one on an app page at all, and the surfaces carry no app chrome.

## 2. Content gates — PASS

- `validate-video-scripts --check`: 64 words against a 132-word budget for a short. (The plan's "63 spoken words is the budget" read the frontmatter's *count* as the budget; the budget comes from `format.json`.)
- Masters exist at 1920x1080 and 1080x1920, **55.15s and 55.09s** — on the 55s target, under the 60s Shorts cap.
- `.srt` cue count 12 == `metadata.json` cues 12.
- `blockedOn: []`.

## 3. Human gates

Cleared: the video demonstrates its exact title claim; every UI state is real and current (the payoff is the live `/plans` route against the demo database); pacing is watchable; captions are legible on a phone and sit at ~78% height, clear of the bottom 15% Shorts UI.

**One item found and FIXED — and it is the one the scan cannot see.** The lower-third card was rendering the literal strings `TITLE_LINE_1` / `TITLE_LINE_2` over the hook, three seconds in. `lower-third.svg` had been exported with its text converted to outlines *with the placeholder words baked into the vector paths*, so `renderCards`' string replace matched nothing, silently. This affected **every video in the catalogue**, not just this one, and `leak-scan.ts` reads the DOM so it is structurally blind to it — exactly the "text baked into an image" gap the checklist lists as a human item. Fixed by restoring `<text>` nodes, and `renderCards` now throws on an absent placeholder (verified the throw fires) so the same export mistake fails the build.

Also fixed on this pass: the runner was not clearing `text/` between takes, so the scan was reading dumps for a beat this flow no longer has.

## Two items left OPEN for the owner

Neither is mine to decide:

1. **"The first three seconds show the payoff."** They do not, and cannot without changing what the short is: the script's own note is "Terminal only, no dashboard until the payoff". I removed the dead air I could — the opening dwell is 150ms rather than 600ms, so typing starts almost immediately instead of holding on an empty prompt — but the first three seconds are still a command being typed. Resolving this properly means a cold open on the dashboard, which is a creative decision about the short's structure.
2. **Loudness is -15.4 LUFS at -3.9 dBTP.** The true peak has ample headroom against the -1.0 ceiling, but the integrated loudness is 1.4 LU under the -14 target. The checklist says "about -14", so this is arguably within tolerance; flagging it rather than silently ticking it.

Licensing and marks: no music bed (fine per the checklist). Third-party names — "Claude Code", "Cursor" — appear only as nominative references to the real products, unaltered, in the output of our own setup command. Fonts are the brand stack already used by every card and caption.

## Status

**Produced, not published.** Upload needs the channel credentials and the owner's decision.
summary: Leak scan 0 errors, 3 unique warns (all accounted for). Checklist walked; found and fixed the lower-third card shipping literal TITLE_LINE_1. Two items left OPEN for the owner: the hook rule vs the script's design, and -15.4 LUFS vs the -14 target. Produced, unpublished.

description:
`collectFromGitWorktreeList` adds every path `git worktree list --porcelain` reports, with no existence check — unlike `collectFromRootScan`, which gates on `isLinkedWorktreeDirectory`. Git keeps reporting deleted worktrees until `git worktree prune` runs, so each dead path currently reaches `describe()` and fires `branch` + `status` + `rev-parse` at a missing directory: three PROBE_FAILED problems (and one silent `aheadCount` failure) for one fact.

Add a single existence gate between candidate collection and `describe()`:

- Partition the deduped candidate list on `existsSync`/`statSync().isDirectory()` of the resolved real path.
- Candidates whose directory is gone become exactly one `STALE_WORKTREE_ENTRY` problem each, carrying the path, and are NOT described (no git probes at all against them) and NOT returned as worktrees.
- Live candidates proceed to `describe()` unchanged.

Stale entries are deliberately excluded from `MAX_DISCOVERED_WORKTREES` accounting — they are not worktrees.

This is also a latency win: four dead paths currently cost twelve `execFile` spawns with a 2s timebox each per page load.
requirements: ["A path reported by git but absent on disk produces one STALE_WORKTREE_ENTRY and zero PROBE_FAILED problems", "No git probe is spawned against a non-existent directory", "Stale entries do not appear in `worktrees` and do not count toward the cap"]
title: Skip stale git worktree entries instead of probing them three times

description:
The bridge between a single take and everything downstream. Consume the word stream in order against the per-sentence SPOKEN text (lexicon-substituted; normalise case and punctuation for matching only) to find each sentence's first and last word.

Cut placement matters: cutting at a word's exact end clips breath and consonant tails. Cut at the midpoint of the gap between the last word of sentence N and the first word of N+1 (falling back to the next word's start when there is no measurable gap), so nothing audible is lost and the sentences still sum to the take.

Slice with ffmpeg into the SAME `NNN-<beat>.wav` names the per-sentence path produces, and write the same `timings.json`. `assemble/timeline.ts` and `assemble/captions.ts` must not need edits — that is the acceptance test.

Desync is the real risk: lexicon substitution turns 'MCP' into 'M C P', which the service may return as one word or three. When the word stream cannot be reconciled with the sentence text, FAIL with the sentence index and the words it could not match — do not fall back to proportional splitting, which drifts silently and shows up later as captions landing on the wrong line.
requirements: ["Pure, unit-tested mapping function separate from the ffmpeg slicing", "Tests cover initialism substitutions, numbers, and a sentence whose words are returned split differently than submitted", "Sliced segment durations sum to the take duration within a frame", "Desync throws with a diagnosable message"]
title: Map word timings to sentence boundaries and slice the take

description:
Addresses hypothesis 2 — the cold token mint. Land only if task 1 shows a credential/token refresh (slow cold mint, or a config/credential file written during `create-chat`).

Problem: `create-chat` and the streaming spawn run back to back with no coordination. If cursor refreshes its auth token on first invocation and writes it to a shared file, two processes can race on a half-written credential — and the user's own `cursor-agent` in a terminal is a third writer. That also explains the workaround: using another agent first burns wall-clock time during which cursor's token settles, and any earlier cursor invocation warms it.

Work:
- Add a process-wide single-flight guard so concurrent first-turns for the same host user mint at most one session at a time (a promise-keyed map in the service, or a small mutex helper). Do not reach for a cross-process file lock unless task 1 shows contention with cursor invocations outside the server.
- Ensure the streaming spawn does not start until the mint has fully closed (it currently awaits `close`, so verify rather than assume — confirm no stdout is still buffering).
- Consider a cheap warm-up probe on server boot or first cursor selection (e.g. `cursor-agent --version` or `cursor-agent status`, whichever is non-mutating) that forces any token refresh outside the user-visible chat path. Gate it behind an env flag and make failure non-fatal.

Tests: unit-test the single-flight guard (two concurrent first-turns → one mint, both resolve to the same id; a rejected mint does not poison later attempts).
title: Serialize the first mint and warm the CLI before the streaming turn

description:
Write the canonical spec doc (repo docs, e.g. docs/monorepo/ or a package README) that becomes the single source of truth the enforcers implement against. Derive it verbatim from the generator template `tools/generators/src/generators/{react,react-router}/files/component/__name__.tsx`.

Spec MUST pin down:
- Exported symbols: `export const Foo` + `export interface FooProps` (empty interface allowed/required).
- Component signature returns `React.ReactElement` (or null), never implicit.
- The exact marker set and ORDER: `// Hooks`, `// Setup`, `// Handlers`, `// Markup`, `// Life Cycle`, `// 🔌 Short Circuit`.
- WHITESPACE rules between markers (one blank line when no early return); how strict to be about leading/trailing blank lines.
- Hoisting rules: out-of-component utils → sibling `../utils`; hardcoded data/config → sibling `../data` (copy → `data.copy.ts`). One component per file.
- SCOPE / exclusions: `react-router-shadcn`, `dist/**`, `__generated__/**`, `__tests__/**`, `*.server.tsx`, story/example files — and the exact glob(s) the enforcers use.
- Edge cases to rule on: `forwardRef`, `memo`, components that legitimately have no props (still export an empty `Props` interface), multiple components in one file.

OWNER PHILOSOPHY (locked): consistency is valued very highly. The DEFAULT is always CONFORM, not exempt. Pass-through / trivially-basic components (error boundaries, context providers) are expected to be made to fit the pattern — and if a component is so basic that conforming feels pointless, that's a signal to question whether it should exist at all (inline/delete it) rather than to exempt it. Concretely: `MailGlobalErrorBoundary` and `LegacyChatTurnProvider` are NOT opt-outs — they conform (or get removed).

OPT-OUT: still define one documented escape hatch (a file-top `/* component-shape: opt-out — <reason> */` pragma both enforcers honor) but frame it as a genuine LAST RESORT for cases where conforming is truly impossible, requiring a written reason. Expect near-zero usage; it is not a convenience for 'this is just a wrapper'.

Deliverable: the spec doc + (ideally empty, or a very short justified) list of legitimately-exempt files. HUMAN GATE — do not start building enforcers until the spec is approved.
title: Codify the primitive-shape spec + scope (design, HUMAN GATE)

description:
## Finding
Plan detail GraphQL selects both `beforeHooks` and `afterHooks`. Each field resolver calls `tasksService.getPlanHooks(planId)` independently → **2 identical service/DB round-trips per plan query**.

## Paths
- `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/plans/plans.resolver.ts` — `beforeHooks` / `afterHooks` ResolveFields (~374–386)
- `packages/nestjs-repositories/src/modules/tasks/tasks.service.ts` — `getPlanHooks`
- Consumer: `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/plans.$planId._index.tsx.graphql` `PlanDetails` fragment selects both hooks

## Measured before
**2× `getPlanHooks(planId)` per `plan(id:)` query** whenever both fields are selected (always, via `PlanDetails`). Existing DataLoader is used for `taskCount` but not for hooks.

```bash
rg -n "getPlanHooks" applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/plans/plans.resolver.ts
```

## Suspected cause
Missing per-request DataLoader / coalescing for `getPlanHooks`. Pattern to copy: `AgentDiscoveryService` SWR+in-flight coalescing (`applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/agent-discovery/`) or the existing `taskCountByPlanIdLoader` in plans loaders.

## Proposed fix
Add a request-scoped DataLoader (or memoize `getPlanHooks` per planId per request) shared by both ResolveFields so the second call is a cache hit.

## Expected after
**1× `getPlanHooks` invocation** per plan id per GraphQL operation when both fields are selected.

## Acceptance
Unit/resolver test: selecting both `beforeHooks` and `afterHooks` on one plan calls `getPlanHooks` exactly once.
title: 8. GraphQL: coalesce beforeHooks/afterHooks getPlanHooks (2× → 1×)

description:
Addresses hypothesis 4 and makes the whole path self-healing. Independent of the root cause — worth landing either way.

Two gaps today:
1. **No retry on mint.** `conversation-stream.service.ts:279-300` catches the throw and immediately publishes a terminal error. A transient cold-start failure kills the turn with no second attempt.
2. **No recovery from a bad persisted id.** Once `conversation.metadata[cursorSessionId]` holds a bad value it is non-empty forever, so the `sessionId === null || sessionId === ''` guard never re-mints and every subsequent turn on that conversation fails identically.

Work:
- Wrap `mintCursorSession()` in a bounded retry: 2 attempts, short backoff, and **only** for retryable failures. Do not retry a genuine auth failure or a missing binary — classify using the error-classification helper from the next task, or add a narrow predicate here and have that task consume it.
- Detect a resume failure in `streamCursorAgent()`: when cursor exits non-zero with a "chat not found" / "invalid chat id" style stderr, surface that as a distinguishable typed error rather than generic terminal text.
- On that signal, have the service clear the persisted `cursorSessionId` metadata and re-mint once, then retry the turn. Bound it to a single re-mint per turn so a persistently broken cursor cannot loop.
- Keep the ephemeral/private-mode path (`persist: false`) correct — nothing to clear there.

Tests in `conversation-stream.service.test.ts` (mocks already exist: `createCursorAgentSessionMock`): mint fails once then succeeds → one terminal-error-free turn; mint fails twice → single terminal error chunk, no retry storm; auth-class failure → no retry at all; resume reports chat-not-found → metadata cleared, exactly one re-mint, turn completes.
title: Retry a failed mint and re-mint a poisoned session id

description:
Net-new — a repo-wide grep confirms there is NO worktree-removal logic anywhere today (no `git worktree remove`, no prune, no server-side teardown). Removal is currently manual, which is why orphan worktrees pile up.

Add `skills/ot-worktree/scripts/destroy.sh` as the third composable action alongside `create.sh` and `heal.sh`. It must be usable standalone AND callable from the other two.

Invocation modes, mirroring `create.sh` so the three feel like one tool:
1. Name as `$1` — resolve to `<root>/<name>` via the same `resolve_worktree_root` ladder from `root.sh`. Never guess a path; if the resolved path is not a registered linked worktree of this repo, fail loudly.
2. Absolute path as `$1` — remove that worktree.
3. No args, run from INSIDE a linked worktree — self-removal. Must `cd` to the primary checkout before removing, since you cannot delete the directory you are standing in.

Behavior:
- Refuse to run against the primary checkout. This is the single most important guard in the script — a bug here deletes the user's actual repo. Assert `is_linked_worktree` for the target and that the resolved path is present in `git worktree list --porcelain` for this repo's common dir. Bail with a clear error otherwise.
- `git worktree remove <path>`; on failure due to a dirty tree, do NOT silently `--force`. Report what is dirty (`git -C <path> status --short`) and require an explicit `--force` flag from the caller. Uncommitted work in a worktree is the exact thing that must not be destroyed by accident.
- Delete the branch only when explicitly asked (`--delete-branch`), and then only if it is merged — `--delete-branch --force` for the unmerged case. Default: leave the branch alone.
- `git worktree prune` afterwards so stale admin dirs in `.git/worktrees/` do not linger.
- Run a repo teardown hook if one exists, BEFORE removal, using the same discovery shape as `provision.sh`: `$OT_WORKTREE_TEARDOWN`, then `.worktree/teardown.sh`. No `scripts/` fallback (there is no incumbent to preserve). Nothing found → no-op. Pass the same env (`OT_SOURCE_REPO`, `OT_WORKTREE_NAME`, `OT_WORKTREE_PATH`), stdin closed. A teardown that exits non-zero aborts the removal — this is where a repo stops a container or releases a port lease, and removing anyway would leak it.
- A `--dry-run` flag that prints exactly what would be removed and exits 0. Given how destructive this is, make it easy to check first.
- Stdout stays quiet (path or nothing); diagnostics on stderr, matching the other two scripts.

Factor the "is this really a removable linked worktree of this repo" check into `common.sh` so `create.sh`'s provision-in-place mode and `heal.sh` can share the same notion of a valid target.

The genuine remaining work is documentation, which moved to the retitled task 4 and to task 5.

description:

**create**
1. `pnpm run worktree:new ot-worktree-smoke` from the primary checkout → lands at `~/worktrees/openthrottle/ot-worktree-smoke`, branch `openthrottle/ot-worktree-smoke`, `setup_worktree.sh` ran (`.env` exists, `.worktree-ports` pinned, ports remapped off 6020), and the LAST line of stdout is the absolute path and nothing else.
2. Hook mode: `printf '{"name":"hook-smoke","cwd":"'$PWD'"}' | ./skills/ot-worktree/scripts/create.sh` → stdout is exactly one absolute path (assert with `| wc -l` = 1 and a `/` prefix); everything else on stderr.
3. Provision-in-place (Cursor mode): from inside a linked worktree, `./skills/ot-worktree/scripts/create.sh` with no args and no stdin → provisions in place, prints its own path, creates nothing new.

**heal**
4. `git worktree add ../plain-smoke` (bypassing the skill), then `cd` in and run `pnpm run worktree:heal` → provisions once; run it a second time → no-op, near-instant.

**destroy** — exercise the guards, not just the happy path.
5. `pnpm run worktree:remove ot-worktree-smoke --dry-run` → prints the target and exits 0 having removed nothing (confirm the directory still exists).
6. `pnpm run worktree:remove ot-worktree-smoke` on a CLEAN worktree → removed, `git worktree list` no longer lists it, `.git/worktrees/` entry pruned, and the branch still exists (default is branch-preserving).
7. Dirty-tree refusal: touch an untracked file in `hook-smoke`, then remove it → MUST fail, print the dirty paths, and leave the worktree intact. Re-run with `--force` → removed.
8. Self-removal: from inside a linked worktree with no args → removes itself without a "cannot remove current directory" error.
9. Primary-checkout guard: run `destroy.sh` targeting the primary checkout path → refuses with a clear error and removes nothing. **Run this in a throwaway clone, not the real checkout.** This is the one failure mode that destroys real work; verify it explicitly rather than assuming.
10. `--delete-branch` on a merged branch removes it; on an unmerged branch it refuses until `--force`.

**foreign repo**
11. In a scratch git repo with the skill synced in and NO provisioner: `create.sh foo` creates `~/worktrees/<scratch-repo>/foo` and logs the no-provisioner no-op without failing; `destroy.sh foo` removes it and logs the no-teardown no-op.

Tear down every smoke worktree afterwards (`git worktree remove` + delete the branches). Record actual observed output in the task summary — if a path fails, fix it rather than noting it.

Wrap the core in a service + resolver, following `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/agent-discovery/` — read `agent-discovery.service.ts` first; it already solves the expensive-probe problem and this should look like its sibling, not a new invention.

1. **Service** with `StaleWhileRevalidateCache`: soft TTL serves fresh, hard TTL blocks rather than serve indefinitely-stale, single coalesced background refresh. Mirror the env-knob naming (`AGENT_DISCOVERY_CACHE_TTL_MS` → `EDITOR_DETECTION_CACHE_TTL_MS`) and document defaults in the module JSDoc as that file does. Use the TTLs task 1 settled.
2. **GraphQL field** returning per-editor presence. Add the presence states as a registered enum so it is typed end to end, and follow the code-first schema flow in CLAUDE.md: boot the server until bootstrap, stop, run `codegen-graphql,codegen-react-router`, commit `applications/openthrottle-server/schema.gql` plus all `__generated__` output.
3. **Decide where it hangs.** Extending the existing `workspaceSettings` payload couples it to that query's failure; a sibling field can fail independently. The plan-detail route hit exactly this and used a separate document so a workspace-settings error could not take the page down. Same reasoning applies — pick deliberately and record why.
4. **Permissions:** match whatever guards `workspaceSettings` today. Do not invent a new permission; do not leave it unguarded.

Validate: `openthrottle-server:test` and the touched packages, sequentially.
summary: editorPresence ships as a sibling top-level query in its own module, NOT a field on workspaceSettings — presence is a nicety and must not be able to take the settings page down with it. Guarded by SETTINGS_READ, matching workspaceSettings. EditorPresenceService mirrors AgentDiscoveryService with StaleWhileRevalidateCache and EDITOR_DETECTION_CACHE_TTL_MS / _HARD_TTL_MS at 60s/600s. Two bugs surfaced: a `private readonly editorPresence` constructor property shadowed the resolver method of the same name (renamed to `presence`), and the module was missing NestjsRepositoriesModule so GqlPermissionsGuard could not resolve RolesService — the server failed to bootstrap, caught only by actually booting rather than by any unit test. Live-verified on a real built server: host run gives CURSOR INSTALLED / VSCODE NOT_FOUND, the same host with the bridge env set gives trusted:false and UNKNOWN for both despite Cursor being physically on disk, and an unauthenticated call is Unauthorized. schema.gql + all __generated__ regenerated and committed. Server lint, typecheck, 1659 tests green.

Acceptance: validation green, two smoke runs verified, docs updated, schedules live.

description:
## Rule
Route primitive shape **R4** (`docs/monorepo/route-primitive-shape.md`): route files stay thin — **210-line cap**, matching the component cap. Soften by hoisting helpers/config/data/JSX chunks into `app/routing/<area>/{utils,config,data,components,hooks}`.

Reported by `pnpm run audit:route-shape` (R1/R3 clean; R4 only).

## Violating files (line counts from audit / wc)
1. `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/skills._index.tsx` — **279** lines (touched 2026-08-17)
2. `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/skills.$slug.tsx` — **237** lines (touched 2026-08-15)
3. `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/auth._index.tsx` — **232** lines (touched 2026-08-17)
4. `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/usage._index.tsx` — **218** lines (touched 2026-08-21)

## Mechanical fix
- Extract loader mappers, filter helpers, and presentational blocks into `~/routing/skills|auth|usage/…`.
- Keep the route as the thin adapter (`loader`/`action`/`meta`/`Component` + section comments).
- Prefer generator-shaped section comments in any new components.

## Deliberate exceptions
None — do not add `route-shape: opt-out` unless genuinely impossible (last resort).

## Acceptance
- `pnpm run audit:route-shape` no longer lists these four files under R4 (or they drop under 210).
- `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:lint` / relevant tests green.
requirements: ["Bring each listed route under the 210-line R4 cap via hoist to routing/<area>", "Do not use opt-out unless last resort", "audit:route-shape quieter; lint/test green"]

description:
The org currently has zero open issues, which makes the first run the cleanest possible test of the prompt's most important property: that an empty inbox produces no writes at all.

Run ad-hoc rather than waiting for cron:

```
pnpm exec workflow-ralph --prompt-file .agents/prompts/Job_Issue_Reporting.md
```

Verify:
- No plan is created (`list_plans_by_status` with titleSubstring '🔁 Issue reporting' stays empty).
- No `append_plan_output` chunk is written.
- No GitHub write of any kind — no comment, label, close, or assignment on any repo.
- No source file is modified (`git status` clean afterwards).
- The run's final message plainly states that the inbox was empty.

Then file one throwaway test issue on OpenThrottle/monorepo, re-run, and verify the opposite path: exactly one plan titled `🔁 Issue reporting: week of <Monday>` with one task, and that a second run in the same week appends nothing new (dedupe holds) rather than opening a second plan. Close the test issue afterwards and note that the OT task stays open — there is no reconcile from GitHub, which is itself the behavior the prompt documents.

Acceptance: both paths verified, evidence recorded on this plan via append_plan_output.
summary: Both paths verified live. EMPTY: no plan, no output chunk, no GitHub write, git status byte-identical to baseline; final message said the inbox was empty and refused to manufacture findings. NON-EMPTY (throwaway on the private OpenThrottle/infrastructure#1 rather than the public monorepo): created exactly one plan 751e5523-0016-44e8-945c-70e8c1daad9b titled "🔁 Issue reporting: week of 2026-08-24" (correct ISO-Monday key for a Friday run) with one task; full intake summary in the description; no GitHub write. DEDUPE: third run same week left the plan at 1 plan / 1 task with updatedAt unchanged and wrote nothing. Untrusted-input handling held — the issue body named this plan and stated what the run "should" do; the run quoted it as a reporter claim and did not obey it. Test issue closed; the OT task stays PENDING, confirming there is no GitHub→OT reconcile, which is the documented behavior. Four defects found and fixed en route: (1) the documented `workflow-ralph --prompt-file` invocation does not work for any of the eleven jobs, (2) `cwd` is deprecated in favour of `repositoryCheckoutId`, (3) `gh repo list`/`gh search issues` were not allowlisted so live enumeration silently fell back to a hardcoded repo set, (4) the required per-run append_plan_output chunk was skipped on the week's first run.
title: Supervised first run: verify it files nothing on an empty inbox

description:
First task in the plan, and deliberately empty of logic. The recording pipeline needs a home **before** it grows the typed-script layer, not after.

## Generate, do not hand-write

```bash
NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:package \
  --name=openthrottle-showroom --organization=@openthrottle --type=node
```

That yields `packages/openthrottle-showroom` as `@openthrottle/openthrottle-showroom`, matching the `openthrottle-mcp` / `openthrottle-agentic-ralph` precedent (directory repeats the prefix; the npm name is `@openthrottle/<dir>`).

## Settled: source-first, private, OpenThrottle-internal

No `build` target. Follow the existing source-first pattern exactly — `packages/nodejs-utils` and `packages/react-router-chat` are the reference implementations:

- `main` and `types` both `./src/index.ts`; consumers transpile the source.
- `private: true`.
- Nx tags: `name:@openthrottle/openthrottle-showroom`, `production:false` (this is content tooling, not code in a deployed app — see `packages/nestjs-express` and `tools/ollama-proxy` for the precedent), `publish:false`, `technology:nodejs`, `type:package`.
- Targets: `lint`, `test`, `typecheck`, plus the `__build` / `__build-package` placeholder discriminators that mark a package as intentionally build-less (`packages/AGENTS.md`).

**Scope is OpenThrottle-only, for now.** Nothing outside this repo consumes it, so do not design for external consumers: no generalised plugin seams, no provider abstractions beyond the TTS backend interface that already exists and already earned itself. Depending on repo internals is fine and expected. If it ever needs to ship on its own, that is a later decision with its own evidence.

Validate the package after generating with `pnpm nx:validate-tags` and `pnpm nx run monorepo:knip`.

## Sketch the internal layout

Empty directories are fine at this stage; the point is that the relocation task has an obvious destination for each piece:

```text
packages/openthrottle-showroom/src/
├── episodes/    # typed episode modules (later tasks)
├── flows/       # demo flows
├── surfaces/    # typeset shell/HTML surfaces
├── fixtures/    # the fictional demo workspace
├── runner/      # Playwright capture
├── narrate/     # TTS + timings
├── assemble/    # ffmpeg masters, captions, cards, metadata
└── scan/        # leak scan
```

Single entry point per the no-deep-imports rule: everything a consumer needs re-exports from `src/index.ts`. Exports that are package public API need a JSDoc `@public` tag so Knip keeps them.

## Done when

`lint`, `typecheck` and `test` all pass on the new project with nothing but the scaffold in it, `pnpm nx:validate-tags` is clean, and `pnpm nx show projects --with-target=build` does **not** list it.
summary: DONE — packages/openthrottle-showroom scaffolded private + source-first, tagged production:false/publish:false, src/ layout sketched. Commit fca1c31f.
title: Generate the openthrottle-showroom package scaffold

description:
Add `skills/ot-worktree/scripts/provision.sh`. Given a worktree path and the primary checkout, find and run the repo's provisioner.

Discovery order, first hit wins, all optional:
1. `$OT_WORKTREE_PROVISION` — absolute, or relative to the worktree root.
2. `<worktree>/.worktree/provision.sh`
3. `<worktree>/scripts/setup_worktree.sh`

Nothing found → log `no repo provisioner found — worktree created but not provisioned` and return 0. That is a valid outcome, not an error.

When found, run it with: cwd = the worktree, stdin closed (`</dev/null` so prompts take defaults), stdout redirected to stderr, and exported `OT_SOURCE_REPO` (primary checkout), `OT_WORKTREE_NAME`, `OT_WORKTREE_PATH`. A non-zero exit from the provisioner propagates (worktree creation fails loudly rather than handing back a half-built tree).

Honor `CLAUDE_WORKTREE_SETUP=0` as the existing skip escape hatch, and add the tool-agnostic alias `OT_WORKTREE_SETUP=0`. Refuse to exec a provisioner that is not a regular readable file; if it is not executable, run it via `sh` rather than failing.
summary: provision.sh delegates to the repo hook: provision_worktree (OT_WORKTREE_PROVISION → .worktree/provision.sh → scripts/setup_worktree.sh) and teardown_worktree (OT_WORKTREE_TEARDOWN → .worktree/teardown.sh), both running with cwd=worktree, stdin closed, stdout→stderr, OT_SOURCE_REPO/NAME/PATH exported. Missing hook = logged no-op rc 0; failing hook propagates (verified rc=3); non-executable hook runs via sh; OT_WORKTREE_SETUP=0 / CLAUDE_WORKTREE_SETUP=0 skip.
title: Write skill scripts: provision.sh (repo-provisioner delegation)

description:
Follow-up raised by the run-detail UI task, which flagged this but could not implement it against the existing capability.

**Why `mcpAutoApprove` cannot drive this warning.** The driver audits established that `mcpAutoApprove: false` means "this driver emits no MCP flags" — which is true for BOTH claude/opencode (they attach the workspace's MCP servers automatically and work fine) AND codex/grok (they cannot reach them at all). The flag conflates the two, so reading it in the UI would warn on the wrong drivers.

What the form actually needs is a distinct capability, e.g. `attachesWorkspaceMcp: boolean` on `DriverCapabilities` — does this CLI resolve the workspace's committed MCP config? Per the audits (recorded in the plan output stream):

- cursor — true (with the `--approve-mcps` fix)
- claude — true (`.mcp.json`, automatic)
- opencode — true (`opencode.json`, automatic)
- grok — false (reads its own TOML; repo ships no `./.grok/config.toml`)
- codex — false (user-scope `~/.codex/config.toml` only; no project-config concept at all)

Steps:
1. Add `attachesWorkspaceMcp` to `DriverCapabilities` in `packages/openthrottle-drivers/src/types/index.ts`, with the values above and each driver's rationale already documented in its JSDoc.
2. Expose it to the developer app. The schedule form needs per-driver capability data; check whether driver discovery already surfaces capabilities over GraphQL before adding a field.
3. On `schedule.create` / `schedule.$jobId.edit`, warn (do not block) when the selected driver has `attachesWorkspaceMcp: false`. Keep copy in the nearest `data.*.ts` per the component/data boundary rule, and use `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn`.
4. Add render-level Vitest coverage for the warning shown/hidden per driver.

Note for codex specifically: reachability is a property of the HOST, not the repo, so the honest copy is that OT cannot verify the server is registered for that CLI — not a flat claim that it is missing.
summary: Surface driver MCP reachability on schedule create/edit, so an MCP-dependent prompt paired with an MCP-incapable driver fails loudly at authoring time.
title: Warn on the schedule form when the chosen driver cannot reach workspace MCP

Root cause of the false positive: this plan's own description already lists

dependency it uses looks orphaned. The two findings were filed as separate items

description:
Create `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/settings/utils/workspace-editor-presence-status.ts`.

Exports:

1. `WORKSPACE_EDITOR_PRESENCE_STATUS: Record<EditorPresenceState, EditorPresenceStatusDescriptor>` — an **exhaustive** Record over the generated `EditorPresenceState` enum (`Installed | NotFound | Unknown`) so adding a state to the schema fails typecheck here until it is given a treatment. Same discipline as `WORKSPACE_EDITOR_LABELS` in `routing/settings/config/workspace-editors.ts`.

   Descriptor shape (no `as` casts, explicit interface, alphabetized keys):
   - `icon` — lucide component (`CircleCheckIcon` installed / `CircleDashedIcon` not-found / `CircleHelpIcon` unknown)
   - `indicatorClassName` — the dot/tone class for the status marker
   - `badgeVariant` — the shadcn `Badge` variant to pair with it
   - `label` — short suffix ("detected" / "not detected" / "unknown")
   - `srLabel` — full sentence for screen readers, e.g. "Cursor was detected on this machine" via a `(editorLabel: string) => string` builder
   - `tone` — `'positive' | 'neutral' | 'muted'` const-union (no enum), so consumers can branch without knowing class names

2. `buildEditorPresenceIndex(editors)` — takes `readonly EditorPresenceEntry[] | null | undefined` and returns a `Map<WorkspaceEditorId, EditorPresenceState>` that yields `Unknown` for any editor not present in the probe result. This is what makes it safe to render availability next to *every* picker option, including ones the probe never covered.

3. `getEditorPresenceStatus(state)` — thin accessor over the Record for consumers that only have a state.

Copy: add the new strings to `WORKSPACE_SETTINGS_COPY` in `routing/settings/data/data.copy.ts` alongside the existing `presenceHeading` / `presenceInstalledSuffix` / `presenceNotFoundSuffix` / `presenceNotFoundCaption` keys — reuse those four rather than inventing second wordings for the same idea. New keys needed: an unknown suffix and the untrusted-probe note (see the last task).

Tests: `utils/__tests__/workspace-editor-presence-status.test.ts` — assert the Record covers every `Object.values(EditorPresenceState)` member, and that `buildEditorPresenceIndex` fills `Unknown` for a missing editor, tolerates `null`, and ignores an unrecognized editor id without throwing.

No component changes in this task.
summary: Added `utils/workspace-editor-presence-status.ts`: exhaustive `Record<EditorPresenceState, EditorPresenceStatusDescriptor>` (badgeVariant, icon, indicatorClassName, label, srLabel builder, tone const-union), plus `getEditorPresenceStatus`, `buildEditorPresenceIndex` and a `readEditorPresence(index, editor)` accessor that centralizes the "unprobed reads as UNKNOWN" rule. 6 new copy keys in WORKSPACE_SETTINGS_COPY (sr suffixes, unknown suffix, untrusted note); reused the 4 existing presence keys. 18 unit-test cases.

description:

- **06-prd-to-plan** — a fictional two-page PRD in the browser, `/plans/upload-decompose`, drag the file onto the drop zone, **Decompose**, the proposed plan and tasks rendering, edit one title, delete one task, **Save**. If it does, this episode is `replay` rather than `live` and its `production.recording` is currently wrong.
- **09-tags-and-rules** — `/rules`, open the rule that just fired, **New rule**, pick a tag and an action, save, back to a plan to add the tag and watch the rule fire, hold on the rule-applications list. The 'watch it fire' beat is the one to verify early: it needs the rule to actually apply within the take, not eventually.
- **10-notes** — a note open on a hard-won gotcha, `/notes/create`, a title, two sentences of body, save, then find it back by searching the symptom rather than the title. That last pair is the payoff and it needs both the notes rows and a working search surface; if search is still blocked, this episode's `blockedOn` gains an entry rather than the flow faking the result.
- **14-scheduled-runs** — `/schedule`, **New job**, pick a plan, pick the repository checkout, save, then open a seeded past run for output and token cost. The snapshot has 10 jobs and 20 runs plus token usage, so the read half is real; the create half mutates.

Done when each records twice in a row and the second take is not filming the first take's leftovers.
summary: Four flows that type and save, on top of whatever convention the mutation task settled.

description:
**This task is a human gate — an agent cannot complete it.** It gathers the handful of facts every later task needs. Do not guess handles; a wrong handle silently renders no Sponsor button.

Decide and record in this task's summary:

1. **Platforms + handles.** `FUNDING.yml` supports one `github:` entry (a user or org, up to 4 accounts) plus platform keys (`open_collective`, `ko_fi`, `polar`, `buy_me_a_coffee`, `liberapay`, `patreon`, `tidelift`, `thanks_dev`, `issuehunt`, `lfx_mentorship`, `community_bridge`) and up to 4 `custom:` URLs. Verify the exact supported key list against the GitHub docs page at implementation time rather than trusting this list. Recommended minimum: `github: [visormatt]` (or the `OpenThrottle` org, if the org is the sponsee) — one canonical destination beats five half-configured ones. A single `custom:` URL pointing at the funding page from task 4 is a reasonable second entry.
2. **Sponsee identity** — individual (`visormatt`) or the `OpenThrottle` org? Note that the trademark/entity plan deliberately deferred forming a company, and GitHub Sponsors for an *org* wants an org bank/Stripe relationship. Individual is the lower-friction answer while no entity exists.
3. **GitHub Sponsors enrollment status.** Enrollment requires a sponsee profile, Stripe Connect payout setup, and tax/identity forms; it is not instant. Record whether it is complete, pending review, or not started.
4. **Which repos get the button** — the public mirror `OpenThrottle/OpenThrottle`, the canonical `OpenThrottle/monorepo`, and/or the org-level `.github` repo as an org-wide default. Task 3 depends on this answer.
5. **Tier amounts.** Confirm the intended monthly tiers (the stated target is $100–$200/mo total recurring). Task 2's cost model will either validate or adjust these.

If enrollment is incomplete, that does **not** block the rest of the plan — ship the file and docs, and note in the funding page that the button goes live on approval.
requirements: ["Platform keys and exact handles recorded (verified against the current GitHub FUNDING.yml docs)", "Sponsee identity chosen: individual vs OpenThrottle org, with the no-entity-yet constraint acknowledged", "GitHub Sponsors enrollment status recorded (complete / pending / not started)", "Target repo(s) for the button decided, including whether the org .github repo supplies an org-wide default", "Intended monthly tier amounts written down"]
summary:
DECIDED (owner answered 2026-08-17), then CORRECTED against the GitHub API — read the corrections, they override the owner's stated answers on two points.

1. PLATFORMS/HANDLES: `github: OpenThrottle` + one `custom:` URL. Schema verified live: community_bridge, github (1 or up to 4), issuehunt, ko_fi, liberapay, open_collective, patreon, tidelift, polar, buy_me_a_coffee, thanks_dev, custom (up to 4 URLs). Must live at .github/FUNDING.yml on the DEFAULT BRANCH.

2. SPONSEE IDENTITY — CORRECTED. Owner said "individual (visormatt)". The API says otherwise, authenticated as visormatt: user(visormatt) hasSponsorsListing=FALSE, sponsorsListing=null, viewerCanSponsor=false; organization(OpenThrottle) hasSponsorsListing=TRUE with a public listing "sponsors-OpenThrottle". The ORG is the enrolled sponsee. Writing `github: visormatt` would have produced exactly the documented silent failure — no button, no error.

3. ENROLLMENT: COMPLETE, but on the ORG. One open item: the org listing has ZERO TIERS defined (tiers.nodes = []), so there is nothing for a sponsor to click through to. The $100/$200 tiers must be created in the org Sponsors dashboard — human-only, tracked as a follow-up task.

4. TARGET REPOS — CORRECTED. Plan assumed OpenThrottle/monorepo is private; the API says private=false, it is PUBLIC. So a root .github/FUNDING.yml renders a public button there directly. The mirror OpenThrottle/OpenThrottle is still a FILTERED EXPORT of applications/openthrottle/ only (root tree = 8 files, no .github/ at all), so it needs the org-level default. OpenThrottle/.github EXISTS (holds .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE, PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md, profile/) and has NO FUNDING.yml — the owner must add one there; it is a separate repo outside this PR's reach.

5. TIERS: $100/mo = required floor, $200/mo = toward desired. Validated by task 1: required $98.52/mo (so $100 genuinely covers the floor), desired $431.55/mo (so $200 is a real step with room to grow).
title: Human gate: pick funding platforms and enroll

description:
Carried from task `aa882633` of plan `7aead6c5` (closed CANCELED by `e1b32fde` — its Monaco premise was false and nothing shipped under it).

## Measured composition of the 232.8 KB `plans._planId._index-*.js`

| Content | KB |
|---|---:|
| Plan-detail feature code (tabs, tables, run config, hooks, transparency panel) | ~134 |
| **zod** (v4 core + JSON-Schema converter — `metadataRegistry`, `reused === 'ref'`, `cycles`) | **~72** |
| misc | ~27 |

The zod comes from `app/routing/plans/utils/workflow-ralph-validate.ts` → `RalphPlanRunTuningInputSchema` from `~/__generated__/schemas`. It validates workflow-ralph run options **live as the user edits**, mirroring `tools/workflows/src/utils/parsers.ts`.

Ruled out already: Monaco is not in this chunk (0 occurrences — it loads from CDN at runtime); the `zod/v3` copy reached from the route's `action` helpers is correctly stripped from the client build; all four app packages already declare `sideEffects: false`.

## The decision
**A. Keep client-side validation**, accept ~233 KB. Live inline feedback while editing run options is real UX value for ~72 KB on one feature page.

**B. Move validation server-side.** Removes ~31% of the chunk, but this is a **UX change, not a code-split** — users lose inline feedback and get round-trip validation instead. Needs a product call, not just a perf call.

## Independent of the above
The **14.5 KB `EditorWindow` lazy-load** is still available on its own merits — worth 14.5 KB for users landing on the Output/Tasks tabs, at the cost of a Suspense boundary. It was deliberately not done in `7aead6c5` because it did not meet that task's acceptance; judged on its own it is a small, clean win. Decide separately.

## Context worth keeping in view
The route's real first-load cost was never this chunk — it was `MarkdownRenderer` at 505.6 KB of a 1292.8 KB static graph, fixed by task 11 of `7aead6c5`.

## Acceptance
A decision is recorded for the zod question (A or B) and for the `EditorWindow` lazy-load (do / don't), each with its reasoning.
title: DECIDE: move workflow-ralph run-option validation server-side?

description:
`app/routing/plans/hooks/usePlanDetailRouteData.tsx` derives its type from `typeof loader`, so after the loader change its `ledger`/`outputChunks`/`runHistory`/`tagVocabulary`/`workspaceRepositories` keys are promises and every consumer stops type-checking. Fix the consumers, do not paper over it with casts (`.agents/rules`: avoid `as`).

Per consumer:

- **`PlanTabDetails.tsx`** reads `planRunAuditRows` and `recentPlanRuns` for `PlanWorkflowRunTransparency`. Keep the summary/markdown/requirements content rendering immediately from critical data, and wrap only the transparency block in `PlanDeferredSection` with `PlanRunTransparencySkeleton`.
- **`PlanTabOutput.tsx`** currently takes `chunks` as a prop from `PlanDetailRoute`. Move the boundary here (or in `PlanDetailRoute` around it, whichever keeps the tab under the shape line cap) with `PlanOutputStreamSkeleton`. The empty-state copy must render only once chunks have actually resolved as empty — never as the pending state.
- **`PlanTabConfiguration.tsx`** takes `repositories`. Wrap in `PlanDeferredSection` with `PlanConfigurationTabSkeleton`; the save handlers stay wired but disabled while pending (see the next task).
- **`PlanToolbar.tsx`** takes `editors` and `tagVocabulary`, both already optional with `= []` / `!= null` guards, so the toolbar's own rendering is unaffected. Wrap just the tag-chip region and the editor-links region in boundaries so the rest of the toolbar (title, status, Run/Queue) paints immediately.
- **`PlanDetailRoute.tsx`** stops threading resolved arrays through props for the deferred keys; the tab counter `Tasks ({resolvedTaskCount}/{tasks.length})` keeps reading critical `tasks` and must not become a skeleton.

Also: `usePlanDetailRoute.ts` reads `loaderData.planRunAuditRows[0]?.isStale` for the toolbar's stale badge. That is now deferred — the stale badge must be absent (not "not stale", and not a skeleton) until run history resolves. Make that explicit in the hook's return (`newestRunIsStale: boolean | undefined`) and have the toolbar render nothing for `undefined`.

Update the existing tab tests (`app/routing/plans/components/__tests__/PlanTabDetails.test.tsx` and siblings) — they build resolved loader data today and will need promises. Keep using `component` (not `screen`) and `userEvent`, per the repo test rules.
summary: Wire the deferred keys through the existing useRouteLoaderData accessor into PlanTabDetails, PlanTabOutput, PlanTabConfiguration and PlanToolbar without prop-drilling promises through the tab shell.
title: Move the tab consumers behind boundaries and make usePlanDetailRouteData promise-aware
