description:
`plan-rules.processor.ts` builds its evaluation context with `environment: null` (called out in its own header comment), so environment-qualified rules never match on the worker path — they only apply on qualified plan-context reads. The rules form offers the control with no hint of that, so a user can save an `environment: ralph` rule that appears to do nothing.

Pick one and make the behavior and the UI agree:

- **Preferred:** thread an environment onto `PlanRulesEvaluateJobData` (`plan-rules.types.ts`) from the trigger site, so `PlanRulesEvaluationService.enqueueEvaluation` callers that know their environment pass it and the worker evaluates with a real value. Callers that do not know it keep passing null. Note that the dedup id in `plan-rules.constants.ts` is per-plan — decide whether environment belongs in the dedup key or whether last-write-wins is acceptable.
- **Fallback:** leave the worker as-is and add explicit copy to `RuleFormMatchSection` stating environment-qualified rules apply only on agent context reads, not on plan evaluation.

Whichever path, update the processor header comment and `data.copy.ts` so the documented behavior is the real one.
title: Make the environment layer honest on the worker path

description:
## The problem
Institutional Memory is a named roadmap theme ([`ce7e2773`](ce7e2773-3c71-4e8f-8229-11355d021723)) and a documented product feature (`docs/openthrottle/features.md`), but the local-first / self-host path silently has no vector memory. `databases/README.md` Embedding dimension strategy documents **Option A**: ingest and openthrottle-server only insert embeddings when the vector length is **1536**; non-matching Ollama models (`nomic-embed-text` 768, `mxbai-embed-large` 1024, `all-minilm` 384) are **skipped with no error**. Option B ("Different dimension — future") was never built. Ollama integration itself was marked completed ([`97e15b8c`](97e15b8c-9728-4677-8a12-17b2120933d3)), which makes the gap look closed when it is not. Evidence from this job: `semantic_search` returned **zero chunks** for every query on both the 2026-08-17 run and this 2026-08-21 run, while `list_sources` / `list_plans_by_status` / `health` succeed — so GraphQL and Postgres are up, and the vector path is the broken leg. Self-Host & Operate markets "local models as a first-class privacy path"; without Option B that path cannot power `ask OT`, this monthly job's own dedupe, or any agent that depends on semantic retrieval.

## The proposed change
Ship **Option B** end-to-end: configurable embedding dimension (env), a storage path that does not break the existing OpenAI `vector(1536)` flow (separate columns/tables or a dimension-tagged store — pick one in a short ADR), query embedding using the same provider/dimension as ingest, fail-*loud* when configured embedding length mismatches (never silent skip), re-ingest docs/agent-assets/plans on dimension change, and a doctor/health check that reports "embeddings: empty / dimension mismatch / ok". Keep OpenAI 1536 as the default when `OPENAI_API_KEY` is set and Ollama env is unset. Align CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md local-embeddings guidance with the real working path.

## What it unlocks
Makes Institutional Memory real for Docker/self-host installs that refuse OpenAI; unblocks every OT workflow that assumes `semantic_search` (including this Job_*, `/ot/ask`, plan dedupe); removes a class of "knowledge base is empty" false bugs that are actually dimension skips; completes the Ollama story that was prematurely marked done.

## Rough size
5–8 days (ADR + migration + ingest/server/MCP path + health check + re-ingest docs). Touches `databases/migrations`, ingest scripts (`database:import-docs`, `database:import-agent-assets`, plan/task embed writers), `packages/nestjs-vector-search`, `applications/openthrottle-server` search/embed path, `packages/openthrottle-mcp` (`semantic_search`), docs under `databases/README.md` and `docs/openthrottle/`.

## Migration risk
Medium–high on the data path: wrong migration can strand existing 1536 rows or mix dimensions in one index. Mitigate: never alter existing `vector(1536)` columns in place (README already requires this); additive Option B store; explicit re-ingest; feature-flag the query path. Rollback: point query embedding back to OpenAI-only / disable Ollama env; drop the additive table if needed.

## The strongest argument against
This environment may simply be missing `OPENAI_API_KEY` while Ollama is misconfigured — a one-line ops fix, not a multi-day schema project. Option A was an explicit, documented decision to keep the schema simple; building Option B for a single-operator dogfood box that can afford OpenAI embeddings is optimizing the brochure ("local-first") over the working default. If almost all production installs will use OpenAI for embeddings anyway, loud failure + better docs ("set OPENAI_API_KEY or your KB stays empty") is the honest cheaper fix.
summary: Implement databases/README Option B so Ollama/local embeddings actually populate and query the knowledge base — today's silent 1536-only skip leaves semantic_search empty on the self-host path.
title: Ship Ollama embedding Option B — local-first Institutional Memory that does not silently no-op

description:
## The problem
Setup/bootstrap was the single most-patched subsystem of the month: #290 (leak audit), #292 (dual-volume Postgres reset), #296 (one-command Docker bootstrap), #297 (MCP auth self-load), #298 (MCP config SSOT), #299 (env prep), #306 (MCP install script), #321 (bootstrap-secrets file + MCP setup skip + RBAC superset), #324 (ensure-migrations gate), #342 (admin permission backfill), #344 (guarantee all six .demo-workstation.local fields), #345/#346 (setup trim/polish) — roughly a dozen PRs in 30 days, each fixing drift between the four parallel install paths: ./scripts/setup.sh (local), the Dockerized bootstrap, pnpm run worktree:new provisioning (#271), and CI. Each path hand-maintains its own env, secrets, DB, migration, MCP-registration, and seed-user handling, so every fix lands in one path and the others drift until they break — the recorded gotchas (stale .env password symptom, MCP config shadowing, pinned-port fallbacks) are all instances of this. The repeated patching says the design, not the scripts, is what is wrong.

## The proposed change
A single bootstrap engine — a small typed CLI package (e.g. packages/openthrottle-bootstrap or under tools/) — that models setup as declarative, idempotent, individually-verifiable steps: env file materialization, secrets (the six bootstrap-secrets fields as a schema, not a convention), Docker services, migrations (delegating to the existing schema_migrations ledger), MCP registration + auth token self-load, seed user + RBAC. Each step exposes check / apply / explain. The four entry points become thin callers selecting a step profile, so a fix lands once. Ship `doctor` as the flagship: run all checks, print exactly what is broken and the one command to fix it — replacing today's guess-and-patch debugging.

## What it unlocks
Ends the fix-one-path-break-another cycle (a dozen PRs/month of it); gives the Self-Host & Operate roadmap theme (ce7e2773) its core artifact — for an open-core project post-launch, install-success *is* the product's front door, and `doctor` converts every future setup bug report into a self-diagnosis; makes worktree and CI provisioning trustworthy for agents (several recorded agent failure modes are bootstrap drift).

## Rough size
5–8 days including migrating all four paths and deleting the superseded script logic. Touches scripts/, tools/ or packages/ (new package), docker compose entrypoints, .github/workflows, docs.

## Migration risk
The main risk is breaking the paths that currently work while porting them — mitigated by migrating one entry point at a time with the old script kept as fallback for one release each, and by `doctor` being additive from day one (pure reads). Rollback per path: repoint the entry script at its previous implementation.

## The strongest argument against
The patch storm coincided exactly with public-launch preparation — a one-time event. If setup churn drops to near zero next month on its own, this builds a framework to solve a problem that just finished existing; shell scripts that now work are cheaper to keep than a bespoke setup engine that itself needs tests, docs, and maintenance. A fair alternative is to wait one month: if the setup-fix rate stays materially above zero post-launch, build it; if not, only extract `doctor` as a read-only script and stop there.
summary: Extract the env/secrets/DB/migrations/MCP/seed steps — currently duplicated and serially patched across four install paths — into one idempotent, self-verifying bootstrap engine with a diagnosis mode.
title: One bootstrap engine behind all four setup paths (setup.sh, Docker, worktree:new, CI) + doctor mode

description:
Pure-function groundwork in `applications/openthrottle-server/src/queues/scheduled-agent-jobs/scheduled-agent-jobs.constants.ts`.

1. **`resolveScheduledAgentJobConcurrencyKey({ cwd, worktree, driverSupportsWorktree })`** — returns the string identity of the directory a run will actually mutate, or `null` when the run needs no serialisation:
   - No worktree requested, or the driver has no `worktree` capability → the resolved cwd (normalised: trimmed, trailing separator stripped) so a legacy explicit `cwd` and a targeted checkout resolving to the same path collide as required by the plan's acceptance criteria.
   - Worktree requested with an explicit NAME → `<cwd>` + the worktree name, so two schedules naming the same worktree on the same checkout still serialise while different names overlap.
   - Worktree requested flag-only (`worktree: ''`, the CLI auto-names a fresh directory per run) → `null` (no lock; already isolated per run).
2. **`resolveScheduledAgentJobsConcurrency()`** — reads `SCHEDULED_AGENT_JOBS_CONCURRENCY`, falling back to a new default > 1. Invalid/non-positive values fall back, matching the existing `resolveScheduledAgentJobTimeoutMs` shape. Note that `docs/openthrottle/scheduled-agent-jobs-usage.md` already documents this env with a footnote saying it is a compile-time constant — that footnote goes away in the docs task.
3. Rewrite the `SCHEDULED_AGENT_JOBS_CONCURRENCY` JSDoc so it describes the keyed-lock mechanism instead of the ef4b5c75 'left at 1' rationale.

Unit tests in `scheduled-agent-jobs.constants.test.ts` covering each key branch (including path normalisation collisions) and the env parsing fallbacks.
requirements: ["resolveScheduledAgentJobConcurrencyKey normalises paths so an explicit cwd and a checkout path resolving to the same directory produce the same key", "A flag-only worktree request yields a null key (no serialisation)", "A worktree request on a driver without the worktree capability is ignored and keys on the cwd", "resolveScheduledAgentJobsConcurrency defaults above 1 and rejects invalid env values", "Vitest unit tests cover every branch"]

description:
Separate bug found while re-running the generator on PR #468's branch. Generating a component whose `__tests__/<Name>.test.tsx` already exists reports `UPDATE` and OVERWRITES it with the starter stub. In that run it silently destroyed two fully written test files; they were only recovered because the work was already committed and could be restored with `git checkout --`.

Observed output:
  CREATE packages/react-router-chat/src/components/ChatActivityGroup.tsx
  UPDATE packages/react-router-chat/src/components/__tests__/ChatActivityGroup.test.tsx

An agent regenerating a component to check conventions — exactly what the rest of this plan encourages — will lose real work. Decide the right behavior and implement it: skip an existing test file and report it as skipped, or refuse the whole invocation unless an explicit overwrite flag is passed. Skipping is likely the better default since the component file itself is the thing being regenerated. Whichever is chosen, the reported action must be truthful — `UPDATE` for a destructive overwrite of hand-written content is the core of the bug.

Check whether the same clobbering applies to the component file itself and to the other sub-generators (`react` and `react-router`: form, hook, modal, route, table, util) and to stories, and fix the class of bug rather than the one instance. Add regression tests.
requirements: ["Regenerating a component over an existing hand-written test file does not destroy it", "The action reported for each file is truthful — no destructive write reported as UPDATE", "The behavior is consistent across react and react-router sub-generators, not patched for component only", "Regression tests cover the existing-test-file case for at least one sub-generator per generator"]

description:
This is the task that decides whether the workbench survives. With ~60 component groups, hand-writing every story guarantees the catalog stalls partway and rots. The generator must exist before the backfill starts.

Per repo policy, generators come before hand-written code. Inspect the existing shape first:

```
NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx list @tools/generators
NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:react --describe
```

Placement: a `story` sub-generator under `@tools/generators:react` is the natural home (alongside the existing `component`, `hook`, and `util` sub-generators) — `react-router` is for router-coupled app code, and the shadcn package is router-free. Confirm against `--describe` output before committing to placement.

Requirements:

- Accept comma-separated `--name` values for batch scaffolding, matching the convention of sibling sub-generators (confirm via `--describe` that `name.description` reads `Comma-separated names supported.`)
- Emit `<Component>.stories.tsx` co-located next to the component source
- Template should include a typed `Meta` and a default story, and derive `argTypes` from the component's `cva` variant map where one exists — `Button`'s `size`/`variant` maps are the reference case
- Follow the existing template conventions; `tools/generators/src/generators/template-conventions.test.ts` enforces them
- Add a generator test mirroring `generator.component.test.ts`

The generated output should be genuinely useful on first run, not a stub someone has to rewrite — that is the difference between a backfill that completes and one that does not.

description:
Three parsers become zero. All three now live inside `packages/openthrottle-showroom`, so this is intra-package rewiring rather than a cross-boundary import.

## Replace

- **`narrate/parse-script.ts`** — delete the file reading and front-matter regex; `parseScript(slug, variant?)` becomes a thin adapter over `getVariant` + the `sentences` helper, keeping the existing `ParsedScript` / `NarrationSentence` return shape so `narrate.ts`, the render cache and the timings writer need no changes beyond the variant plumbing.
- **`assemble/assemble.ts`** — drop the three regexes (`^title:`, `^titleCard:`, and the `/^ {2}- (.+)$/gm` tag scrape that matches any two-space bullet in the file). Read `episode.youtube.title`, `episode.production.titleCard` and `episode.youtube.tags` directly. The hardcoded description block moves out in favour of the composition helper.
- **`scan/leak-scan.ts`** — it reads `metadata.json` and the `.srt`; confirm it still resolves both once outputs are variant-namespaced, and update its path resolution if not.

## Narration matching becomes time-based — the substantial part

`assemble/timeline.ts` matches narration to flow beats **positionally**: nth narration sentence to nth flow beat. The 05 flow carries a comment warning that an extra flow beat "does not merely go unnarrated — it shifts every later beat's narration one beat early".

The typed format makes that untenable, and deliberately so. A variant owns its own timings — narration is a list of `['0:09', 'the words']` cues, independent of the episode's beats, because nothing says a slower payoff-first read speaks at a problem-first read's moments. There is no longer an nth-to-nth correspondence to rely on.

Replace it with a time-based reconciliation:

- The runner's `manifest.json` stays the authority on when a beat **actually** happened. Script and cue times are intent; captured spans are fact.
- Map each cue onto the beat span its `t` falls within, then keep the existing rule that governs the result: where a beat's narration runs longer than its on-screen action, **extend the dwell on the last frame** rather than speeding the picture up. Sped-up picture is the loudest "this was automated" tell there is.
- A cue whose time falls outside every captured span is an error worth naming, not a silently dropped line.

This removes the positional hazard rather than relocating it. Cover it with tests over a fixture manifest — this is the part of the rewiring most likely to be quietly wrong, and a wrong answer here means narration drifting against picture in a shipped video.

## Watch for

- `runner/format.ts` owns `repositoryRoot()` and `outputRoot()`. Do not grow a second copy of either alongside the episode helpers.
- `runner/run.ts` resolves flows by dynamic import template `../flows/${flowId}.flow.ts`. Co-located episodes make that `../episodes/${id}/flow.ts`.
- Anything still importing the old `tests/demo/**` paths.

## Done when

A narrate → assemble run for one migrated episode produces byte-identical narration text and an equivalent `metadata.json` to a pre-migration run, the three regexes are gone, and the timeline's cue-to-beat mapping is covered by tests.
summary: DONE — three regex parsers gone, cues match beats by time in both timeline and captions, 10 new tests. Episode 05 narrates again and --variant works. Commit fbb6b508.
title: Rewire narrate, assemble and scan onto the typed loader

description:
Write down the rule the next three tasks implement, so the row and the trigger cannot drift apart. Decide and record, in the component JSDoc:

1. **Direction.** Recommended: middle-ellipsis, preserving the tail (`claude/nx-…-ce8b01`), because every branch here shares its prefix. The alternative — plain end `truncate` — is one class and zero new code, and is acceptable if you decide the label matters more than the branch. Pick one; do not ship two.
2. **Shrink budget.** Who yields first when the row is tight: the display name, the qualifier, or the branch? Recommended: the branch is capped (a `max-w-*`) and allowed to shrink, but the name keeps priority — the name is what the user picks on.
3. **Full-value carrier.** `title` on the branch element is the cheap answer and works in a popover; a `Tooltip` inside a `CommandItem` inside a `Popover` is a third layer of portal and is likely not worth it. Recommended: `title`.

Acceptance: the decision is written in `ChatCheckoutSelectorRow`'s and `ChatCheckoutSelectorTrigger`'s doc comments as a stated rule, not implied by classnames.
requirements: ["Direction, shrink priority, and full-value carrier are each decided explicitly", "The rule is recorded in component JSDoc so a later edit cannot silently diverge", "No implementation in this task"]
title: Settle the branch-truncation contract

description:
## Finding
Found while doing task 4 — **not a regression, pre-existing on `main`.** Importing the built `ide-engine.server-*.js` chunk from a production server build throws at module load:

```
Could not find @vscode/ripgrep-darwin-arm64.
Ensure optionalDependencies are installed for this platform (darwin-arm64).
```

The platform package **is** installed (`node_modules/.pnpm/@vscode+ripgrep-darwin-arm64@1.18.0` exists in both this worktree and the main checkout). The problem is resolution scope, not installation.

## Reproduction
```bash
pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:build --skip-nx-cache
cd applications/openthrottle-developer/build/server
node -e "const p=require('node:fs').readdirSync('assets').find(f=>f.startsWith('ide-engine.server-'));import('./assets/'+p).then(()=>console.log('OK')).catch(e=>console.log('FAILED:',e.message.split('\n')[0]))"
```
Verified this fails **identically with and without** the task-4 `ssr.external: ['ts-morph']` change (stashed the vite config, rebuilt, same error), so it predates that work.

Also:
```bash
cd applications/openthrottle-developer && node -e "require('@vscode/ripgrep')"   # Cannot find module
cd <repo root>                       && node -e "require('@vscode/ripgrep')"   # Cannot find module
```

## Root cause
`@vscode/ripgrep` is a dependency of `@openthrottle/openthrottle-ide`, so under pnpm's strict layout it only resolves from inside that package's own `node_modules`. Vite **bundles** `openthrottle-ide` into the SSR chunk (it is source-first, `main: ./src/index.ts`), and the bundled ripgrep shim then does a runtime lookup for its native binary relative to the bundle's location — `applications/openthrottle-developer/build/server/assets/` — where neither `@vscode/ripgrep` nor its platform package is reachable.

Because this throws at **module load**, it takes down every tier of the IDE engine, including the ts-morph tiers that never touch ripgrep.

## Impact
All `/ide` routes (`ide._index`, `ide.files`, `ide.symbol`, `ide.symbols`) fail on a production build. Dev mode works, which is why this has gone unnoticed.

## Proposed fix
Same shape as the task-4 fix: add `@vscode/ripgrep` to `applications/openthrottle-developer/package.json` dependencies and mark it `ssr.external` in the app's `vite.config.ts`, so Node resolves both it and its platform-specific optional dependency from the app's own `node_modules` at runtime. Confirm the Docker image ships the matching `linux-x64`/`linux-arm64` optional dep.

## Acceptance
The reproduction command above prints `OK`, and `listFilesVM` / `searchVM` return real results against a checkout on a production build.
title: 12. BUG: @vscode/ripgrep unresolvable from the built SSR bundle (IDE routes broken in production)

description:
`OpenThrottle/monorepo` is PUBLIC, so standard GitHub-hosted runners are free with unlimited minutes. `ubuntu-latest` is 4 vCPU / 16 GB — the same core count as `blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2204` and more RAM.

Replace `runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2204` with `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` in:
- `.github/workflows/continuous-integration.yml` — `changes`, `build`, `ci-success`, `nx-dependency-graph`
- `.github/workflows/vercel-deploy.yml` — `compute-affected`, `deploy` (currently `if: false`; convert anyway so re-enabling does not silently reintroduce paid runners)

**Measure before/after wall clock on the same commit.** Blacksmith buys speed (faster clock, sticky-disk caches), not cost, when the alternative is free. Expect some regression — the question is how much against a 30-minute ceiling on a job that currently averages 5.3 minutes.

**If the regression is unacceptable:** keep Blacksmith on `main` only (the trusted cache writer, ~26 pushes/day) and use free runners for all PR and merge_group events. That captures most of the saving while keeping the fast path where serialized correctness matters.

**Bonus:** the extra RAM (16 GB vs Blacksmith's 8 GB at 4 vCPU) may remove the reason `test` is pinned to `--parallel=1`. Do not change that here — task 8 owns it, after this lands.
requirements: ["All jobs in continuous-integration.yml on ubuntu-latest (or documented main-only Blacksmith exception)", "vercel-deploy.yml converted too, even though gated off", "Wall-clock before/after recorded on the same commit", "The 💰 comment block updated to reflect the new cost model rather than left stale"]
title: Move CI compute to free GitHub-hosted runners (public repo means $0)

description:
No presenter means the voice *is* the channel's identity — pick it deliberately and never change it mid-season.

- Evaluate options: a hosted TTS (ElevenLabs / OpenAI / Google) for quality vs local (`say`, Piper, Kokoro) for zero marginal cost and no data egress. Given OpenThrottle's self-hosting stance, a local option that sounds good is worth a real look — but do not ship a robotic voice to save pennies; this is the one place quality dominates.
- Extract the narration column from the Task 2 script format and render per-beat audio clips (per-beat, not one blob — so a re-record of one beat doesn't invalidate the take).
- Emit word-level or segment-level timings for caption generation.
- Normalize loudness to about -14 LUFS (YouTube's target) so videos don't jump in volume between uploads.
- A pronunciation lexicon: "OpenThrottle", "Ralph", "MCP", "Nx", "pgvector", "Postgres" — TTS mangles these by default, and it's audible.

Output: `pnpm ... narrate <script-slug>` producing `output/<slug>/audio/*.wav` + `timings.json`.
summary: Script markdown → generated voiceover audio + word-level timings, with a locked voice and a cost/quality decision.
title: Build the TTS narration pipeline

Why this matters: these files are loaded into agent context, so a dead skill reference is higher-risk than a stale README link.

Stale claims:
- `AGENTS.md:67` lists a `workflow-ralph` skill at `skills/workflow-ralph/SKILL.md`, but that path does not exist.
- `.agents/skills/openthrottle-stack/SKILL.md:24,32` tells readers to use a `workflow-ralph` skill and links `.agents/skills/workflow-ralph/SKILL.md`, which does not exist.

description:
Capture the trap so the next person does not spend a session rediscovering it: with `cacheControl: true`, `ApolloServerPluginCacheControl`'s `defaultMaxAge` is 0, and an operation's cache policy is the most restrictive of its fields — so ONE un-hinted field makes an entire document uncacheable, silently.

Add a short note where a reader would actually hit it: the `nestjs-graphql` cache-plugin surface (`src/config/nestjs-graphql.plugins.ts` and/or the package README), stating the rule and pointing at `GithubResolver.setCacheHint` as the reference pattern.

Keep it to a few lines. Do NOT introduce a global `defaultMaxAge` as a blanket fix — that would silently start caching operations whose authors never opted in (plans, tasks, queue stats), trading a perf bug for a staleness bug.
requirements: ["Note explains the minimum-policy rule and the 0 default", "Points at a concrete reference implementation", "Explicitly records why a global defaultMaxAge was rejected"]
title: Document the minimum-policy cache footgun

description:

```

```

Then the payoff for the "it will not scale" constraint: a **catalog rebuild**. When the UI changes, every published video silently goes stale. A scheduled job (this repo already has scheduled agent runs and BullMQ) that re-records the full catalog against `main` and flags visual diffs turns re-shooting from a manual chore into a notification. That also makes the demo flows a de-facto visual regression suite.

Scope this task to: the Nx targets, the per-stage caching, and a documented (not necessarily enabled) scheduled catalog rebuild.
summary: One command produces a finished video from a script slug; a scheduled run can rebuild the whole catalog when the UI changes.

description:
Today `WorkspaceEditorMultiSelect` maps `WORKSPACE_EDITOR_OPTIONS` straight to `{label, value}` with no availability signal, so the user picks blind and only learns about detection from the advisory row underneath.

Changes:

- Add an optional `presence?: Map<WorkspaceEditorId, EditorPresenceState> | null` prop, built by `buildEditorPresenceIndex` (task 1).
- Render each option's label with a leading status dot from the descriptor's `indicatorClassName` and append the short `label` suffix in muted text. `Unknown` renders **no** marker at all — plain label, exactly as today.
- Pass presence down: `settings.workspace._index.tsx` already has `editorPresence` in loader data and passes it to `SettingsWorkspaceEditorsForm`; build the index once there (or in the form) and hand it to the multi-select.

Hard constraint: presence must not disable, reorder, filter, or pre-select any option. Every editor stays selectable regardless of state — a containerized server reports `unknown` for everything and the picker must behave identically to today in that case.

Check what `MultiSelect` in `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn` accepts for its `options` before designing this — if its option type is `{label: string; value: string}` and cannot take a node, either extend that shared component's option type (preferred, benefits every caller) or keep the marker to a text prefix. Do not fork the component. Whichever route you take, say so in the task summary when you close it.

Tests: extend `components/__tests__/SettingsWorkspaceEditorsForm.test.tsx` (or add a multi-select test) proving an option with `NotFound` is still selectable and still submits, and that `Unknown` renders no marker.
summary: Took the PREFERRED route: extended the shared `MultiSelectOption` in @openthrottle/react-router-shadcn with two optional fields — `adornment?: React.ReactNode` and `hint?: string` — rather than forking the component or settling for a text prefix. Every caller benefits; existing callers are unaffected (both optional). The adornment renders in the option row AND the trigger tag (the picker is closed at rest, so the selection needs the marker too). Deliberately left `CommandItem value={opt.label}` alone: folding the hint into the cmdk search key would make "detected" match every option at once. `WorkspaceEditorMultiSelect` now takes `presence?: ReadonlyMap<...>` and renders the shared `WorkspaceEditorPresenceMarker` + status word per option; UNKNOWN gets neither, so an all-unknown index behaves byte-identically to no index. Index built once in the route's useMemo and handed down. 3 new MultiSelect tests + 4 picker tests, including "NOT_FOUND is still selectable and still submits" and "identical to today with no presence".
title: Show availability inside the editor picker options

**Rewritten 2026-08-30. Was: "Register the ten cron schedules via createScheduledAgentJob", BLOCKED on the prompts reaching `main`.**

Both premises are stale. The prompts are on `main`, and the schedules were **already registered out-of-band** — `scheduled_agent_jobs` holds all eleven rows, ten with a `last_run_at`. This is no longer a registration task; it is a reconciliation task, and the drift is total.

**Live rows vs. `docs/monorepo/recurring-agent-jobs.md` (read 2026-08-30):**

| Field | Documented | Live |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `driver_id` | `claude` | `cursor` — all eleven |
| `model` | `sonnet` / `fable` per job | `NULL` — all eleven |
| `cwd` | resolved from `WORKSPACE_ROOT` | `NULL` — all eleven |
| `cron_pattern` | e.g. `Job_DeadCode` = `0 14 * * 2` | e.g. `Weekly - Dead Code` = `0 9 * * 1` — **not one row matches** |
| `enabled` | all, after staged rollout | ten of eleven **disabled**; only `Daily - Issue Reporting \| @openthrottle` is live |
| `name` | `Job_DeadCode` | `Weekly - Dead Code` — prose names, no link back to the prompt file |

The model column being NULL everywhere means the whole `sonnet`-for-mechanical / `fable`-for-judgment split in the doc is **not in effect** — the fleet is running on whatever the `cursor` driver defaults to. That decision was the point of the registry table.

**Decide first, then reconcile — do not just overwrite the rows.** Someone deliberately registered these on `cursor` with different crons. Establish which artifact is authoritative before touching either:

- If the doc is right, update the eleven rows to match it and note why `cursor` was rejected.
- If the live config reflects a later decision, rewrite the doc's cadence and model tables to match reality and say what changed the call.

Either way the two must end up agreeing, and the `name` should reference its prompt file so a row is traceable to the prompt it runs.

**Then stage the rollout as originally planned:** confirm the one live job (`Daily - Issue Reporting`) files exactly one plan per run and edits nothing, then enable the rest — but **not before tasks 5 and 6 land**. Enabling ten more jobs against an empty `semantic_search` index and NULL cost columns is the failure mode task 4 exists to prevent, at ten times the volume.

**Acceptance:** the eleven rows and `docs/monorepo/recurring-agent-jobs.md` agree on driver, model, cron and name; the divergence is resolved in writing rather than silently; `cwd` resolves correctly for every job; tasks 5 and 6 are closed; all eleven enabled with at least one verified clean run each.
summary: The schedules already exist — every one of them drifts from docs/monorepo/recurring-agent-jobs.md on driver, model, cron and cwd, and ten of eleven are disabled.

description:
## Finding
Every `openthrottle-developer` route pays a **2253 KB** base shell because `root.tsx` eagerly imports `GlobalMetrics`, which pulls `recharts` into a shared client chunk.

## Paths
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/root.tsx` (imports `GlobalMetrics`)
- `packages/react-router-ui-global/src/components/GlobalMetrics.tsx`
- `packages/react-router-ui-global/src/components/GlobalMetricsChart.tsx` (`import { LineChart, … } from 'recharts'`)
- Built: `applications/openthrottle-developer/build/client/assets/src-BD*.js` (**1650.8 KB raw / 470.5 KB gzip-9**; fingerprints recharts/cmdk/sonner/vaul). Referenced by `root-*.js`.

## Measured before
```bash
pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:build
# base shell = entry+jsx+root+src-BD*+runtime+react+rollbar ≈ 2253 KB
# src-BD*.js alone: 1650.8 KB raw / 470.5 KB gzip
```
Home (`_index`) total ≈ **2266 KB**; usage/dashboard ≈ **2274 KB** — charts are paid even when the metrics panel is closed.

## Suspected cause
Eager `GlobalMetrics` → `GlobalMetricsChart` → `recharts` from the app shell. Commander (`cmdk`) and toaster/drawer libs ride the same shared chunk.

## Proposed fix
Lazy-load `GlobalMetrics` / `GlobalMetricsChart` (dynamic import when the metrics panel opens). Split recharts out of the root-shared chunk. Keep commander/toaster reviews secondary once recharts is gone.

## Expected after
- Root-shared vendor chunk containing recharts **absent** from the initial graph
- Base shell (same composition as above) **≤ 1200 KB raw** (target: remove ≥400 KB gzip from first load)

## Acceptance
Production build: `src-BD*.js` (or successor shared chunk) either drops below **800 KB raw** or no longer contains `recharts` / `LineChart`; `root-*.js` has no static import of the metrics chart module. Re-measure base shell < 1200 KB.
title: 2. Developer root: lazy-load GlobalMetrics/recharts (1650.8 KB shared)

Register in `CONVERSATION_CLI_BACKENDS` (`registry.ts` — follow its 4-step header procedure) and export from `conversation-backend/index.ts`. Flip `chatStreaming: true` on the gemini driver IN THE SAME CHANGE (the drift guard asserts registry keys ≡ chatStreaming drivers). Map only the controls Gemini really honors (permission modes via --approval-mode; likely no reasoning-effort/service-tier) — the control-honoring guard test enforces that every advertised control maps to a real flag. description:
Each CI run spins **three** billed runners: `changes` (full `fetch-depth: 0` clone of a 47 MB repo just to run one `git diff`), `build`, and `ci-success` (a runner to echo two variables and exit). Docs-only and draft PRs still pay for two of them — 6 of the last 12 runs skipped `build` yet still billed `changes` + `ci-success`.

If task 2 lands fully, this becomes free and this task is a wall-clock nicety. If Blacksmith is retained on `main`, this is a direct saving. Either way, do not undo the design: the `changes` / `ci-success` split exists for a real reason (documented at length in the workflow header — a workflow-level `paths-ignore` makes a required check hang forever as "Expected — waiting for status").

Work:
1. Pin `changes` and `ci-success` to `ubuntu-latest` **unconditionally**, even if `build` keeps Blacksmith. They are trivial jobs; there is no reason to buy fast cores for a `git diff` and an `echo`.
2. Drop `fetch-depth: 0` in `changes`. It only diffs `base.sha` against `head.sha`, both of which it already fetches explicitly — a shallow checkout plus the existing `git fetch --no-tags origin "$base"` is enough.
3. Consider replacing the `changes` job entirely with a `paths-filter` step at the head of `build` plus an early exit, keeping `ci-success` as the stable required check. Only do this if it demonstrably preserves required-check reporting on docs-only PRs — test on a scratch PR before adopting.
requirements: ["changes and ci-success on ubuntu-latest regardless of what build uses", "fetch-depth reduced in changes with the git diff still correct", "Docs-only PR verified still reporting ci-success green", "Draft PR verified still skipping build"]
title: Stop paying a runner startup for the two satellite gate jobs

description:
`detectEditorPresence` returns `trusted: false` with every editor `unknown` when the server is containerized (bridge mapping or `/.dockerenv` / `/run/.containerenv`), when the platform is not darwin, or when the probe threw. The `trusted` field is already selected by the `getEditorPresence` document but nothing in the UI reads it — the row simply vanishes, which is indistinguishable from "the query failed" and from "no editors were found".

Add, in `WorkspaceEditorPresenceHints`, a single low-key line rendered **only** when the probe returned `trusted === false` (or every entry is `Unknown`): a one-sentence note that OpenThrottle cannot inspect this machine from where the server is running, so no detection is being claimed. New copy key in `WORKSPACE_SETTINGS_COPY`.

This requires passing the full `editorPresence` object (not just `.editors`) into the hints component — widen the prop, keeping `null` meaning "query failed, render nothing at all". Note the distinction the component must now hold: `null` → render nothing; `trusted: false` → render the note, no chips; trusted with entries → render chips.

Consider surfacing `scannedAt` as a relative timestamp on the row — decide yes/no and record the reasoning in the task summary rather than leaving it silently dropped. Bias toward no if it adds noise; the probe runs per page load, so it is always fresh.

Tests: cover all three states in `WorkspaceEditorPresenceHints.test.tsx`.
summary: Prop widened from `editors` to the full `presence` object, and the component now holds three outcomes apart instead of collapsing them into one silent row: `null` → nothing (no result to characterize); `trusted: false` OR every entry UNKNOWN → the new `presenceUntrustedNote` line, no chips (`data-testid="WorkspaceEditorPresenceUntrusted"`); trusted with a real claim → chips, with individual UNKNOWN entries still filtered out. Treating all-unknown the same as explicitly-untrusted is deliberate: the server had nothing it was entitled to claim either way. scannedAt: NO — the probe runs per page load behind a short soft TTL, so a relative timestamp would read "just now" on every render, which is noise that implies staleness the user never has to reason about. It's documented in the component JSDoc and pinned by a test asserting no timestamp leaks into the markup. 6 outcome tests + the existing suite migrated.
title: Handle the untrusted / all-unknown probe honestly

description:
Verdict: **move/re-scope** — not dead, but misplaced.

1. `socket.io` — root package.json:222:6, knip-flagged unused at root. Real consumer: packages/nestjs-logging/src/gateways/nestjs-logging-websocket.gateway.ts (+ its .test.ts). `grep -rln "from 'socket.io'" applications packages` (excluding dist) returns only these two files, both inside packages/nestjs-logging. Recommend adding `socket.io` to packages/nestjs-logging/package.json `dependencies` (it's a published/source-first package per repo convention — a runtime import must not rely solely on root hoisting) and evaluating whether it can be dropped from the root package.json once every actual consumer declares it directly.
2. `bcrypt` — root package.json:140:6, knip-flagged unused at root. Real consumers: packages/nestjs-repositories/src/modules/mcp-connectors/mcp-connectors.service.ts, .../users/users.service.ts, .../service-accounts/service-accounts.service.ts (+ test files). `grep -rln "from 'bcrypt'" applications packages` (excluding dist) returns only files inside packages/nestjs-repositories. Recommend adding `bcrypt` to packages/nestjs-repositories/package.json `dependencies` for the same reason.

Not included: `@nestjs/graphql` (also knip-flagged unused at root) was checked and has 202 real import sites spread across many packages/applications — that one is correctly shared at root and is a knip false positive from checking root package.json usage in isolation, not a re-scope candidate. Most of the other ~48 root 'Unused dependencies' knip hits are the same false-positive pattern; this task only covers the two verified single-consumer cases.

Acceptance criteria: `socket.io` added to packages/nestjs-logging/package.json and `bcrypt` added to packages/nestjs-repositories/package.json (dependencies, not devDependencies — both are runtime-imported); `pnpm nx run @openthrottle/nestjs-logging:build`, `:test` and `pnpm nx run @openthrottle/nestjs-repositories:build`, `:test` stay green; confirm whether removing them from the root package.json is safe (no other direct root-level usage) before doing so, and only remove from root once each declared package genuinely no longer needs the hoisted copy.
summary: socket.io and bcrypt are declared only in the root package.json but are actually consumed exclusively by one package each (nestjs-logging and nestjs-repositories respectively) — move the declaration down instead of leaving it hoisted-and-invisible.
title: root package.json: re-scope socket.io and bcrypt to their real consumer packages

description:
Do this first — everything else builds on the resolver.

In `packages/react-router-chat/src/turn-events.ts`, replace the key-sniff-only `extractToolName` with an explicit-first resolver that reads the whole parsed metadata record, not just `metadata.toolCall`:

1. `metadata.toolName` (the canonical field task 2 adds) when it is a non-empty string.
2. `metadata.name` (claude) / `metadata.tool` (opencode) when non-empty strings.
3. `metadata.toolCall.name` when it is a non-empty string (gemini/antigravity, today's `name` bug).
4. Legacy fallback: the existing first-non-reserved-key sniff over `metadata.toolCall`, stripping a `ToolCall` suffix (cursor-agent's `{ toolCallId, readToolCall }`), skipping keys whose value is not a record so `{ name, parameters }` can never resolve to `name` again.
5. `'tool'` when nothing resolves.

Wire it through `normalizeMetadata` (so `ParsedChunkMetadata.toolName` is right for both `applyTurnToolCall` and the synthesized-result branch of `applyTurnToolResult`) and through `toolLabelFromMetadataJson`, which powers the one-line activity marker.

Keep the function pure and driver-agnostic — no per-backend branching by name.

Tests in `src/__tests__/turn-events.test.ts`: one case per real metadata shape (cursor-agent, gemini, antigravity, claude, opencode, plus the canonical `toolName`), asserting the resolved name, and one asserting the `'tool'` fallback on an empty/absent payload.

Done when `pnpm nx run react-router-chat:test` passes and no shape resolves to the literal `name`.
title: Client: explicit-first tool-name resolution in turn-events

description:
Gate commits on the same audit CI/pre-push enforce.

Steps:
1. In `.husky/pre-commit`, after the existing `lint-staged` invocation, source the shared gate from task 1 (`. "$(dirname "$0")/lib/component-shape-gate.sh"`). Run it AFTER lint-staged so any lint/prettier auto-fixes are on disk first.
2. Do NOT swallow the exit code — a non-zero from the gate must abort the commit. (lint-staged already aborts on its own failure; the gate is an additional gate after it.)
3. Keep it to the single authored command `pnpm run audit:component-shape:strict` — do not add `:shadcn:strict` here (matches CI/pre-push; see plan Decision).

Acceptance:
- A commit that introduces an R4/R5 violation is BLOCKED at commit time with the audit's failure message (verify by staging a deliberate violation in a throwaway file, attempting `git commit`, confirming it fails, then discarding).
- A clean commit succeeds and the audit adds only ~1-2s.
- `git commit` on the current green `main`/worktree still succeeds.
- Confirm the hook does not interfere with commits that touch zero component files (audit is repo-wide, so it always runs — that's expected).
title: Add the component-shape strict audit to .husky/pre-commit

description:
Verdict: **needs owner judgment**, leaning delete. Evidence: not exported from `packages/nestjs-worktrees/src/index.ts`; `grep -rl` across applications/packages/tools finds zero references outside its own `__tests__/openthrottle-client.test.ts` (which imports it 8 times). Last touched 2026-07-10.

If abandoned: delete `src/utils/openthrottle-client.ts` and `src/utils/__tests__/openthrottle-client.test.ts`; `pnpm nx run nestjs-worktrees:build` and `:test` stay green; `pnpm nx run monorepo:knip` no longer lists it. If mid-development: leave in place and note the owning plan/task in this task's description for future audits.

---

## STATUS 2026-08-20 (/ot-claude-loop): BLOCKED on owner input

Re-verified the evidence — it holds, and one additional finding strengthens the "abandoned" reading:

- Confirmed not exported from `src/index.ts` (checked the full export list).
- Confirmed the only importer is `src/utils/__tests__/openthrottle-client.test.ts`, via dynamic `await import('../openthrottle-client')` in 8 places.
- **New:** there is already a real, actively-used `openthrottle-client` elsewhere — `packages/node-client/src/openthrottle-client.ts`, which *is* exported (`node-client/src/index.ts:9`) and consumed (e.g. `node-client/src/embedding-content.ts`). The nestjs-worktrees copy is a much smaller direct-`pg` implementation (`ensureOpenThrottleReachable`, `getTasksByPlanId`, `updatePlanStatus`) that reads as superseded by the node-client one.

So the likely story is: scaffolded for worktree child jobs, then node-client became the real client and this was never wired up or removed. That is a guess about intent, not something grep can settle — which is exactly what the task said. Not deleting unilaterally.

**Question for the owner:** is this stub still wanted for the worktree/child-job path (i.e. an in-flight plan expects to grow it), or should it be deleted in favour of `@openthrottle/node-client`? Answer determines delete-vs-keep; if keep, note the owning plan id here.
summary: openthrottle-client.ts (worktree/child-job Postgres reachability + task-update client) isn't exported from the package's index.ts and has zero non-test consumers — looks scaffolded but never wired in, not obviously abandoned.

- Measured 2026-08-27 for scale expectations: 30d ≈ 208 plans, ~1,400 tasks, ~1,200 output chunks, 123 conversations, ~2,700 work artifacts.

Done when: `export --days 30` produces a snapshot directory, running it twice against the same database produces identical bytes, and the row counts per table are printed as a summary table.

description:
The script's first beat is "add the tag `needs-review` to the plan; a rule fires and a toast shows" over "I added one tag. Something just happened on its own." This is the hook, and `docs/marketing/youtube-format.md` treats the first three seconds as where retention is decided - so it cannot be quietly softened.

`queues/plan-rules/plan-rules.processor.ts` is a BullMQ worker: one job is one full evaluation pass over a plan, loading the plan owner's enabled rules, running the pure evaluator, dispatching matched actions through `ActionExecutorRegistry` and reconciling the ledger. Nothing in that path pushes anything to the browser. Adding a tag revalidates the plan; the rule's effect lands out of band.

Option A (recommended) - re-time the beat. Add the tag, hold, and let the injected task appear on the plan when the pass completes. "Something just happened on its own" is MORE true when it happens with no further click, and this teaches the real mental model instead of implying a synchronous UI reaction. Costs the flow a `waitFor` on the injected task rather than a fixed dwell, and costs the take some non-determinism.

Option B - open on the aftermath: start on a plan that already carries the tag and the injected task, then show why. Safest to record, weakest hook.

Option C - surface rule application as a live notification. Real product work well outside a screencast plan; if it is wanted, it should be its own plan and this one blocks on it.

Record the decision and the reasoning here before task 3 starts.
summary: DECISION: option A, re-timed further. No client feedback path exists at all (no toast; PlanRuleApplications commented out; InjectTaskExecutor emits no notification, so the plan page does not live-update). The flow adds the tag, dwells while the worker runs, then RE-OPENS the plan and waits on the injected task title. Verified live 2026-08-26.
title: Decide how the cold open shows a rule firing

description:
New rule in `tools/dotfiles/src/rules/`, following `route-primitive-shape.ts` and `pre-hooks-unpack.ts` — read both first; they are the working precedent for rule structure, registration in `src/index.ts`, and co-located tests in `src/__tests__/`.

**What it flags:** an array or `Set` literal containing ≥2 string literals that are all members of a registered vocabulary, outside that vocabulary's own SSOT file. That is the `new Set<string>([Cursor, Vscode])` shape that caused the bug.

**How it knows the vocabularies:** decide between (a) a static list in the rule's options, and (b) discovering `vocabulary(...)` / `vocabularyFromEnum(...)` call sites. (a) is simpler but is itself a list that can drift — the irony is worth avoiding if (b) is tractable without type information. ESLint rules here run without a type checker unless the config opts in, so verify what is available before committing to (b).

**The message must teach the fix**, not just refuse: point at `.subsetOf()` and state that a subset still has to be exhaustive. A rule that says only "don't do this" gets suppressed.

**Ship as `warn`.** `route-primitive-shape` is `warn` today and the max-lines errors during PR #443 showed how a hard error mid-task forces unrelated churn. Promote to `error` in a follow-up once the pilot vocabularies are clean.

Mandatory: false-positive tests. A legitimate two-element array of unrelated strings must not trigger, and neither must the SSOT declaration itself. Include the real call sites from tasks 3 and 4 as fixtures.

Validate: `pnpm nx run @tools/dotfiles:test,lint,typecheck`, then `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:lint` to confirm no new warnings on already-migrated code.
summary: Rejected both offered designs — a static vocabulary list would drift exactly like the lists it polices, and discovery needs cross-file/type info that ESLint here does not have (verified). The rule instead matches the defect's SYNTAX, so it needs no registry: a literal Set, or a module-scope SCREAMING_SNAKE const array, containing ≥2 non-computed member accesses off one object. Two findings: (1) flagging bare-string Sets by default fired on the rule's own factory-name lookup table, so bare strings moved behind includeStringLiteralArrays (off by default) with a regression test — the repo-wide survey is the audit script's job; (2) the SSOT check is an import check rather than a generic AST walk, which needed a banned `as` cast. Messages name .subsetOf() and state that subsets must still be exhaustive. Shipped warn repo-wide. 20 test cases (6 invalid, 14 valid) including every migrated call site from tasks 3/4/4.5 asserted at the stricter option. Zero hits on migrated code; found ONE true positive outside the pilots — data.rollout-kinds.ts hand-lists four generated RolloutFlagKind members plus its own guard, a fourth instance of this plan's bug, left for the backlog per the plan's scope.
title: Add the openthrottle/no-adhoc-vocabulary ESLint rule

description:
In a worktree created with `pnpm run worktree:new <name>`, `node_modules/.bin/workflow-ralph` (and `workflow-lighthouse`, `workflow-link-merge`) do not exist. In the primary checkout they do.

**Re-verified 2026-08-30 — the root cause is structurally unchanged, though the file moved.** Provisioning was rewritten in TypeScript since this was filed (`scripts/setup_worktree.sh` is now a thin tsx shim over `scripts/setup_worktree.ts`), but the ordering defect survived the rewrite verbatim: `scripts/setup_worktree.ts` runs `step('pnpm', ['install'])` at **line 250** and `step('pnpm', ['build'])` at **line 253**. `tools/workflows/package.json` still declares its three bins as `./dist/src/bin/*.js`, so at link time the targets still do not exist and pnpm still skips creating the shims.

Re-running `pnpm install` afterwards does not repair it — pnpm reports "Already up to date" and exits, and `pnpm install --force` does the same (both verified on a fresh worktree; the package's `dist/src/bin/*.js` were present and executable, timestamped one minute *after* the install).

Effect: `pnpm exec workflow-ralph …` fails with `Command "workflow-ralph" not found` in any fresh worktree, so every documented `pnpm exec workflow-*` invocation is broken there until someone rebuilds and reinstalls. Worked around during the smoke runs by invoking `node tools/workflows/dist/src/bin/ralph.js` directly.

Fix at the root — either order the install after the build, or add an explicit relink step to the provisioning script. Do not paper over it by rewriting the docs to call `node dist/...`.

**One scoping note before starting:** `@tools/workflows` now carries a `deprecated` field in its `package.json` directing new code to `@openthrottle/nestjs-agentic-workflow`, and describes `workflow-ralph` as "a thin local CLI shim", with `workflow-link-merge` and `workflow-lighthouse` "staying here until relocated". Check whether these three bins are being relocated before investing in the fix — if they are moving to a package that builds differently, fix the install/build ordering anyway (it is a general provisioning defect that will bite the next `dist`-bin package) but do not spend effort on `@tools/workflows`-specific plumbing that is about to be deleted.

Acceptance: a worktree created fresh via `pnpm run worktree:new` has working `workflow-ralph`, `workflow-lighthouse`, and `workflow-link-merge` shims in `node_modules/.bin`; `pnpm exec workflow-ralph --help` succeeds there with no manual repair.
summary: Still live: scripts/setup_worktree.ts installs (line 250) before building (line 253), so pnpm skips the @tools/workflows bin symlinks and a later install reports "Already up to date" without repairing them.
title: Fresh worktrees cannot run any documented `pnpm exec workflow-*` command

description:
**This is the highest-value task — it is a deterministic break that shard assignment has been masking, and it accounted for 3 of the 7 red runs including two on `main`.**

In `packages/nestjs-mcp-developer/package.json` the package name is `@openthrottle/nestjs-openthrottle-mcp`, and:

- `main` / `module` / `types` → `./src/index.ts`
- `exports['.']` → `./dist/src/index.js` + `./dist/src/index.d.ts`
- `exports['./*']` → `./dist/*.js`

`dist` is gitignored (`.gitignore:14`), and Vite/Vitest resolve through `exports`, ignoring `main`. Its own suite `src/nestjs-mcp-developer.service.test.ts:5` does `import * as packageEntry from '@openthrottle/nestjs-openthrottle-mcp'` (plus a named import on line 13), so collection fails with `Failed to resolve entry for package ...` unless `dist/` already exists on the runner.

### Fix

Rewrite the dev-time `exports` block to mirror `main` (source-first), leaving `publishConfig` untouched — it already rewrites `exports`, `main`, `module`, and `types` to the built `./src/index.js` shape at publish time, so the published artifact is unaffected:

```json
"exports": {
  ".": { "types": "./src/index.ts", "import": "./src/index.ts", "require": "./src/index.ts" },
  "./*": { "types": "./*.ts", "import": "./*.ts", "require": "./*.ts" }
}
```

Do **not** solve this by rewriting the test to a relative `./index` import: the test exists to assert the *package entry* contract, and a relative import silently stops testing that.

Do **not** solve it by adding a self `build` to the `test` targetDefault in `nx.json` — that would add a tsc build to every project's test run workspace-wide to work around two packages.

### Verify


description:
Second confirmed production instance of this plan's failure mode, and the one that justifies the raw package. Sequenced after the driver-id migration (task 4) because it consumes that vocabulary.

**The bug (already patched, cause still open).** `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/settings/data/agent-clis.data.ts` holds `AGENT_CLI_CATALOG`, a hand-maintained mirror of the drivers registry. `mergeAgentCliStatuses` iterates the **catalog**, not the discovery result, so any CLI absent from the catalog is dropped even when the server reports it installed. Antigravity shipped in `ALL_DRIVERS` (PR #440) but was never added here, so `/settings/agents` hid it while `discoverAgentClis` was returning `{backend: 'antigravity', enabled: true, version: '1.1.21'}`. Patched by hand in PR #443; nothing stops the next driver from repeating it.

The file's own docstring is the tell: *"Keep this list in sync with the registry."* A comment doing a type's job.

**Why this is the raw package's reason to exist.** The docstring also records the real constraint: `@openthrottle/openthrottle-drivers` *cannot* be imported into the browser bundle — it pulls node-only modules. So "just import `ALL_DRIVERS`" is not available, and that is precisely the gap `@openthrottle/nodejs-parts-department` fills: a dependency-free package both the browser bundle and the node-side driver registry can share. Task 1's design must account for this; a vocabulary package that cannot be imported client-side would not have prevented this bug.

**What is genuinely duplicated vs genuinely local** — establish before refactoring:
- `backend` — pure duplication of `DRIVER_IDS`.
- `installUrl` — pure duplication; every catalog URL is byte-identical to that driver's own `install.url` (gemini is the lone exception: the driver has no install url and the catalog points at a docs page — confirm which is correct rather than assuming).
- `label` — genuinely different and must stay: the catalog shows `'Claude Code'`, the driver's label is `'claude-code'` (the binary-ish name). This is the `.labelled()` case, not a duplication to delete.

**Cheap tripwire available immediately** — evaluate before building anything larger: the browser-bundle constraint does **not** apply to tests, which run in node. A test that imports `ALL_DRIVERS` and asserts the catalog covers every driver id would have caught this. Two known snags to check first: the developer app does not currently depend on the drivers package, and that package is source-first using explicit `.ts` import extensions, which may not resolve under the app's Vite/vitest config. If it resolves cleanly, ship this test on its own — it is worth far more than its cost and does not wait on the rest of the plan. If it fights the resolver, fold the check into the task-6 audit script (which already runs in node) and say so.

Validate: `openthrottle-developer:typecheck`, `:lint`, `:test` sequentially; confirm `/settings/agents` lists all seven CLIs against a running server.
summary: Two gates, because each catches what the other cannot. Compile time: AGENT_CLI_CATALOG is now AGENT_CLI_BACKENDS.labelled() keyed by backend, so a backend cannot exist without a label + install link; mergeAgentCliStatuses iterates the vocabulary, not the catalog array — that iteration was the actual cause of the dropped row. Test time: the drivers package DOES resolve in the app's vitest (verified with a probe), so it went in as a devDependency and a new parity suite asserts the browser-safe mirror equals ALL_DRIVERS in both directions, per-driver install urls included. Gemini confirmed from the driver descriptor (method:'npm', no url) — its docs link is correct and is encoded as a named exception. Gate verified by re-creating the antigravity bug: 4 of 5 assertions fail. Also strengthened settings.agents.test.tsx, whose comment said "all five catalog CLIs" (there are seven) — it now iterates ALL_DRIVERS. Did NOT live-verify against a running server; used render-level assertions over the real registry instead. typecheck/lint/test green, 705 files.
title: Make the /settings/agents CLI catalog derive from the drivers registry

description:
## Decision: option A — typeset the shell in the recording browser

Rejected B (reshoot around `/settings/mcp`): the short's subject is wiring an agent CLI so it can write plans. `/settings/mcp` is the dashboard's connector catalogue — a different feature. Reshooting there does not make the short cheaper, it makes it a different short, and 06/07 already need the dashboard.

Rejected C (real terminal capture): `spike/README.md` settled Playwright over screen capture, and nothing in this script is evidence against that decision. It would also put the operator's real shell — scrollback included — in frame, which is the exact failure the fixture-only database exists to prevent.

## How option A is built

Two new verbs in `runner/types.ts` + `runner/actions.ts`, both of which read as on-screen actions in a script's action column:

- `stage(name)` — put a typeset surface on camera via `page.setContent`. Surfaces are declared on the flow (`DemoFlow.surfaces`, name → HTML) and reach `runStep` through `ActionContext.surfaces`. NOT a `navigate`: `navigate` waits on `#ot-env` for app hydration, which a static surface does not have and should not fake.
- `reveal(selector)` — un-hide an element staged with `data-demo-hidden`. This is what makes "the printed block appears", "the paste lands" and "the agent replies" single steps instead of four near-duplicate surface variants. Hidden elements are `display:none`, so they are absent from `innerText` and therefore absent from the beat's leak-scan dump until the beat that actually puts them on screen — which is the correct semantics, not a workaround.

`installCursor` is self-contained (it injects its own stylesheet and SVG), so the synthetic cursor, the click ring and `__demo_highlight` all work on a staged surface with no change.

## The output on camera is the real command's real output

`scripts/setup_mcp-instructions.ts` already exports `renderInstructions(root, status)` as a pure function, precisely so it can be asserted without parsing colorised stdout. The terminal surface calls it. So the block the viewer is told to copy is generated by the same code path `pnpm run setup:mcp-instructions` runs — it cannot drift from the product the way a hand-pasted mock would — while `root` and `status` stay under the recording's control. chalk emits no ANSI when stdout is not a TTY, so the string arrives as plain text.

This is what makes A strictly better than a mock, and it is what resolves tasks 2 and 3 without touching the script's behaviour.

## Script correction the decision forces

Beat 0:15 as written ("Editor opens `.mcp.json`; paste the block; save") describes a surface the command does not produce. `setup_mcp-instructions.ts` prints, for Claude Code, a single `claude mcp add-json … --scope user` command line; the paste-into-a-file branch is Cursor's `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. The short's title, title card and narration are all Claude Code, so the beat follows the Claude Code branch: copy the printed command, run it in the same terminal. The editor leaves the short entirely.

That also removes an editor pane from the frame, which is the surface most likely to carry a path — a welcome side effect given task 2.
summary: DECIDED: option A. Typeset surfaces via page.setContent + two new verbs (stage, reveal); terminal output comes from the real renderInstructions() export, not a mock.
title: Decide how a terminal-and-editor short is captured

description:
Research and recommendation only — no implementation, no scaffolding.

Today distribution is three separate mechanisms: skills fanned out by `/skill-sync`, committed `.cjs` hook bundles, and hand-maintained `.claude/settings.json` hook entries. There is no `.claude-plugin/` anywhere in the repo. A vendor plugin could package skills + hooks + MCP server config as one installable unit.

Answer:

1. **What a Claude Code plugin can actually carry** at the current version — skills, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, agents, settings — and the manifest/marketplace mechanics. Verify against current docs, not memory.
2. **Cursor and the other vendors**: is there an equivalent packaging unit, or does the fan-out stay the only option there?
3. **Reconcile with what exists**: `/skill-sync` and the `skills/` → `.agents/skills` inverted model, and the foreign-workspace skill injection work (OT `d3a30314`). Does a plugin replace, wrap, or duplicate them? Duplicating them is a NO-GO.
4. **Zero-dependency question**: can a plugin-delivered hook keep the self-contained-`.cjs` guarantee, or does plugin packaging imply a runtime install step?
5. **Downstream story**: what a foreign repo does to get OT's hooks — today vs under a plugin — and whether OT-specific config (server URL, auth token, plan binding) can travel safely without leaking secrets.

Deliverable: a written GO/NO-GO with the migration sketch if GO, and a follow-up OT plan created for the implementation (do not implement here).
summary: Evaluate packaging OT skills+hooks+MCP as a Claude Code plugin (and the Cursor analogue) against today's skill-sync fan-out; produce GO/NO-GO plus a follow-up plan.
title: Spike: ship OT hooks + skills + MCP as a vendor plugin (GO/NO-GO)

description:
Write a short design decision (append to plan output / a docs/ note per repo convention — NOT a plan markdown file) resolving the two open design questions before implementation.

1. **Same-machine signal.** Decide how the server knows the browser is on the same host so the native dialog can appear on the user's screen. Note user-cancel exit codes (must map to a clean no-op, not an error).

Deliverable: the decided predicate + per-OS command table + cancel/timeout handling, referenced by the server tasks below.

description:
## Finding
`docsManifest-*.js` is a **141.8 KB** client chunk in the developer shared graph (referenced widely including from the large `src-BD*` chunk consumers). It is static docs metadata riding along common navigations.

## Paths
- Built: `applications/openthrottle-developer/build/client/assets/docsManifest-*.js` (141.8 KB)
- Likely source under developer docs routing / manifest generation used by `/docs`

## Measured before
```bash
pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:build
# docsManifest-*.js ≈ 141.8 KB raw
```
Present in the dependency set reachable from many routes via the shared chunk graph.

## Suspected cause
Docs manifest imported from a shared module (shell, search, or commander) instead of only the `/docs` route.

## Proposed fix
Confine the manifest import to `docs.*` routes (dynamic import). Ensure commander/search does not statically import the full manifest.

## Expected after
`docsManifest-*.js` only in the `/docs` route graph; non-docs navigations do not download it. Chunk ≤ 141.8 KB still OK if route-scoped; **0 bytes** on home/plan/schedule graphs.

## Acceptance
Production build: `docsManifest-*.js` is not a dependency of `root-*.js`, `_index-*.js`, or `plans.*` / `schedule.*` chunks (only `docs*` routes).
title: 10. Developer: route-scope docsManifest (141.8 KB shared)

description:
`/ot-claude-loop` asks the model to `append_plan_output` as it goes; nothing enforces it, so runs go dark. Make the harness do it.

- On `PostToolUse` for `mcp__openthrottle-mcp__update_task`, when a task transitions (`IN_PROGRESS`, `COMPLETED`, `BLOCKED`, `SKIPPED`) and a plan is bound to the session, append a structured progress chunk to `plan_output_stream` with the transition, the task title/id, branch, and elapsed time since the `IN_PROGRESS` stamp — reusing the existing start-correlation pattern in `src/data/starts.ts` for the timing.
- On `Stop` / `SessionEnd`, if the session touched a bound plan but emitted **no** narration for the task it worked, append a synthesized summary chunk so the stream is never empty for work that happened.
- Deduplicate against model-authored output: do not double-narrate when the model already appended for that `taskId` since the transition. Prefer the model's chunk; the hook is the floor, not a replacement.
- Attribute every chunk to the correct `taskId` (plan-level only for genuinely plan-scoped notes), and label hook-authored chunks distinguishably so a reader can tell mechanical narration from the model's.
- Buffer + drain like every other event; a dead server must never lose the chunk or stall the turn.
- Tests: transition → chunk, dedupe against a model-authored chunk, empty-session synthesis, no plan bound → no-op.
summary: Hook-authored append_plan_output on task transitions and at session end, deduped against model-authored narration.
title: Force plan-output narration from hooks instead of trusting prose

description:
Rank 3 — unbounded growth (soft-delete without hard purge).

**Tables:** `agent_conversations`, `agent_conversation_messages` (`051_create_agent_conversations_tables.sql`, `081_add_deleted_status_to_agent_conversations.sql`).
**Entities:** `agent-conversation.entity.ts`, `agent-conversation-message.entity.ts`.

**Evidence:** Audited DB: 49 active / 62 deleted conversations; 218 of 352 messages hang off `status='deleted'` rows; messages table ~944kB and growing with chat. README still describes archive-only v1; migration 081 says a later purge job may hard-delete — none exists. Not in `DATA_RETENTION_POLICIES`.

**Growth driver:** Every chat turn + soft-delete keeps rows forever.

**Proposed policy:** Add a data-retention policy: hard-delete conversations with `status='deleted'` older than N days (e.g. 30–90) by `updated_at`; rely on `ON DELETE CASCADE` for messages. Keep `archived` out of scope unless product agrees. Dry-run via existing `DATA_RETENTION_ENFORCE` gate. Document in `databases/README.md` § Data retention.

**Acceptance:** Policy registered; dry-run counts deleted-status rows; enforce deletes in batches; no orphans; README updated; comment gate unaffected/passes.
title: Retention/purge for soft-deleted agent_conversations + messages

Decide explicitly — keep a capped-divergence re-sync contract, or declare these files fully owned and drop the registry contract. This bounds how far conform can go.

description:
Two more vocabularies, chosen to exercise the parts the editor migration does not.

**Driver ids** — `packages/openthrottle-drivers/src/registry/index.ts`. `DRIVER_IDS` is already a clean `as const` SSOT with a derived guard, so the interesting defect is downstream: `DriverRegistry = Partial<Record<DriverId, AgentDriver>>`. `Partial` means adding an id never forces registering a driver module. The file comments say the registry is assembled incrementally to avoid import cycles — so confirm whether `Partial` is load-bearing for that, or merely convenient. If it is genuinely needed, add a runtime completeness assertion at registry assembly so a missing driver fails fast at boot instead of surfacing as `UnknownDriverError` later. Do not silently tighten to a full `Record` without checking the cycle constraint the comment describes.

**Terminal task statuses** — `packages/nestjs-repositories/src/modules/tag-action-rules/rule-applications.service.ts`:

```ts
const TERMINAL_TASK_STATUSES = ['CANCELED', 'COMPLETED', 'SKIPPED'] as const;
```

This is the canonical `subsetOf` case: add a task status and it is silently non-terminal. Convert to an exhaustive `Record<TaskStatus, boolean>` so a new status must be classified. Find the task-status union first — it may live in the GraphQL schema, the entity, or both; if there are already several representations, say so in the plan output rather than quietly picking one, since that is its own instance of this plan's problem.

Also convert `PROMPT_ROLES` in `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/conversation-stream/conversation-stream.resolver.ts` — a deliberate subset excluding the `tool` role. It must keep excluding `tool`; the point is that the exclusion becomes explicit and a new role forces a decision. Preserve the existing comment's intent.

Validate: tests for every touched project, run sequentially.
summary: Drivers: confirmed Partial IS load-bearing (registry/index.ts cannot import driver modules without closing a cycle), so instead of tightening the type or adding the proposed runtime boot assertion, the completeness gate moved up to drivers/index.ts where imports are legal — DRIVER_REGISTRY is now DRIVERS.labelled<AgentDriver>(...) and ALL_DRIVERS derives from it, making a missing driver a compile error rather than a boot failure. Also closes an unnamed gap: ALL_DRIVERS was a second hand-listed array. Task statuses: flagged that PLAN_STATUS (8) and TASK_STATUS (7, no QUEUED) both exist and are legitimately different; picked TASK_STATUS since the query updates Task (the plan body's example sketched the wrong 8-member set). TERMINAL_TASK_STATUSES and PROMPT_ROLES both converted to .subsetOf(); tool stays excluded as an explicit false. All three tripwires verified firing with temporary members, then reverted. 8 validation targets green.
title: Migrate driver ids and the terminal-task-status subset
