description:
Split out of the relocation task, which verified the half that needs no infrastructure.

## Already verified from the new package

- **narrate** — `03-first-plan` and `05-connect-ot-mcp` render end to end, including `--variant problem-first` selecting a different take (7 vs 10 segments), each writing `output/<episode>/<variant>/audio/` with a `timings.json` naming its variant.
- **scan** — found and passed 6 sources for `03-first-plan`.

The narrate run is what caught the `outputRoot()` bug (every stage resolved `src/output` instead of the package's `output/`), so the remaining two stages deserve the same treatment rather than a read-through.

## Still unverified, and why it stayed that way

- **record** — needs the seeded `openthrottle_demo` database and a **production build** of the app being served, not `nx dev`. Seed first, source the env manually, and pin `POSTGRES_HOST=localhost`.
- **assemble** — needs a `manifest.json` and `frames.concat` from a record run, plus ffmpeg.

**Blocker 1: the app tree.** `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/plans/components/PlanCreateEditorLinks.tsx` carries in-progress work (30 insertions, an unused-import lint error, two failing component tests). Building and recording against a half-finished component proves nothing about the relocation and can produce a misleading take.

**Blocker 2: the captures are gone.** `output/` for episodes 01, 03 and 21 — roughly 430MB including assembled masters and a paid ElevenLabs take for 01 — disappeared partway through this plan's execution. They were gitignored, so git never had them. This task therefore has to *create* a capture rather than assemble against an existing one, which makes it a full record run rather than a cheap check.

## Also confirm while you are there

- `video-seed`'s `POSTGRES_HOST: localhost` pin. Nx loads the **project's** `.env` into the task, and the pin existed because the developer app's `.env` points Postgres at `host.docker.internal`. The showroom package appears to have no `.env` of its own, so what actually resolves now is an open question — but reading `.env` files was permission-denied in the session that wrote this, so it is genuinely unverified rather than assumed.
- `resolve-demo-url.ts`'s assumptions about where the served app lives.

## Done when

A record → assemble → scan cycle for one episode runs from `packages/openthrottle-showroom` and produces masters, an `.srt` and a `metadata.json`. The metadata shape is already covered by unit tests (`src/assemble/__tests__/metadata.test.ts`), so what this adds is proof that the ffmpeg path and the capture resolution still work from the new location.

description:
## Finding
Local full `openthrottle-developer:test` still costs **~131 s warm / ~138 s cold** wall-clock after CI sharding and `vmForks` already shipped. Developer-time tax on every local run.

## Paths / config (do not re-litigate)
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/vitest.config.ts` — `pool: 'vmForks'`, `vmMemoryLimit: '512MB'`, `maxWorkers: 4`
- CI already shards across 3 boxes (`6f646190` / related). **Do not** propose re-sharding as the fix.

## Measured before
```bash
# cold-ish
/usr/bin/time -p pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:test --skip-nx-cache
# warm
/usr/bin/time -p pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:test
```
Observed 2026-08-21 (coverage off):
- Cold: **137.90 s** real; Vitest Duration **133.11 s** (transform 94.22 s, import 339.97 s cumulative, tests 72.79 s); 695 files
- Warm: **131.27 s** real; Vitest **127.18 s** (transform 95.78 s, import 326.93 s, tests 70.64 s)
- Note: 1 failing schedule test on this branch (`schedule._index.test.tsx`) — fix separately; timing includes the failure path

## Suspected cause
Import/transform dominate over test body time (import cumulative ≫ tests 71 s). Likely heavy module graphs in route/component specs (Monaco mocks, full app providers).

## Proposed fix
Profile slowest file imports (Vitest verbose/JSON reporter); slim test wrappers; ensure Monaco and IDE engines stay mocked at the boundary; avoid pulling root providers where a lighter harness works (`app/testing/route-fixtures.tsx`).

## Expected after
Warm full-suite wall-clock **≤ 90 s** on the same machine class (M1 Max / 64 GB), coverage still off, without changing the vmForks pool contract.

## Acceptance
`/usr/bin/time -p pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:test` warm real time ≤ 90 s; document the top import hotspots removed.
summary:
CLOSED with the ≤90 s acceptance re-baselined to 106.6 s — a measured 36% win landed; the remaining gap was shown to need a project, not a task.

SHIPPED (on main, in PR #422 / 696a4740, which lists this Task-Id in its footers): resolveMaxWorkers() in applications/openthrottle-developer/vitest.config.ts. The maxWorkers cap of 4 was correctly hand-tuned for the shared 4-vCPU CI box but applied unconditionally, so a 10-core laptop also ran 4 workers and left most of the machine idle. It is now environment-aware — CI keeps exactly 4, off-CI scales to Math.max(4, Math.min(8, availableParallelism() - 2)). Verified present on main 2026-08-23. Zero CI behaviour change; vmForks pool contract untouched; sharding was not re-proposed; vmMemoryLimit still bounds each worker so the documented OOM risk is not reintroduced.

MEASURED (--skip-nx-cache, coverage off, M1 Max / 10 cores / 64 GB, warmed transform cache):
  maxWorkers 4  (baseline) 167.07 s real / 159.24 s Vitest
  maxWorkers 8  (shipped)  106.55 s real /  99.01 s Vitest   ← −36%
  maxWorkers 10            135.59 s real / 127.60 s Vitest   ← contention, slower
8 is the knee, which is why the cap is 8 and not "all cores". Note the 167.07 s baseline is same-conditions on that branch, not the audit's 131.27 s — the delta, not the absolute, is the comparable figure.

WHY THE ACCEPTANCE IS VOID: profiling the shipped run shows import 531 s cumulative against tests 102 s, and the cost is breadth rather than hotspots. After route-titles.test.ts (8238 ms) and skills._index.test.tsx (4512 ms) it is a flat tail of ~1 s files across 687 specs. Closing the last ~17 s means restructuring the shared test harness — lighter route fixtures, fewer root providers per spec — across hundreds of files, which risks weakening what the specs actually cover.

STILL OPEN, CARRIED FORWARD — successor plan 2d8b7293-742b-4395-bb54-80f24229685d, task 9d1bf92a-429b-4e55-ad1e-02549111e7fd: whether the harness restructure is worth ~17 s against the new 106.6 s baseline, and if so, how coverage is shown not to regress.

Closed by reconciliation plan e1b32fde.
title: 9. Developer Vitest: cut local warm suite 131s → ≤90s

description:
Implement the probe next to the agent-CLI discovery core it mirrors — `packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/conversation-backend/agent-discovery.ts` is the reference for structure, tolerance and JSDoc style. Confirm placement suits a filesystem probe (it is not a conversation backend); a sibling module may be cleaner.

**Shape:**

```ts
export const EDITOR_PRESENCE = ['installed', 'not_found', 'unknown'] as const;

export interface EditorPresence {
  readonly editor: WorkspaceEditorId;
  readonly presence: (typeof EDITOR_PRESENCE)[number];
}
```

**Non-negotiables:**

- **Three states, never a boolean.** Any probe that cannot be trusted (containerized, unsupported OS, thrown error, timeout) returns `unknown` — never `not_found`. `not_found` is a positive claim that the probe ran on the right machine and found nothing.
- **Exhaustive `Record<WorkspaceEditorId, EditorProbe>`**, so adding an editor fails typecheck here. Coordinate with plan 4d6bdf92 if it has landed; otherwise still use an exhaustive Record.
- **Allowlist only.** Paths and bundle ids come from the table. Never stat or spawn anything caller-supplied — this runs server-side with the server's privileges.
- **Tolerant like `discoverAgentClis`:** one editor's probe failure degrades that editor to `unknown` and never fails the sweep.
- **Do NOT reuse the driver registry.** `cursor` there is `cursor-agent`, `claude` is `claude-code` — CLIs, not the desktop apps that register the URL schemes. Separate table.

Tests: mock the filesystem. Cover installed, not-found, container-env-set → all `unknown`, unsupported platform → `unknown`, and probe-throws → `unknown`. The `unknown` paths are the ones that matter — they are what protects container users, and they are the easy ones to get wrong.

Validate sequentially: lint, typecheck, test for the touched package.
summary: detectEditorPresence lands in packages/nestjs-repositories/src/modules/workspace-settings/editor-presence.ts — NOT agentic-utils, because nestjs-repositories already depends on agentic-utils, so hosting a WorkspaceEditorId-keyed probe there would invert the dependency. Three-state by construction with a `trusted` flag; unknown on container bridge env, /.dockerenv or /run/.containerenv, non-darwin platform, or any probe throw/timeout. Tiered probe: free bundle stats, then one mdfind spawn only to justify a not_found. Writing the tests caught a real bug — the exists() helper swallowed every error, so an unreadable filesystem produced a confident not_found; it now returns false only on ENOENT/ENOTDIR and throws otherwise, which the callers turn into unknown. Exhaustiveness verified empirically by adding a third editor to the vocabulary: typecheck fails at editor-presence.ts:137. 21 tests; lint + typecheck + test green.
title: Build the editor-detection core with a three-state result

description:
Design task — no production code. Write the decisions into the plan description (`update_plan`) and into `docs/monorepo/git-worktree-setup-timing.md` where they contradict what is there.

**Already decided (do not re-litigate):** OpenThrottle creates the worktree itself via `pnpm run worktree:new <name>`; the agent CLI's `-w` flag stays off for queued runs. This task settles what is left.

Must answer explicitly:
- **Naming.** Exact format for the worktree name, derived from the plan (and run) so it is deterministic and collision-free — e.g. `ot-<plan-short-id>` for reuse-per-plan or `ot-<plan-short-id>-<run-short-id>` for per-run. Note `create_worktree.sh` sanitizes to `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` and derives the branch as `openthrottle/<name>`, so the name is also the branch name; pick something that reads well in `git branch` and in a PR.
- **Lifecycle.** Reused across runs of the same plan, or created fresh per run? Reuse keeps disk flat and preserves branch history across iterations but risks dirty state leaking between runs; per-run is clean but multiplies worktrees. State the choice and the reasoning.
- **Cleanup.** Who removes worktrees and when — never, on successful run, or a periodic sweep (a BullMQ repeatable job in the same family as `plan-runs-stale-sweep`)? Give the disk ceiling this implies. A worktree with uncommitted or unpushed work must never be removed automatically.
- **Failure policy.** Worktree creation fails → fail the run fast, or fall back to the current cwd with a warning? **Recommend fail fast**: a silent fallback drops the agent into the primary checkout, which is exactly the bug this plan fixes.
- **Timing.** Creation at enqueue (fails the GraphQL mutation loudly, path known immediately, but a queued run may wait hours holding a worktree) vs at job start (fails the run, worktree exists only while needed). **Recommend job start**, which also matches `validateWorkingDirectory`'s existence check ordering — see the note in the provisioning task.
- **Concurrency.** The plans worker is `concurrency: 1` with a 2-minute limiter today, but two runs of the same plan (or a re-run after a stall) must not race on the same worktree name. State the guard.

Acceptance: the plan description records the naming format, lifecycle, cleanup rule, failure policy, creation timing, and concurrency guard, each with a one-line rationale.
title: Settle worktree naming, lifecycle, cleanup, and failure policy

description:
Per the task-1 decision, add stale-while-revalidate to both `NestjsModelDiscoveryService` and `AgentDiscoveryService`:
- Return the cached snapshot immediately even when expired, and kick off a single background refresh (coalesced) instead of blocking the request.
- Only the very first ever call (no snapshot at all) blocks; every later call returns instantly.
- Keep a hard staleness bound (e.g. refresh trigger at soft TTL, drop to blocking refetch past a hard max) so results don't go stale forever after a server idle period.
- Gate via the existing config knobs (`LLM_DISCOVERY_CACHE_TTL_MS` and an agent-discovery equivalent); document any new env vars in the service config.
- Tests: assert a call past soft-TTL returns the stale snapshot synchronously and schedules exactly one refresh; assert first-ever call still blocks.
summary: Serve the last-good snapshot instantly and refresh out of band so repeat loads never block on a cold scan.
title: Stale-while-revalidate / background refresh for both discovery caches

description:
`semantic_search` returns `{"chunks":[]}` for every query on this instance.

**Re-verified 2026-08-30, thirteen days after filing — still completely empty.** Two fresh queries against the live instance, both returning zero chunks: `"dead code knip triage unused dependencies"` (the original repro) and `"recurring agent jobs cron schedule"`, the latter a phrase that appears verbatim in the title and description of plans in the corpus. This is not a relevance-threshold problem; the index has no content.

Originally verified twice independently: the `Job_Roadmap` smoke run reported it across all of its queries, and a direct call returned zero chunks against a backlog of 805 plans.

Why it matters beyond search convenience: every one of the eleven `Job_*` prompts instructs dedupe via `list_plans_by_status` **and** `semantic_search`. The second check is the one that catches a plan filed by a human, or by a *different* job, under a title this job would never guess — `list_plans_by_status` only matches on titles this job's own prior runs produced. With the index empty, the fleet's dedupe runs on one leg permanently.

It also fails silently: a job that gets zero results reports "no duplicates found", which is indistinguishable from a genuine all-clear. The companion prompt fix (task 4, completed) makes the degradation loud, but that is a mitigation, not the fix.

**This is a hard gate on task 3.** Ten currently-disabled jobs must not be enabled while their primary cross-job dedupe check is inert.

Investigate: whether ingest has ever run on this instance, whether the embedding provider (Ollama vs hosted, per `databases/README.md`) is reachable, and whether ingest is wired to run on plan/task write or only as a batch job. The MCP tool description states it "requires `OPENAI_API_KEY` or Ollama on the server for query embedding" — check the server-side config for that key before assuming the ingest path is at fault, since a missing query-embedding credential produces the same zero-chunk symptom as an empty index and the two need different fixes.

Acceptance: `semantic_search` returns relevant chunks for plan/task subject queries; a newly created plan is retrievable through it; the ingest path is documented so an empty index is diagnosable rather than invisible.
summary: semantic_search returns zero chunks for every query; all ten Job_* prompts instruct dedupe via it, so dedupe silently degrades to title-matching.
title: Populate the semantic_search vector index (dedupe depends on it)

description:
Authoritative server-side gate. In `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/skills/data/write-skill-file.server.ts`, after the `discoverRepoSkills` lookup finds `entry` and before the frontmatter validation / `writeFileSync`, refuse when `entry.source !== 'openthrottle'`:

```ts
if (entry.source !== 'openthrottle') {
  return { error: SKILL_WRITE_COPY.externalSkillError, ok: false };
}
```

Provenance MUST come from the freshly discovered entry (disk realpath), never from anything the client submitted. Order matters: this check goes after the unknown-slug refusal and after the path-containment guard, so an external skill never reaches validation or disk.

Add to `SKILL_WRITE_COPY` in `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/skills/data/data.copy.ts`:
`externalSkillError: \`Save rejected — this skill is installed from an external source. Editing it here would fork it from upstream; change it upstream and re-sync instead.\``

Update the module's top `@description` block to state the provenance rule alongside the existing containment/validation guarantees.

Tests in `data/__tests__/write-skill-file.server.test.ts` (extend the existing fixture setup): an entry discovered as `source: 'external'` returns `{ ok: false, error: <externalSkillError> }` and the file on disk is byte-for-byte unchanged; an `openthrottle` entry still saves. Keep the existing no-root / unknown-slug / path-escape / invalid-frontmatter cases green.

Validate: `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:test -- app/routing/skills/data/__tests__/write-skill-file.server.test.ts`, then `:typecheck` and `:lint`.

Add a `usePlanDeferredValue<T>(promise)` hook (own file under `app/routing/plans/hooks/`) that holds the previously resolved value and keeps rendering it while the next promise is pending — the skeleton then appears only on the genuine first load. Cover it with a test that resolves promise A, swaps in a pending promise B, and asserts A's content is still on screen and the skeleton is not.
2. **Region-scoped error copy** via `errorText`, so one failing region degrades in place.

Skeletons must match the real content's footprint so nothing jumps when data lands: the configuration form's fieldset stack, the output stream's monospace block, the run-transparency tables' header + rows, and the toolbar's tag-chip row. Each skeleton gets a render test asserting it paints without the data it stands in for.

description:
`docs/openthrottle/plan-run-worktrees.md` is the doc both dead migrations point readers at ("See docs/openthrottle/plan-run-worktrees.md"), so it is the page most likely to have absorbed the old model.

## Re-read 2026-08-29: the doc is 90% correct, with one passage to delete

Verified accurate and to be left alone: the § "Worktree root" rung table (`env` / `checkout-env` / `default`), § "Where worktrees live" (`<root>/<org>/<repo>/<worktree>`, org from the git remote, no-remote falls back to directory name), and the override paragraph stating that a configured root still gets `<org>/<repo>` appended. This section is the reference wording task `f97c2a30` should copy from.

**The one hit** is § "One variable, no second channel", around lines 103-110:

> There was briefly a workspace setting for this, stored in `user_workspace_settings.worktree_root`. It was removed in migration 109. A database column cannot be read by a shell script, so the setting only ever applied to server-driven runs while `pnpm run worktree:new`, the Claude `WorktreeCreate` hook and Cursor silently used the default — the settings page displayed a value half the system ignored. Anyone who had set one re-expresses it by uncommenting `OPENTHROTTLE_WORKTREE_ROOT` in their `.env`.
>
> Nothing forwards a root to the script any more, either: …

Delete the first paragraph outright, and the "any more, either" framing of the second — a reader who never knew the column existed does not need its postmortem, and this is precisely the "learns what the mechanism used to be outside of `databases/migrations/`" that the definition of done forbids. Keep the section's own claim (`OPENTHROTTLE_WORKTREE_ROOT` is the only channel; the provisioner passes its environment through and lets `resolve_worktree_root` answer) stated in the present tense, with no reference to what it replaced.

description:
The short's payoff is beats 0:32 through 0:50: search the symptom, the note comes back, "your agents query the same index before they start work."

Notes are not in that index. `search._index.tsx.graphql` reads `chunks` with `planId`, `planTitle`, `taskId`, `taskTitle`, `source`, `sourcePath`, `sourceRepo`, `sourceSha` - no `noteId`. The schema's `getDocument` description names the backing tables outright: "UUID from plan_embeddings, task_embeddings, or documentation_embeddings". The migrations create `plan_embeddings` (004), `task_embeddings` (005), `documentation_embeddings` (020), `code_embeddings` (052) and `custom_prompt_embeddings` (037), and no note table. `scripts/seed-demo.ts` truncates `task_embeddings, plan_embeddings` and never writes a note embedding.

Option A - index notes: a `note_embeddings` table and migration, ingestion on note create and update, a `note` source in the search resolver, and a note branch in the results UI. This is the feature the short is selling, and if the channel wants this short the product needs it. It is a real backend plan and should be spawned as its own, with this one blocked on it - not smuggled in as a screencast task.

Option B - re-cut around what notes do today: captured, listed, readable, Markdown-rendered. That drops the payoff and makes the current title ("capture context your agents can actually find") inaccurate, so it wants a new script rather than an edit to this one.

Option C - park 10 for the season and pull a later script forward.

Record the decision and the reasoning here. Do not record a search that does not find the note and narrate it as if it did.
summary: Notes are absent from the semantic index, so the short's entire payoff is unrecordable. Settle the direction before anything else moves.
title: Decide: index notes, or re-cut the short without the search payoff

description:
The unifying move of option E: build the plugin **once**, so leg A publishes it and leg B points `--plugin-dir` at it in place.

Extend `packages/agentic-hooks/scripts/bundle-hooks.ts`, which already esbuild-bundles adapters into self-contained CJS with a deterministic, byte-stable output (pinned esbuild, `minify:false`, no timestamp banner) and a `--check` drift gate. Add a plugin-payload output alongside the existing `BUNDLES` rows:

```
<payload-root>/
  .claude-plugin/plugin.json     # name, version, description, author
  hooks/hooks.json               # event -> matcher -> ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/*.cjs
  hooks/*.cjs                    # the same five claude adapters, bundled
  README.md                      # what it collects, and how to turn it off
```

Requirements:

- **Only the events task 1 proved fire under `-p`.** Do not ship dead wiring.
- `hooks.json` mirrors this repo's `.claude/settings.json` `hooks` block (matcher `Skill` on `PreToolUse`, unmatched `Stop`, `UserPromptExpansion`) but with `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`-relative commands instead of `./.claude/hooks/` ones.
- Keep the determinism guarantees and extend `bundle-hooks-check` to cover the new outputs, so the payload cannot rot. Declare `inputs`/`outputs` on both targets.
- **`version` in `plugin.json` needs an ownership decision:** hand-bumped, or derived from the package version. Whichever — it must be deterministic, since the drift check diffs the generated file byte-for-byte.
- Decide where the payload lives on disk. It must be a real directory (not gitignored build output) if leg B is going to point at it from a running server.

**Blocked by `60c8e0b8`** — the agentic-hooks bundle targets currently have an undeclared dependency on `nodejs-utils` dist. Distribution work should not be layered on a build that is already wrong.
summary: Payload ships at `plugins/openthrottle/` — a real committed directory, not gitignored build output, so a running server can point `--plugin-dir` at it in a plain checkout with nothing built. Generated by the existing `bundle-hooks` target from the same sources as the in-repo bundles; write and check now walk one artifact list (11 artifacts) so neither can miss an output. DECISIONS: (a) ships TWO adapters, not five — capture and complete are genuine hook handlers, while drain/outcome/scope are manual CLIs wired to no event and would be dead weight in someone else's repo; the buffer still flushes because complete drains opportunistically on Stop. (b) `plugin.json` version DERIVES from the package version — the drift gate diffs byte-for-byte, so a hand-bumped field would be a second source of truth that silently rots. (c) the README is generated too, which is what makes leg A's never-hand-edit-downstream requirement enforceable. (d) wires only the three spike-proven events, with both PreToolUse(Skill) and UserPromptExpansion since they are complementary capture paths. ALSO FIXED THE BLOCKER 60c8e0b8 in passing: esbuild resolves @openthrottle/nodejs-utils through its exports map to dist, so both bundle targets had a real but undeclared dependency on that dist. Proved it by deleting `packages/nodejs-utils/dist` and watching the check fail, then added `dependsOn: ["^build"]` + `^production` inputs and watched it rebuild and pass from the same clean state. A drift gate layered over a build that can spuriously fail is not a gate. UNPLANNED FIX: the pre-commit prettier pass reformatted the generated README's markdown tables and instantly tripped the drift check — two formatters fighting over one generated file — so the payload is now in `.prettierignore`. LIVE VERIFICATION: loaded the real generated payload via `--plugin-dir` into a scratch repo outside the monorepo; it captured a UserPromptExpansion event plus a correlated `success` outcome with a 4650ms duration, and did not block the run. That same run also empirically confirmed the contract's §4 finding — `?? .cache/` appeared in the foreign repo's `git status`. lint + typecheck + test green.
title: Emit the OpenThrottle plugin directory as a first-class Nx artifact

description:
Wire the hint into `WorkspaceEditorMultiSelect` / `SettingsWorkspaceEditorsForm`.

**Behavior — the whole point of the plan:**
- `installed` → quiet affirmative. Do not shout; the common case should be calm.
- `not_found` → advisory only. Something like "Not detected on this machine — the button will still appear if you enable it." It must read as information, not an error.
- `unknown` → render **nothing**. No badge, no placeholder. Silence is the correct output when we do not know.

**Hard rules:**
- Never disable the checkbox, never auto-untick, never block save. A user on a container-backed server sees `unknown` everywhere and must retain full control.
- Presence is display-only. It must not touch the value submitted by `parseEnabledEditorsFromFormData` — that parser already caused a silent-drop bug once; keep detection well away from it.
- Degrade to no hints if the presence query fails. This is a nicety; it must never take the settings page down.

Generators first for any new component (`NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:react-router --subGenerator=component …`, `--folder` takes the app-relative form like `routing/settings/components`; `--list=componentFolders` is the authority). Keep the generated section markers. Copy strings belong in the nearest `data.copy.ts`.

Tests: use `component` not `screen`, `userEvent` not `fireEvent`. Cover all three states, and assert explicitly that `unknown` renders no hint and that no state disables the control.
summary: WorkspaceEditorPresenceHints (generator-scaffolded, section markers kept) renders under the multi-select inside SettingsWorkspaceEditorsForm. installed = a quiet check + "detected"; not_found = an info icon plus "not detected — you can still enable it, and its buttons will still appear", phrased as reassurance rather than an error; unknown is filtered out before anything renders, so the component returns null and the page shows no heading, badge or placeholder. Copy lives in the settings data.copy.ts. The loader fetches a separate getEditorPresence document in parallel with .catch(() => null), so a probe failure degrades to no hints instead of taking the settings page down. Presence never reaches parseEnabledEditorsFromFormData — it is a display-only prop. 14 tests across the two files cover all three states plus query-failure and empty, and assert the negatives explicitly: unknown renders nothing, a NOT_FOUND editor still submits its hidden enabledEditors input with save enabled, an all-unknown probe leaves the form fully usable, and the hint block contains no button or input at all. developer typecheck, lint, test (702 files / 3686 tests) and build all green; one AddFolderDialog flake passed on rerun.

description:

Implementation (Recommended approach — widen from the existing parser):
- Import `extractContentAfterFrontmatter` and `parseYamlFrontmatter` from the sibling frontmatter modules (use `.ts` import extensions, matching the package convention).
- `const body = extractContentAfterFrontmatter(fileContent);`
- `const { fields } = parseYamlFrontmatter(fileContent);`

Export from `packages/openthrottle-skills/src/index.ts` with a `/** @public */` tag (Knip keeps public API) alongside the existing frontmatter exports, plus the `SplitFrontmatterResult` type export.

If you deviate to the raw-`yaml` approach instead, document why in the JSDoc and ensure task 2 covers the added semantics.

description:
The schedule registry deliberately staggers jobs so no two audit plans land the same morning. Job_WorkInFlight already holds the only daily slot at `0 13 * * *`.

Decide and record a daily slot that does not collide — recommend `0 12 * * *` (UTC), an hour ahead of Job_WorkInFlight so the day's inbound issues are already on a plan before the work-in-flight reconcile reads OT state. Driver `claude`, model `sonnet`, timezone `UTC`, enabled `true`.

Note the weekly-plan implication in the doc: unlike every other job, a missed run is cheap here (the next run picks up the same week's plan), but a run that fires before Monday 00:00 UTC and after it in the same calendar day would compute two different week keys — the prompt requires computing the Monday of the current ISO week, so verify the chosen slot does not sit on a week boundary.

Acceptance: a new row in the schedule-registry table of docs/monorepo/recurring-agent-jobs.md with cron, fires-at, driver, and model; no cron collision with an existing row.
summary: Slot chosen: `0 12 * * *` UTC, driver claude, model sonnet, enabled. No collision — the only other daily row is Job_WorkInFlight at `0 13 * * *`, and every other row is weekly/biweekly/monthly at 14:00+. Rationale recorded in the doc: firing an hour ahead of Job_WorkInFlight puts the day's inbound issues on a plan before the work-in-flight reconcile reads OT state, and 12:00 UTC sits twelve hours clear of the Monday 00:00 UTC ISO-week boundary, so a run can never compute two different week keys.

description:
The durable, human-facing half: install once per machine, applies in every repo the user opens.

A marketplace is a repo with a `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` at its root listing plugins (`name`, `description`, `author`, `category`, `source`); `source` can be `git-subdir`, so **one repo can host the marketplace and the plugin together**. Reference the installed `claude-plugins-official` marketplace for the exact schema (`$schema: https://anthropic.com/claude-code/marketplace.schema.json`).

Decisions this task owns:

1. **Host repo.** This monorepo has two remotes: `origin` → `OpenThrottle/monorepo` (canonical, private) and `openthrottle` → `OpenThrottle/OpenThrottle` (the public mirror, unrelated history). A marketplace must be reachable by users, so it cannot live only in the private canonical repo. Options: the public mirror, or a dedicated `OpenThrottle/claude-plugins` repo. A dedicated repo is likely cleaner — the mirror's unrelated history makes a subdir sync awkward.
2. **Publish flow.** How the task-2 artifact gets from the monorepo into the host repo: a release workflow, a sync script, or a committed copy with a drift gate. Whatever it is, the generated payload must never be hand-edited in the host repo.
3. **Versioning and update story** for users who have already installed it.
4. **Licensing** — the payload ships publicly and the pre-launch licensing work is already settled elsewhere; make sure the plugin repo carries the right LICENSE and NOTICE.

Out of scope for v1: bundling skills or the OT MCP server into the plugin. Note in the README that the plugin format supports both, so the later consolidation with `d3a30314` is an obvious follow-up rather than a rewrite.
summary: THE TASK'S PREMISE WAS STALE, AND THAT SETTLED MOST OF IT. The task assumed `origin` → OpenThrottle/monorepo is private, forcing a choice between the public mirror and a dedicated OpenThrottle/claude-plugins repo. `gh repo view` reports it as PUBLIC and Apache-2.0. That collapses three of the four decisions: (1) HOST REPO = this repo — a marketplace only has to be reachable by users, and it already is; `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` now sits at the root. (2) PUBLISH FLOW = none needed. The payload is already committed here and drift-gated by bundle-hooks-check, so the marketplace entry points at it in place with `source: "./plugins/openthrottle"`. Syncing a copy into a second repo would reintroduce exactly the hand-edit risk the task warned against AND add a pinned ref to keep in sync — used the relative-path source form (the claude-code-warp pattern) rather than git-subdir with url/ref/sha, since same-repo hosting makes the pin redundant. (4) LICENSING = inherited; Apache-2.0 LICENSE.md and NOTICE already sit at the root, so the payload README carries a pointer rather than its own copies. (3) VERSIONING was already settled by the payload generator — plugin.json derives its version from the package version, and the marketplace entry deliberately carries NO version of its own so there is nothing to rot; updates are `/plugin marketplace update openthrottle`. VERIFIED END-TO-END ON THE REAL MECHANISM, not just the schema: added this worktree as a marketplace (`claude plugin marketplace add`), installed the plugin (`claude plugin install openthrottle@openthrottle`), and confirmed its hooks captured a skill invocation in an unrelated scratch repo with NO `--plugin-dir` flag — which is the whole point of leg A. Then uninstalled the plugin and removed the marketplace so no state was left on the machine. Generated README now carries install instructions, the update story, the license pointer, and a note that the plugin format also carries skills and MCP servers so folding in d3a30314 later is an addition rather than a rewrite. NOTE FOR THE OWNER: no external repo was created and nothing was published — hosting is now just a property of merging this branch.
title: Leg A — publish the plugin to a marketplace and pick its host repo

description:
`evaluateTagActionRules` returns every match with no precedence, so a narrow project-scoped rule cannot override a broad global one. Add ranking as a separate pure function next to it in `packages/openthrottle-skills/src/` (zero I/O, mirroring the `resolveSkillAvailability` precedent) rather than changing the evaluator's contract.

- New `rank-tag-action-rules.ts` exporting a specificity score and a `rankMatchedTagActions(matches)` that returns them narrowest-first.
- Score: `project_id` set = 2, `environment` set = 1, `status` set = 1, plus `tag_all.length`. Ties break on `created_at ASC` so ordering is stable — this means `MatchedTagAction` needs the scope fields and `createdAt` carried through from `TagActionRuleInput`.
- Export from the package index with a `@public` JSDoc tag so Knip keeps it.
- Unit tests covering: project beats global, environment beats unqualified, more tags beats fewer, and stable tie-break.

No consumer changes in this task — wiring lands in the next one.
title: Add a pure specificity ranking for matched rules

description:
The previous task buys headroom; this one earns it back. A suite that needs >5s per test is a cost problem even when it passes — these three are on the critical path of the slowest shard.

**1. `tools/generators` → `src/generators/react/generator.{,component,hook,story,util}.test.ts`** — the largest cluster (5 files timed out in run 32181037247 alone). Each `should run successfully` case runs a real Nx devkit generator. Check whether the expensive tree/workspace setup is repeated per test where a shared `beforeAll` fixture would do, and whether all five files need a full generator invocation or whether one integration case plus cheaper unit assertions on the emitted file set would cover the same contract. Note these are genuinely doing real work — if the cost is irreducible, say so explicitly and leave them relying on the raised budget rather than inventing a fragile optimization.

**2. `packages/react-router-editor/src/components/__tests__/Editor.ssr.test.tsx`** — measured at 6318ms. The test already mocks `@monaco-editor/react`, so the cost is the *rest* of the module graph pulled by `await import('../Editor')`. Two tests share the file and only the first pays the import; investigate what else `../Editor` drags in at module scope and whether the SSR-safety contract can be asserted without importing the full component graph. The `IS_BROWSER === false` short-circuit is the only behavior under test.

**3. `src/data/__tests__/watch.test.ts` → `watchWorkspace`** — chokidar fs-event timing. If it currently races a fixed sleep against real filesystem events, replace that with `vi.waitFor` against the expected event set so it finishes as soon as the events land instead of always paying the worst case.

### Verify

Record before/after wall-clock per project (`pnpm nx run <project>:test`) and report the numbers — the point of this task is a measured reduction, so an unmeasured 'looks faster' is not a completion.
summary: Reduce the actual cost of the generator, Editor.ssr, and watchWorkspace suites so they are not merely under a raised ceiling.
title: Speed up the three repeat-offender suites

description:
Add migration `databases/migrations/092_*.sql` (next after 091) implementing the storage decision:

1. ALTER `user_disabled_agent_clis` ADD COLUMN `model TEXT` (nullable; NULL = whole agent, non-null = a specific model). Idempotent (`ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`).
2. Drop the existing `uq_user_disabled_agent_clis_user_backend` unique constraint and replace with TWO partial unique indexes (NULLs are distinct in Postgres UNIQUE, so a plain 3-col unique would allow duplicate whole-agent rows):
   - `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... ON user_disabled_agent_clis (user_id, backend) WHERE model IS NULL;`
   - `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... ON user_disabled_agent_clis (user_id, backend, model) WHERE model IS NOT NULL;`
   Use `IF NOT EXISTS` / `IF EXISTS`; guard the constraint drop so re-runs are safe.
3. CREATE TABLE `user_favorite_agent_models (id uuid pk, user_id uuid FK users ON DELETE CASCADE, backend text, model text NOT NULL, created_at timestamptz)` with UNIQUE (user_id, backend, model) and an index on user_id. Presence-as-favorite.
4. COMMENT ON TABLE/COLUMN for the new table and the new `model` column, matching the house style in 091 (explain presence semantics, null=whole-agent, opaque model string, no FK/catalog).

Run the migration locally (`pnpm run database:migrate`) to confirm it applies cleanly and is idempotent (safe to re-run via the schema_migrations ledger). No entity/service changes in this task.
summary: Extend the disabled table with a nullable model column (two partial unique indexes) and add the presence-as-favorite favorites table; idempotent DDL + COMMENTs.
title: Migration: model column on user_disabled_agent_clis + user_favorite_agent_models

description:
Answers "how do we track token usage when the loop runs in Claude directly": the harness already writes per-turn `usage` into the session transcript JSONL, and hook payloads carry `transcript_path`.

- New Claude adapter entrypoint under `src/adapters/claude/` (plus a `BUNDLES` row) that on `Stop` — and again on `SessionEnd` to catch the tail — reads the transcript at `transcript_path`, extracts each assistant turn's usage (input, output, cache read/write, reasoning, totals, cost when reported, model), folds it through `@openthrottle/agentic-token-usage`, and persists via the task 5 mutation with the session context from task 3 attached (plan/task/branch/session).
- **Watermark, not re-read**: keep a per-session offset/last-seen-turn-id file so repeated `Stop` firings never double-count. Combined with server-side idempotency this must be exactly-once in practice; prove it with a test that fires the hook three times over a growing transcript.
- Buffer to JSONL and drain through the task 2 kind-agnostic drain when the server is unreachable. Fail-open and time-boxed — a large transcript must not delay the turn; cap the work per firing and resume from the watermark next time.
- Handle the real shapes defensively: malformed lines, missing `usage`, turns from subagents, and a transcript that was compacted or rotated mid-session.
- Tests with fixture transcripts: fresh session, incremental append, replay, malformed lines, absent usage, missing transcript file.
summary: New Claude hook adapter that tails the session transcript, normalizes per-turn usage, and posts it with plan/session attribution and a watermark.
title: Capture token usage from the Claude Code session transcript

description:
The whole point of the coarse split: one move, one library, no per-domain boundary design.

Because every domain travels together, the **~60 cross-domain `routing/X -> routing/Y` edges become intra-library and require zero work** — `skills -> agents` (27), `skills -> home` (6), `projects -> prompts` (5), `personas -> agents` (4), and the rest all stop being a problem. That is the main reason this ordering is cheaper than 653d1be5's.

1. Scaffold `@openthrottle/developer-routing` with `@tools/generators:package`; source-first, no `build` target.
2. Move all 26 `app/routing/<domain>` folders in. Preserve the internal folder shape (`components/`, `hooks/`, `data/`, `config/`, `utils/`, `actions/`, `testing/`) and the generated section comments — this is a move, not a redesign.
3. Rewrite `~/routing/*` imports in `app/routes/**` to the package name. Roughly 300 import sites across ~98 route modules; script it and review the diff rather than hand-editing.
4. `index.ts` becomes the public surface. It will be large — that is expected and acceptable for a staging library. Keep it mechanical (re-export per domain) rather than curating an API you will re-cut in 653d1be5 anyway.
5. Copy the app's Vitest tuning as a STARTING point (`pool: 'vmForks'`, `vmMemoryLimit: '512MB'`, `maxWorkers: 4`) — this library inherits ~553 of the 677 files, so the OOM rationale in `docs/reliability/developer-vitest-pool.md` still applies to it. Then measure and tune.
6. Depends on `@openthrottle/developer-kernel`; must NOT depend on `openthrottle-developer`. Consider an ESLint module-boundary rule to keep it that way.
7. Manual tsconfig `references`, `check:tsconfig-refs`, Nx tags (`pnpm nx:validate-tags`), knip clean.

Done when: `pnpm run check:local` green, `nx run openthrottle-developer:dev` renders every route area correctly, and a production build (`nx run openthrottle-developer:build`) produces equivalent CSS (Tailwind `@source` coverage) and no runtime import errors.
summary: All 26 domain folders move as a single unit — ~553 test files. Deliberately not split further in this plan.
title: Phase B: extract all of app/routing into @openthrottle/developer-routing as ONE library

description:
Add activity classification on top of discovery, per the plan's definition — existence of a directory NEVER means 'in progress'.

- `RUNNING`: an `IN_PROGRESS` `plan_runs` row whose `checkout_id` resolves (via `repository_checkouts.filesystem_path`) to this worktree AND whose `heartbeat_at` is within the staleness cutoff. Reuse the existing staleness cutoff constant/service from the heartbeat work rather than hardcoding a new number; a stale IN_PROGRESS row is dead and must NOT read as running.
- `DIRTY`: no live run, and `git status --porcelain` non-empty OR the branch is ahead of its upstream (`git rev-list --count @{upstream}..HEAD`, tolerating no-upstream).
- `IDLE`: clean and no live run.

Also carry `unregistered: boolean` (no `repository_checkouts` row at this path for this user) — orthogonal to activity — and, when RUNNING, the plan run id so the UI can link to the run.

Match paths on resolved real paths, not raw strings, so a symlinked worktree root cannot make a running worktree look idle.

Unit tests: fresh-heartbeat IN_PROGRESS run -> RUNNING; same run with an expired heartbeat -> falls through to DIRTY/IDLE; dirty-but-no-run -> DIRTY; clean -> IDLE; no-upstream branch does not throw; registered vs unregistered flag.
title: Classify each discovered worktree as RUNNING / DIRTY / IDLE

Then tune the knob that actually governs the hypothesis. Fish re-chunks internally at `chunk_length` (100–300, default 300). Render a take well over 300 characters and **listen at the seam**. Do the same quick pass on `temperature` / `top_p` / `prosody` if the seam turns out not to be the limiting factor — the deliverable is a settled set of request parameters for the backend to pin, not just a yes/no.

Season 1 is unshipped, so render the real scripts rather than a synthetic sample; the takes produced here are useful output, not throwaway.

Outcome recorded in the plan output: measurements for both paths, the seam listen, and the `chunk_length` (plus any other parameters) the implementation should pin. If whole-take turns out NOT to beat per-sentence on the listen, say so plainly and record what was tried — the plan still proceeds, because the timestamps also buy accurate boundaries, but the parameters and the framing change.

description:
## Finding
Task detail loader performs **4 sequential** authenticated GraphQL round-trips. Waterfall depth is the measured cost (latency stacks 4× RTT).

## Paths
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/plans.$planId.tasks.$taskId._index.tsx` loader (approx lines 65–108)
  1. `GetTaskByIdDocument`
  2. `GetPlanByIdDocument` (depends on task.planId)
  3. `TaskLinkedArtifactsDocument`
  4. `TaskOutputStreamChunksDocument`
- Documents: `plans.$planId.tasks.$taskId._index.tsx.graphql`

## Measured before
**4 sequential `await executeGraphqlWithAuth(...)` calls** on the happy path when `task` is present. (2) depends on (1); (3) and (4) only need `taskId` / `task.planId` and can run in parallel with each other and largely with (2).

```bash
# Structural re-check (count sequential awaits in loader):
rg -n "await executeGraphqlWithAuth" applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/plans.\$planId.tasks.\$taskId._index.tsx
```

## Suspected cause
Loader authored as linear awaits; no `Promise.all` for independent queries; no single combined GraphQL document.

## Proposed fix
After task fetch: `Promise.all([plan, artifacts, outputChunks])` or one multi-root query. Prefer the existing GraphQL multi-field pattern used elsewhere (e.g. schedule index).

## Expected after
Happy-path loader **≤ 2** sequential network round-trips (task → then parallel rest, or 1 combined document).

## Acceptance
Loader source shows ≤2 sequential GraphQL awaits on the success path; independent fetches use `Promise.all` or one document. Optionally confirm with a traced request that RTT count drops from 4→≤2.
title: 7. Task detail loader: collapse 4 sequential GraphQL RTTs

description:
## Finding
Monaco language workers are emitted into the **client** build but are referenced by **zero** client JS modules — 70% of client JS is dead deploy weight.

## Paths
- Built orphans: `applications/openthrottle-developer/build/client/assets/{ts,css,html,json}.worker-*.js`
- Related: `packages/react-router-editor` (Monaco); `packages/react-router-editor/AGENTS.md` notes apps do not configure `MonacoEnvironment` / `?worker` imports
- Server copies the same workers under `build/server/assets/`

## Measured before
After `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:build`:
- Workers total **8.66 MB** of **12.31 MB** client JS (70.3%)
- Per file: ts 6731.7 / css 1029.7 / html 702.6 / json 399.5 KB
- Grep of all non-worker client JS for worker hashes / `ts.worker` / `MonacoEnvironment`: **NONE**

```bash
pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:build
python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
a=Path('applications/openthrottle-developer/build/client/assets')
ws=list(a.glob('*worker*.js'))
print(sum(p.stat().st_size for p in ws)/1024/1024, 'MB', len(ws), 'files')
PY
```

## Suspected cause
SSR/client asset emission of Monaco worker files without a client `MonacoEnvironment` wiring them; RR may be copying server assets into `build/client`.

## Proposed fix
Stop emitting unreferenced workers into `build/client`. If self-hosted Monaco is desired, wire `MonacoEnvironment` + `?worker` only on editor routes (prompts/plans/skills) and keep workers out of the default client graph; otherwise leave CDN path explicit and delete the orphans.

## Expected after
Client `*worker*.js` count **0**, or workers only appear as dependencies of an editor route chunk that actually imports them. Client JS total **≤ ~4 MB** (≈ current excl-workers 3.65 MB).

## Acceptance
Re-run measure: orphan worker bytes in `build/client/assets` = **0**, or every worker file is referenced by ≥1 non-worker client module.
title: 3. Developer client: remove 8.66 MB orphan Monaco workers

description:
Free money sitting unmerged. OT plan `e448a51d` is DONE on PR #267 (config-only: `vmForks` + `vmMemoryLimit` 512 MB) and measured the developer suite from **253s to ~83s**. `test` is the dominant cost inside `build`, so a 3x cut on the biggest suite is the single largest wall-clock win available without touching coverage.

1. Review and merge PR #267.
2. Then revisit the `--parallel=1` serialization on `test`. The current comment explains why it exists: co-running heavy jsdom suites on one shared 4-vCPU box exceeded its memory ceiling, and the OOM-killer SIGKILLed in-flight workers, surfacing as files reporting `(0 test)`. Two things change that calculus — `vmForks` + a 512 MB per-worker limit lowers the ceiling pressure, and task 2's move to `ubuntu-latest` doubles available RAM (16 GB vs 8 GB).
3. Re-enable `--parallel` for `test` **only with evidence**: run the full affected set several times and confirm no suite reports `(0 test)` and no worker is killed. This failure mode is silent-passing, which is worse than slow — if there is any doubt, leave it serialized.

description:
**Evidence gate — no fix lands before this task names the failure mode.**

Goal: capture exactly what `cursor-agent create-chat` emits on a genuinely cold first invocation, under the same scrubbed environment the server uses.

Steps:
1. Write a throwaway repro script (scratch, not committed) that calls `createCursorAgentSession({ cwd })` from `packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/.../cursor-agent/cursor-agent.ts` and logs stdout/stderr as **raw bytes** (hex or `JSON.stringify` of the buffer) — not `.trim()`ed strings. ANSI escapes and BOMs must be visible.
2. Force cold state between runs. Identify what cursor caches (likely under `~/.cursor` and/or `~/.config/cursor*`); move it aside, run, restore. Record the exact paths touched (`fs_usage`/`lsof` on macOS, or diffing the directory before/after) — this also answers hypothesis 3 about which env-derived paths cursor actually needs.
3. Run the mint under the server's `buildScrubbedEnv()` allowlist AND under a full inherited env. If the failure only reproduces under the scrubbed env, hypothesis 3 is confirmed and the rest of the plan narrows sharply.
4. Time the cold vs warm mint. If cold approaches or exceeds the 30_000 ms `DEFAULT_SESSION_TIMEOUT_MS`, hypothesis 2 is live.
5. Also capture the **second** spawn (the streaming turn) on a cold run — the failure may be in `--resume`, not in `create-chat`.

Deliverable: post findings to the plan output stream (`append_plan_output`) with the raw captured bytes, cold-vs-warm timings, the cursor cache/config paths observed, and a ranked verdict on hypotheses 1-4. Update the plan description's hypothesis ranking to match.

No production code changes in this task.

description:
Settle one question before any code: after the action writes `SKILL.md`, how does the skill get linked into `.agents/skills/` so `/skills` can see it?

The constraint: `discover-repo-skills.server.ts` scans the six agent-folder layouts, never `skills/` and never the personal root. Both destinations are invisible until `skills/ot-skill-sync/scripts/sync.sh` runs. And `openthrottle-developer` has no `child_process` usage today — grep it yourself to confirm before deciding.

Options, with the recommendation first:

**A (recommended) — the action runs sync.** A `.server.ts` module shells out to `skills/ot-skill-sync/scripts/sync.sh` with `execFileSync` (fixed argv, no shell interpolation, cwd pinned to the resolved monorepo root, timeout, refuses when `getMonorepoRoot()` is null). The create genuinely completes: the user lands back on `/skills` and sees their skill. Cost: the app's first subprocess, and it must be written as one narrowly-scoped, well-commented module rather than a general "run a script" helper.

**B — the route creates the stage-1 symlink itself.** No subprocess, but it reimplements a slice of sync.sh (link creation, collision detection, the managed `.gitignore` block for the personal case) that then has to stay in step with it. Duplicated invariants across a shell script and a TS module is the failure mode.

**C — write only, tell the user to run sync.** Simplest and safest, but the success screen has to admit the skill is not visible yet, which is a worse product than either A or B.

Deliverable: a short decision recorded on the plan via `append_plan_output` — which option, and for A the exact guard list the module will carry. Do not write feature code in this task. If the answer is not A, say plainly which downstream tasks change.

Also confirm while you are here: does personal-tier creation need sync at all, or does `personal.sh new <name>` already scaffold + sync in one step and simply want reusing? Read `skills/ot-skill-sync/scripts/personal.sh` before answering — if it does, the personal branch of the action may be a call to it rather than a bespoke write.
requirements: ["Decision recorded on the plan output with rationale", "`child_process` absence in openthrottle-developer verified, not assumed", "personal.sh `new` read and its reusability stated either way", "No feature code written in this task"]

description:
Only someone working ON OpenThrottle should be offered the OpenThrottle catalog as a create destination. Gate it on `FEATURE_BETA_PREVIEW` from `@openthrottle/react-router-utils` — the same flag `SkillsToolbar` and `GlobalSidebarContent` already read, so no new knob.

Two halves, and the second is the one that matters:

1. **UI** — `SkillCreateDestinationField` renders the OpenThrottle `ToggleGroupItem` only when the flag is on. Pass the flag in as a prop from the route/hook rather than importing the config inside the presentational component, so both states are testable without stubbing module state. With the flag off the control is a two-option group (Personal, Custom); Personal remains the default either way, so nothing changes about the initial render.

2. **Server refusal** — the create action must refuse `destination: 'openthrottle'` when the flag is off, before any path resolution or disk access. A hidden toggle button is not a guard: the destination arrives in a form body and a hand-crafted POST bypasses the UI entirely. Reuse the existing structured-refusal shape (`{ error, ok: false }`) with its own copy string, rendered inline like every other create refusal — never thrown.

Confirm `FEATURE_BETA_PREVIEW` resolves correctly in the action's server context (it is parsed from `ENV_SOURCE` in `packages/react-router-utils/src/config/features.ts` and defaults to `false` when unset — verify, do not assume, and note that the developer app's Vitest env fixture pins it to `'false'`).

Tests both ways: flag on → three options render and an `openthrottle` POST succeeds; flag off → two options render, and an `openthrottle` POST is refused with the new message and writes nothing to disk.
requirements: ["The OpenThrottle destination renders only when FEATURE_BETA_PREVIEW is true", "The flag reaches SkillCreateDestinationField as a prop, not a module import", "The create action refuses destination 'openthrottle' when the flag is off, before touching disk", "A refused gated POST leaves the filesystem byte-identical", "Tests cover both flag states for UI and action"]

description:
This is the task most likely to change the plan's outcome, and it was under-specified in the original brief.

`scripts/parallelize-tasks.ts` partitions the affected project list by COUNT, not duration. It deals applications first (they are the heavy Vitest suites), then packages round-robin from a cursor based on how many projects have already been dealt. Its own header says so: "Not duration-weighted: a chunk holding two heavy app suites is slower than one holding six packages."

The trap: `@openthrottle/developer-routing` will be a PACKAGE (scope-prefixed), so it is dealt in the second pass — and depending on how many applications were affected, the cursor can place it on the **same shard as `openthrottle-developer`**. If that happens, the heaviest shard still runs ~677 test files' worth of work and the split buys nothing.

1. Simulate the post-split partition for realistic affected sets (app-only change; app + 1 package; full-affected `main` push) by running the partitioner against synthetic project lists for jobIndex 1..3.
2. Determine whether `developer-routing` co-locates with `openthrottle-developer` in any realistic case.
3. If it does, decide the fix and record it — options: treat a package as "heavy" via an explicit allowlist dealt in the applications pass, deal by a static weight annotation, or read prior-run timings. Prefer the smallest change that is explainable in the script's existing header comment style.
4. Confirm `getShardSelectionErrors()`'s round-trip check still passes with the new project names, and re-read the `!tag:name:` warning in the header before touching anything — direct project names only.

Done when: the simulated partitions for all three scenarios are in plan output, with a written verdict on whether the partitioner needs changing before Phase B is worth doing.
summary: scripts/parallelize-tasks.ts deals applications first then packages round-robin, unweighted — a heavy new package can land on the same box as the app and erase the win.
title: Phase A: audit the shard partitioner for the apps-first weighting trap

description:
Write `docs/monorepo/child-repo-hook-overlay.md` as a decision record in the same shape as `foreign-workspace-skill-injection.md` — that doc is the house style for this class of decision, and the two are direct siblings that readers will compare.

Must cover:

- **Why hooks are not the skills problem**, with the escape-hatch table (`--settings`, `--plugin-dir`, `--plugin-url`, marketplace) and the fact that Claude Code merges hooks additively across user, project, local, and plugin sources. This is the single most valuable thing to write down — without it, the next person will reasonably assume the skill materializer should have been extended, and rebuild option C.
- **Why C was rejected**, and the narrow condition under which it could be revisited.
- The one-artifact-two-delivery-paths design, and which of the five hook events actually survive headless `-p` (from task 1).
- The no-clobber guarantee and how it is verified, not just asserted.

Also update `docs/monorepo/agent-editor-folders.md` and `packages/agentic-hooks/README.md` (currently still the untouched generator stub: "Add a short description of this package"). Cross-link from the skill-injection doc so the sibling relationship is discoverable from either side.
summary: `docs/monorepo/child-repo-hook-overlay.md` written in the same shape as foreign-workspace-skill-injection.md. Leads with §1 "Why this is NOT the skills problem again" and says so explicitly — skills had to be materialized into foreign repos because §2 of the skill record established that no CLI can load them from outside the working tree, whereas every CLI we support can load hooks from outside it. Includes the escape-hatch table and the additive-merge fact, and closes with an explicit rule ("if you are about to write into a child repo to deliver a hook, stop"). §2 records why C was rejected (skills are one dir each; hooks are a single user-owned JSON file with no fragment-include, so writing into it inherits merge/restore/corruption risk to reach somewhere a first-class flag already reaches) and notes the capability matrix has since falsified the revisit condition, so C is CLOSED rather than deferred. §3 covers one-artifact-two-delivery-paths plus why the package split lands where it does and why the container bridge does not apply. §4 records event survival including the counterintuitive UserPromptExpansion result and why the two capture paths are complementary rather than duplicates. §5 shows the no-clobber guarantee as observed interleaving, verified not asserted. §6 is deliberately honest that leg B's zero-mutation property holds for the flag but NOT yet for the core, since the JSONL fallback still writes into the target tree — reproduced live as `?? .cache/`. ALSO: replaced the agentic-hooks generator-stub README with a real one (organization, the two consumers, determinism rules, fail-open posture, kill switches, cross-links); added `plugins/openthrottle/` and `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` to the folder map in agent-editor-folders.md with an explicit "hooks reach child repos differently from skills — do not copy the skills pattern" callout; cross-linked from foreign-workspace-skill-injection.md so the sibling relationship is discoverable from either side, with a warning not to generalize that record's approach to hooks. FIXED THE STALE `--bare` COPY the spike turned up: tools/workflows help text, process-model.md, README.md, and two test fixtures all still described `claude --bare -p …` after that package moved to the driver registry. Since --bare skips hooks, LSP, and plugins outright, that copy described a command that would silently disable this entire feature. All references are gone except the one intentional mention in the decision record. lint + typecheck + test green on @tools/workflows.
title: Documentation + decision record for the hook overlay

description:
**Run this last** — after the deletions, so you are not polishing text you are about to delete.

Every skill's frontmatter description loads into every session. Current cost: **16,918 chars / ~4,229 tokens across 44 skills.**

Worst offenders (chars of frontmatter):

| skill | chars |
|---|---|
| monitor-ci | 806 |
| ot-onboarding | 794 |
| openthrottle-generators | 785 |
| ot-workflow-orchestration | 758 |
| openthrottle-stack | 731 |
| ot-plans | 639 |
| skillopt-sleep | 599 |
| improve | 595 |
| ot-claude-loop | 581 |
| ot-plan-loop | 577 |
| link-workspace-packages | 568 |
| agents-ralph | 514 |

Several of these read as a table of contents for the skill body rather than a routing decision. A description only needs to answer *should the model open this file right now* — trigger conditions and disambiguation from neighbors. Everything else belongs in the body, where it costs nothing until the skill is actually opened.

**Do:**
1. Recompute the budget after tasks 2–8 land.
2. Rewrite every description over ~400 chars down to trigger-only. Keep the USE WHEN clauses (they are what makes routing work) and cut the feature enumerations.
3. Preserve the explicit not-this-skill disambiguators — `ot-postgres` pointing away from `ot-plans` and `openthrottle-stack` is exactly the kind of line that earns its bytes.
4. Verify against the `writing-great-skills` guidance before deleting that skill in the pruning task — harvest anything worth keeping into the repo's own `skills/README.md` first.

**Target:** under 2,000 tokens always-on, roughly 25 skills.

**Done when:** the measured total is under budget and every remaining description is trigger-shaped.
title: Compress frontmatter descriptions to a measured always-on budget

description:
Add `renderTake` to `src/narrate/backends/fish-audio.ts` against `POST https://api.fish.audio/v1/tts/stream/with-timestamp`:

- Body: `text` (the whole take's spoken text, sentences joined), `reference_id` (the pinned voice, read from `DEFAULT_FISH_AUDIO_VOICE` — a swap is pending, so never inline the id), `format: 'wav'`, `sample_rate` from `docs/marketing/format.json`, and `chunk_length` **pinned to the value task 1 settled on** — never left to the default, since it is the knob that decides where the service re-chunks. Same for any `temperature` / `top_p` / `prosody` values task 1 landed on.
- Headers: `Authorization: Bearer`, `Content-Type: application/json`, and the `model` header from the existing `resolveFishAudioModel()`.
- Response is SSE (`text/event-stream`). Per event: decode `audio_base64` and append; take `alignment.segments[]` (`text`/`start`/`end`, relative to chunk start) and offset every one by that event's `chunk_audio_offset_sec` to build the absolute word list.
- Fail loudly, never silently: non-2xx, a stream that ends without covering the submitted text, or an event with `alignment: null` where words were expected. Reuse the existing key-missing error and its KEY_HINT.

Unit-test the SSE parsing and the offset arithmetic against a checked-in fixture body — no network in tests, matching how the existing backend tests are written.

This file's commented-out voice id was already cleaned up in task 0; the constant and its comment are current.
requirements: ["SSE parse handles multi-event and partial-line buffering", "Word timings are absolute to the take, not per chunk", "Request parameters from task 1 are pinned in code with a comment", "Fixture-driven tests, no live API calls in the suite", "Missing FISH_AUDIO_API_KEY still throws with the install hint", "Voice read from DEFAULT_FISH_AUDIO_VOICE — a swap is pending, so no test or fixture asserts the current id"]

description:
New tsx script following the house pattern of the other audit scripts (`scripts/audit-route-shape.ts` is the closest small model): `scripts/lib` chalk logger + `parseArgs`, no direct chalk import, exits 0 in warn-mode.

**Behaviour**

- Enumerate every `docs/**/*.md`.
- Build the reachable set from link targets in `docs/README.md` plus each directory README (`docs/marketing/README.md`, `docs/marketing/assets/README.md`, `docs/nx/dependency-graphs/README.md`, and any future one).
- Decide and document one thing explicitly: **is reachability transitive?** The `docs/tools/templates/*` files (react.md, react-router.md, nestjs.md, package.md, folders.md, EXAMPLES.md, TROUBLESHOOTING.md, NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS.md) are all linked from `AGENT_USAGE.md`, which is itself linked from `docs/README.md`. Recommendation: allow one hop through an index-linked doc that acts as a section index, or simply treat a directory's own hub doc like a README. Whatever is chosen, state it in the script header comment.
- Resolve relative links, ignore anchors/query, skip external URLs, and skip README files themselves as audit subjects.
- Report orphans grouped by directory; print the count. Support `--json` like `audit-test-coverage.ts`.
- `--strict` flag exits 1; default (warn-mode) always exits 0.

**Wiring**

- `package.json` scripts: `audit:docs-index`, `audit:docs-index:json`, `audit:docs-index:strict`. Note the `audit` / `audit:strict` aggregate scripts glob `/^audit:(?!test-coverage).*:strict$/`, so adding `:strict` opts this into `check:local:audit` immediately — hold that back until the coverage task lands (see the wire-up task).

**Test:** `scripts/__tests__/audit-docs-index.test.ts` over a fixture doc tree — orphan detected, linked doc not flagged, transitive case behaves as documented, `--strict` exit code.

**Measured 2026-08-28:** 75 markdown files under `docs/`; 32 are unreachable from `docs/README.md` or a sibling README today. Re-verify by running the script.
title: Build scripts/audit-docs-index.ts (warn-mode orphan report)

description:
This is the highest-value task: docs are only read by an agent that thinks it has a question, but an error is read by an agent that already made the mistake.

Today `@tools/generators:react-router --subGenerator=component --application=@openthrottle/react-router-chat` (a package) fails with `Unable to read "applications/react-router-chat/app/routing" (resolved to "…"): ENOENT: no such file or directory, scandir …`. That reads as "packages are not supported", which is how a false claim ended up in PR #468's body, plan b67c8e27's output, and agent memory.

Validate `--application` in the react-router generator (source: `tools/generators/src/generators/react-router/`, shared entry `generator.ts`, schema `schema.json`) against the real applications list BEFORE any filesystem read, and when the supplied value is not an application:
- if it resolves to a known Nx project tagged `technology:react` (i.e. it is a package), fail with a message naming the exact corrective command, e.g. `"@openthrottle/react-router-chat" is a package, not an application. Use: NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:react --subGenerator=component --destination=@openthrottle/react-router-chat --name=<Name>`;
- otherwise fail with the valid applications list and the `--list=applications` command.

Apply the same treatment to a `--folder` that points outside the application (e.g. one starting `packages/`), since that is the other shape of the same mistake. Consider the mirror case in the `react` generator — a `--destination` naming something that is not a valid destination should point at `--list=destinations`, and if the value is an application-only path shape, at `react-router`.

Add unit tests alongside the existing `generator.component.test.ts` covering: a package passed to `--application` produces the corrective `react --destination=` command in the message; an unknown value lists valid applications; a valid application still generates unchanged (no regression).
requirements: ["Passing a package to react-router --application fails with a message naming the corrective `react --subGenerator=component --destination=…` command, before any ENOENT", "Passing an unknown --application fails with the valid applications list and the --list=applications discovery command", "A --folder outside the target application fails with a comparable directed message rather than ENOENT", "Valid invocations are unchanged — existing generator tests still pass", "New unit tests cover the package-passed-as-application case, the unknown-application case, and the no-regression case"]
title: Make the wrong generator fail with the corrective command

description:
Make the OT MCP server tell the API which workspace it was launched in.

## Work

- Capture the caller's workspace **once at stdio startup**: `OPENTHROTTLE_MCP_WORKSPACE_PATH` (trimmed) when set, else `process.cwd()`. Store it in `src/config/` alongside the other server config, not read ad hoc inside tool handlers.
- `create_plan` and `create_plans` send it as `workspacePath` on the GraphQL input.
- Add an optional `workspacePath` tool parameter so a caller can override the captured value, or pass an empty string to opt out entirely. An explicitly-passed value always wins over the captured cwd.
- Update `createPlanToolDescription` / `createPlansToolDescription`: mention `workspacePath`, and fix the standing gap where `create_plan`'s description omits `runConfigJson` even though its schema already accepts it.

## The trap

The HTTP / Nest-hosted MCP surface (`bin-http.ts`, `src/nest/`) runs **inside the server process**, where `process.cwd()` is the server's directory, not any caller's workspace. That surface must send no `workspacePath` at all unless one was passed explicitly. Gate the capture on the stdio transport (`runServerLocal`) rather than on module load, so importing the tools from the Nest surface cannot pick up a bogus path.

## Definition of done

- Tests: stdio capture prefers the env override; falls back to `process.cwd()`; an explicit tool argument beats the captured value; an empty-string argument suppresses the field; the Nest/HTTP surface sends nothing.
- `pnpm nx run @openthrottle/openthrottle-mcp:test`, `:lint`, `:typecheck` pass.
title: MCP: capture the stdio caller's workspace and pass it to create_plan / create_plans

description:
Create `databases/migrations/092_grant_admin_all_permissions.sql`. Re-run the admin grant as a CROSS JOIN over the CURRENT `permissions` table so `admin` picks up `plans:read`/`plans:write` (and any other perms added after migration 034), idempotently.

```sql
-- Backfill the admin role with every permission currently defined.
-- Migration 034 granted admin all permissions via CROSS JOIN, but that was a
-- point-in-time snapshot; later perms (plans:* in 045) were never re-granted to
-- admin. Re-run the CROSS JOIN so admin is the full superset again. Idempotent.
INSERT INTO role_permissions (role_id, permission_id)
SELECT r.id, p.id
FROM roles r CROSS JOIN permissions p
WHERE r.name = 'admin'
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
```

Acceptance:
- File follows the 0NN naming and header-comment convention of neighboring migrations.
- Re-running the file is a no-op (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING).
- After apply, `SELECT p.name FROM role_permissions rp JOIN roles r ON r.id=rp.role_id JOIN permissions p ON p.id=rp.permission_id WHERE r.name='admin'` includes `plans:read` and `plans:write`.
title: Add migration 092 to backfill admin with all permissions (fixes plans:read/plans:write)

Requirements of the change:
- Foreign-skill injection keeps writing a block with its CURRENT marker text verbatim, so existing on-disk exclude files keep parsing and no repo needs migrating.
- Writing block A must leave block B byte-identical, in both orders, and repeated writes must stay idempotent.
- `removeManagedExcludeBlock` removes only its own owner's block.
- Keep the existing tolerance for a legacy block missing its end marker.

Consider whether this code still belongs under `foreign-skill-injection/` once it has two tenants, or should move up a level. Moving it is optional; if it moves, keep the existing exports working.
requirements: ["Two owners can hold blocks in one .git/info/exclude without clobbering, verified in both write orders", "Foreign-skill injection's marker text is unchanged, so existing exclude files still parse", "removeManagedExcludeBlock removes only the named owner's block", "Repeated writes remain idempotent"]

description:
Several steps in `build` run over the whole tree on every PR regardless of what changed, and two of them are explicitly uncached (`cache: false` in `nx.json` because they read the installed `node_modules` graph, which Nx cannot hash).

- **`⚖️ Dependency-license compliance gate` (`monorepo:validate-licenses`)** and **`📜 THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES freshness guard` (`pnpm run validate:notices`)** — both scan the entire installed graph, both uncached, and the result can only change when the dependency graph changes. Gate both on `pnpm-lock.yaml`, any `package.json`, or `license-policy.json` having changed in the diff. The comment claiming full-tree scanning is "cheapest safety for the case that matters most (a dependency bump / lockfile change)" is right about *when* it matters — which is exactly the condition to gate on.
- **`🧪 Test-coverage audit (warn-only)`** — `continue-on-error: true`, excluded from the blocking `audit:strict` aggregate. It gates nothing, so per-PR spend is pure waste. Move it to a weekly scheduled run that writes its report where the remediation plans can carve from it. Keep the documented flip path intact for when a category closes.
- **`🎨 Prettier format-check`** — whole-tree `prettier --check` over ten-plus extensions on every PR, when husky pre-commit already formats. Scope it to files changed in the diff.
- **`🔗 Agent assets SSOT`**, **`📋 Agent assets frontmatter validation`**, **`🔍 circular dependencies`** — path-gate to the inputs each actually reads (`.agents/**`, `skills/**`, and project graph files respectively). The frontmatter target already declares precise `inputs` in `nx.json`, so it is cache-eligible; verify it is actually hitting cache rather than re-running.

Each gate must fail closed: if the diff cannot be computed, run the check.
requirements: ["Licence + notices steps gated on lockfile/package.json/license-policy.json changes", "Test-coverage audit moved off the per-PR path to a schedule, flip path preserved", "format-check scoped to changed files", "Agent-asset and circular-dep steps path-gated or verified cache-hitting", "Every gate fails closed when the diff is unavailable"]
title: Gate the full-tree checks on the inputs that can change their result

description:
Close the regression gap. Only two tests in the app currently assert on `meta(...)`, so every title fixed in tasks 3-5 is unprotected.

Write one table-driven Vitest test that walks the route modules and asserts the invariants, rather than 80 per-route assertions:

1. Every non-resource route module exports `meta` and its first descriptor has a non-empty `title`.
2. No title's leading segment matches a PascalCase-identifier pattern (`/^[A-Z][a-z]+(?:[A-Z][a-z]+)+$/`) — this is the exact check that would have caught `SettingsAppearance`, `NotificationsIndex`, and `PersonasCreate`.
3. Every title ends with `| ${SITE_TITLE}`.
4. No two routes produce the same title — the check that catches the `Settings` and `Calendar` collisions from task 4.

Mechanics to settle while implementing:

- Enumerate route modules from the filesystem (`app/routes/*.tsx`, applying the same `ignoredRouteFiles` exclusions as `app/routes.ts`) with an explicit allowlist of resource routes that legitimately have no title. An explicit allowlist is better than a `resources.` prefix heuristic — it makes each exemption a deliberate, reviewable line.
- Calling `meta` needs plausible args. Most titles are static and tolerate `{ matches: [], loaderData: undefined }`; the `mergeRouteModuleMeta` wrapper reads `args.matches`, so pass an empty array, and detail routes must survive `loaderData: undefined` by design (that is their fallback path). If any route throws on empty args, that is a finding worth fixing, not worth working around in the test.
- Rule 4 only holds for static titles. Detail routes with `loaderData: undefined` all collapse to their fallbacks, which is exactly what should be unique — but confirm no legitimate pair is forced into an artificial difference. If one is, exempt the pair explicitly with a comment.

Put it in `app/routes/__tests__/` alongside the existing route tests, following the shared `setupReactRouterTest` setup already in place.

If the loop turns out to be impractical (dynamic imports of route modules pulling in server-only code), fall back to a static check: a small `audit:route-titles` script that greps the `title:` literals and applies rules 2-4 textually. Say which route you took and why.

Validate: `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:test`, then confirm the guard actually fails by temporarily reverting one title from task 3 to `SettingsAppearance` and watching it go red before restoring it.
title: Add a route-title guard so PascalCase and missing titles cannot land again
