description:
Human decision, not agent work. Read the plan description and pick one of A / B / C / D / E (or a variant). Record the choice and the reasoning as a plan output chunk, then write the implementation task breakdown against it.

The single question that decides most of it: **is the target audience a human opening a child repo, or an OT-orchestrated run?**

- Human-first → needs a persistent, install-once mechanism (A, the plugin).
- Orchestrated-first → needs a spawn-time mechanism (B), and nothing has to touch the user's disk at all.
- Both → E.

Second question, only if multi-CLI parity is a v1 requirement rather than a v2: that is the one force that could justify C, since codex/opencode/grok may have no out-of-repo hook config at all. Answer task 2 first if this is in doubt.
summary: DECIDED 2026-08-18 (owner): option E — plugin (leg A) + spawn-time `--plugin-dir` injection (leg B), built against one shared plugin-directory artifact. Option C explicitly rejected (managed-block merge into a user-owned settings.json, to reach somewhere the CLI already has a first-class out-of-repo flag for); may only be revisited if the capability matrix proves a non-Claude CLI has no out-of-repo hook config AND parity becomes a v1 requirement. Option D retained as the fallback for non-Claude CLIs. Implementation breakdown written against E.
title: 🚦 DECISION GATE — pick the hook-overlay direction (owner)

description:
The reason Season 1 being unshipped matters: it is now the test corpus, not something to protect. Render every Season 1 episode (01–22, L1, L2) through the whole-take Fish path at the pinned parameters, and listen to the result.

A full pass is ~11.3k spoken characters ≈ $0.17, so re-running the whole season after a parameter change costs less than the time spent deciding whether to.

What to look for, per episode, because these are the failure modes this change can introduce that a single spike script would not surface:
- Sentences that get clipped or run together at a slice boundary.
- Long scripts (the two longform episodes, 1.2–1.5k characters) crossing several internal chunks — the seam behaviour at real length, not sample length.
- Shorts that now blow the duration cap: NARRATION.md records hosted voices reading ~25–30% slower than Piper, and the budget warning fires from `format.formats[script.format].maxDurationSeconds`. Cut words; do not speed up the voice.
- Lexicon terms that the whole-take read handles differently from the per-sentence read. NARRATION.md still owes a per-term pass against the winning voice — do it here, since every term is about to be heard in context. Remove entries the voice gets right on its own rather than leaving a workaround that now sounds wrong.

Record which episodes needed script edits and which needed lexicon edits, so the next season starts from a shorter list.
requirements: ["All 24 episodes rendered whole-take and listened to", "Any short exceeding its duration cap fixed by cutting words, not by rate", "The owed per-term lexicon pass completed against this voice", "Episodes needing script or lexicon edits recorded in the plan output"]
title: Re-render Season 1 through the whole-take path and listen to all 24

description:
The export pipes every row through a sanitize stage before it reaches disk:

- **Deny-listed tables** never export regardless of FK closure: `mcp_connector_connections` and anything credential-adjacent (audit the schema for token/secret/credential columns and write the list down with reasons). A denied table that other exported rows FK into gets its FK column nulled or the dependent row dropped — decided per case in the manifest.
- **Secret detector, fail-closed**: known key shapes (AWS, GitHub, Anthropic/OpenAI, JWTs, private key blocks, connection strings with passwords) plus a high-entropy-string heuristic over all kept free text. A hit STOPS the export naming table, column and row id — no silent redaction. Accepted residual risk is explicit: this is best-effort; recordings are human-reviewed before publishing.
- **Identity scrub inside free text**: emails, `/Users/*` and `/home/*` paths, machine hostnames. Word-boundary replacement from a small committed mapping (e.g. real email → demo user email). GitHub usernames and repo names are KEPT deliberately — the repo is public and the workspace is expected to become public.
- **Timestamp rebase**: all timestamps rewritten to the existing minute-offset-from-seed-time convention (offset from the newest timestamp in the window), so a frozen snapshot renders as a fresh, recently-active workspace on camera. Preserve relative ordering exactly; keep plan_output_stream offsets strictly increasing and unique per plan.

Done when: a seeded-with-a-fake-secret dev row makes the export fail naming the row, the scrub is covered by unit tests over representative free text, and the rebase preserves ordering in a property test.
summary: Best-effort sanitization that fails closed on secrets and never exports credential tables.
title: Sanitize pass: deny list, secret detector, identity scrub, timestamp rebase

description:
Against a production build of the developer app pointed at the demo database, with `GITHUB_USER=atlas-ada`:

```
pnpm exec tsx applications/openthrottle-developer/tests/demo/runner/run.ts --flow 06-prd-to-plan --base http://localhost:<port>
```

Then narrate (`NARRATION_BACKEND=piper`, the ship voice) and assemble the 16:9 and 9:16 masters plus the `.srt` and `metadata.json`.

The risk specific to this short is the decompose wait. A real ingest call is slow and non-deterministic, which is the opposite of what a 54-second short wants: too fast and the viewer misses that work happened, too slow and there is dead air the narration cannot cover. Expect to tune this beat more than any other, and `waitFor` on the rendered preview rather than guessing a dwell.

Re-run record without re-narrating while tuning - the stages are independently runnable precisely so a pacing fix is not a re-record of everything.
summary: Run the four pipeline stages and review the masters, watching the decompose wait for dead air.
title: Record, narrate and assemble the short

description:
BullMQ groups / rate-limit-by-key are **BullMQ Pro** features and this workspace pins OSS `bullmq@5.81.3`, so the plan's fallback is the implementation: an application-level advisory lock.

New `scheduled-agent-job-directory-lock.service.ts` in the scheduled-agent-jobs queue folder, injecting the shared `REDIS_CLIENT` from `@openthrottle/nestjs-redis` (nullable — `null` when `REDIS_HOST` is unset).

- `acquire(key, { timeoutMs, signal })` — `SET <ns>:<hashed key> <token> NX PX <ttl>` in a poll loop until acquired, the timeout elapses, or the signal aborts. Returns a release handle (or a no-op handle when Redis is unconfigured, so a Redis-less deployment behaves exactly as today rather than refusing to run).
- **TTL + heartbeat**: the TTL must be short enough that a killed worker frees the directory promptly, so it cannot simply cover the 15m+ run duration. A `setInterval` renewal (`PEXPIRE` guarded by a token check) extends it while the run is in flight; the interval is unref'd and always cleared on release. This is what satisfies the plan's 'a worker killed mid-run does not permanently block that directory'.
- **Release** via a Lua compare-and-delete on the fencing token, so a lock that already expired and was re-taken by another worker is never deleted out from under its new owner.
- Redis errors are logged and treated as 'lock unavailable → proceed' rather than failing the run: the lock is an optimisation against a git-index race, not a correctness gate, and a Redis blip must not take scheduled jobs down.
- Keys are namespaced and hashed (a resolved cwd is an unbounded-length absolute path).

Unit tests with a stubbed ioredis client: acquisition, contention then acquisition after release, timeout, abort, renewal firing, compare-and-delete not deleting a foreign token, and the unconfigured-Redis no-op path.
requirements: ["Acquire uses SET NX PX with a unique fencing token", "A heartbeat renews the TTL while the run is in flight and is always cleared on release", "Release is a Lua compare-and-delete that never deletes another owner's lock", "Redis unconfigured or erroring degrades to proceeding without a lock, never to a failed run", "Unit tests cover acquire, contend, timeout, abort, renew, and foreign-token release"]
summary: New ScheduledAgentJobDirectoryLockService: SET NX PX per concurrency key with a fencing token, a renewal heartbeat while the run is in flight, and a compare-and-delete release, degrading to a no-op when Redis is unconfigured.
title: Add a Redis advisory directory-lock service with TTL, heartbeat renewal, and safe release

description:
Eliminate `packages/react-router-rollout/src/catalog/` — its contents move up into the package's existing canonical folders. The package already has top-level `components/ config/ data/ hooks/ utils/`, a root `types.ts`, and a root `index.ts` barrel.

## File moves (catalog/ -> destination)
- `catalog/rollout-flag-kind.ts` -> `config/rollout-flag-kind.ts` — it exports the `ROLLOUT_FLAG_KIND` `as const` object, the `isRolloutFlagKind` guard, and the `RolloutFlagKind` type (constant catalog => config).
- `catalog/assert-rollout-flag-catalog.ts` -> `utils/assert-rollout-flag-catalog.ts` — `assertRolloutFlagCatalog` + `isRolloutFlagValueForKind` (assertion/guard helpers => utils).
- `catalog/define-rollout-flags.ts` -> `utils/define-rollout-flags.ts` — `defineRolloutFlags` factory (=> utils).
- `catalog/types.ts` -> merge its type exports (`RolloutBooleanFlagKey`, `RolloutFlagCatalog`, `RolloutFlagCatalogInput`, `RolloutFlagDefinition`, `RolloutFlagDefinitionForKind`, `RolloutFlagKey`, `RolloutFlagValue`, `RolloutFlagValueByKind`, `RolloutJsonValue`) into the package root `src/types.ts`.
- `catalog/index.ts` -> DELETE (fold its re-exports into root `src/index.ts`).
- `catalog/__tests__/define-rollout-flags.test.ts` -> `utils/__tests__/define-rollout-flags.test.ts`.

## Rewire imports
- Root `src/types.ts` currently does `import type { RolloutFlagKind } from './catalog'` — repoint to `./config/rollout-flag-kind`.
- `assert-rollout-flag-catalog.ts` and `define-rollout-flags.ts` import the kind const/type and catalog types — repoint their relative paths (kind => `../config/rollout-flag-kind`, shared types => `../types`). Watch for cycles: `config/rollout-flag-kind.ts` must stay leaf (import nothing from `utils/` or root `types.ts`).
- Root `src/index.ts`: replace the `from './catalog'` block with direct exports from `./config/rollout-flag-kind`, `./utils/assert-rollout-flag-catalog`, `./utils/define-rollout-flags`, and the catalog types now in `./types`. KEEP the exact same set of named exports leaving the barrel (public API unchanged). Alphabetize.
- Moved spec: fix relative import depth (`./define-rollout-flags` -> `../define-rollout-flags`).

## Validate
`rm -rf packages/react-router-rollout/dist` (stale). Then:
`pnpm nx run react-router-rollout:lint`
`pnpm nx run react-router-rollout:typecheck`
`pnpm nx run react-router-rollout:test`
Confirm `src/catalog/` no longer exists and no file references `./catalog`. Commit with Plan-Id/Task-Id footers.
title: react-router-rollout: dissolve src/catalog/ into config/utils/types

- `safeParse`s against a generated Zod schema (function or schema — match existing `FooInputSchema()` export shape).
- Maps Zod issues to a concise action-error shape.

- Supports both `{ slug, tag }` flattened forms and `{ input: { … } }` variable shapes so callers can pass the result straight to `executeGraphqlWithAuth`.

description:
The fix stops new damage; it does not clean up what already shipped. At least one real repo is affected today (ssm-data-pipeline), with untracked entries sitting in its tracked skills/ dir and a ledger pointing at paths that do not match them.

Decide and implement the healing path:
- Detect a ledger whose recorded paths do not exist but whose resolved equivalents do (the old-format signature).
- Remove those stray entries — but ONLY where they are still identifiably OT-injected (symlink pointing into <OT_ROOT>/skills, or a recorded fingerprint match). A target-owned or user-created file must never be touched, exactly as teardown already guarantees.
- Clean the stale .git/info/exclude block.

A one-shot reconcile at boot is likely the right home, alongside the reaper. If healing is judged too risky to automate, ship a documented manual cleanup instead and say so plainly in the doc — but do not leave affected repos silently dirty with no path forward.
requirements: ["ssm-data-pipeline ends up with a clean git status and its own skills/ intact", "Nothing is removed that is not provably OT-injected", "Stale exclude block is cleaned"]
summary: No new code needed — the existing boot reap + reconcile already heals affected repos. Proven by deliberately re-breaking ssm-data-pipeline to the exact pre-fix state (old-format ledger + reverted exclude, 10 stray entries) and letting one unattended boot heal it: 0 strays, all 20 ledger entries git-ignored, the repo's own skills untouched. Caveat: durable only once the running server restarts onto a build with 02e80bb6. Unrelated residue found: `?? .openthrottle/workspace-editors.json`, a different feature.
title: Heal repos already polluted by the old behavior

3. Create a **repo** skill. Assert: `skills/<slug>/SKILL.md` exists, it appears with the `OpenThrottle` badge, and `git status` shows exactly the new `skills/<slug>/` directory as untracked — no generated links leaking in.
4. Run `bash skills/ot-skill-sync/scripts/sync.sh --check` — must exit 0 in both cases. This is the real proof the create flow produced a layout-valid skill.
5. Walk the refusals in the UI: duplicate slug, non-kebab slug, empty description, and a hand-broken frontmatter body. Each must show an inline error and leave nothing on disk.
6. Open the new skill's detail page and confirm the existing edit/save path works on it.

Clean up both fixtures afterwards, and screenshot the create route in light and dark.

description:
## Finding
Discovered while doing task 2. The developer app's root shell statically pulls a **505.6 KB** chunk that Rolldown names `MarkdownRenderer-*.js`. Fingerprinting it found **two copies of acorn** (`tryReadTemplateToken`, `` `Using declaration is not allowed in single-statement positions` ``), an astring-style code generator, and micromark character tables — i.e. a complete JavaScript parser plus the react-markdown/MDX pipeline, downloaded on every navigation.

This is now the single largest item in the developer base shell.

## Paths
- Static importer inside root's graph: `chat-toolbar-reconcile-*.js` (75.3 KB) -> `MarkdownRenderer-*.js`
- `packages/react-router-markdown/src/**` (`MarkdownRenderer`)
- `packages/react-router-chat/src/**` (chat toolbar / message rendering reached from `GlobalLayoutHeader`'s ChatDialog)
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/root.tsx`

Other static importers (legitimately markdown-rendering routes, fine to keep): `plans.$planId._index`, `plans.$planId.tasks.$taskId._index`, `notes.$noteId`, `docs._index`, `skills.$slug`, `faq._index`, `schedule.$jobId._index`, `OutputStream`, `DocPageView`.

## Measured before
```bash
pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:build --skip-nx-cache
```
Root transitive **static** graph = **1207.6 KB raw / 381.4 KB gzip** (114 chunks), of which `MarkdownRenderer-*.js` is **505.6 KB** — 42%.

Confirm the edge with:
```bash
# list chunks that STATICALLY (not dynamically) import the markdown chunk
# see the graph walker used in this plan's task-2 notes
```

## Suspected cause
The global header mounts the chat surface eagerly; chat message rendering statically imports `MarkdownRenderer`, so the markdown/MDX stack is hoisted into the shared shell chunk rather than staying on the routes that actually render prose.

## Proposed fix
`React.lazy` the markdown renderer at the chat-message boundary (same pattern as `GlobalMetricsChart` in task 2), so the shell keeps only the chat chrome. Verify whether the MDX/acorn path is needed at all — if the renderer only handles CommonMark, dropping the MDX plugin removes both acorn copies outright.

## Expected after
- `MarkdownRenderer-*.js` **not** in the static import graph of `root-*.js`
- Root transitive static graph **≤ 750 KB raw**
- Markdown-rendering routes (`plans.*`, `docs.*`, `notes.*`, `skills.*`) still render prose correctly

## Acceptance
Production build: `root-*.js` has no static path to the markdown chunk, root static graph ≤ 750 KB raw, and `openthrottle-developer:test` stays green.
title: 11. Developer shell: keep react-markdown/acorn (505.6 KB) off every route

description:
Replaces the original "verify + regression guard" task. Verification already happened in task 2 (real unmodified stories screenshotted rendering correctly under an rAF shim), and there is no defect to guard against.

The real risk now is **recurrence of the misdiagnosis**: any agent or human who inspects the workbench through a headless/background browser will see empty charts again and re-file this bug. That is what needs a durable guard.

Add a short, findable note to `applications/openthrottle-workbench/AGENTS.md` (and/or `README.md`) covering:
- Recharts animates chart geometry from t=0 via `requestAnimationFrame`.
- Browsers do not fire rAF in a hidden tab (`document.visibilityState === 'hidden'`), which is the normal state for automated browser tools.
- Therefore Bar/Pie render **no** shapes and Line/Area render invisible ones (`stroke-dasharray: 0px ...`) in that environment. This is an artifact, not a bug.
- Counting DOM nodes is not a valid check — a Line path exists while drawing zero length. Screenshot instead.
- To inspect charts through automation, shim `requestAnimationFrame` onto a timer, or pass `isAnimationActive={false}` in a scratch story. Do not change the shipped components.

Done when: the note exists, is discoverable from the workbench docs, and names the `visibilityState`/rAF mechanism explicitly.
title: Document the hidden-tab rAF pitfall so this is not re-filed

description:
Thread the creating workspace through GraphQL plan creation and record it on the plan's run config.

## Work

- Add optional `workspacePath` to `CreatePlanInput` (`applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/plans/plan.input.ts`). Document it as: absolute path of the caller's workspace; resolved server-side to one of the caller's registered checkouts and recorded as the plan's default run workspace; ignored when `runConfigJson` already names one.
- Thread the authenticated user into `createPlan` and `createPlans` with `@CurrentUser('sub')` — the decorator is already imported and used elsewhere in `plans.resolver.ts`. Pass it down to `PlanCreationService`.
- In `resolvePlanCreateFields`, after `parsePlanRunConfigJson`: if the parsed run config has **no** `checkoutId`, `repositoryId`, or `workingDirectory`, and `workspacePath` resolves via the task-1 service, set `checkoutId` (and `repositoryId` from the resolved checkout). Otherwise leave the run config untouched.
- Apply to the batch path (`createPlansFromInput`) as well as the single path, so `create_plans` behaves identically.

## Hard constraints

- **Never fails creation.** An unresolvable, unregistered, relative, or absent `workspacePath` is a debug log and a no-op, never a `BadRequestException`.
- **Explicit wins.** A `runConfigJson` naming any workspace is never overridden.
- Resolution is server-side and user-scoped — the client path is a *hint*, and a path the caller does not own resolves to nothing.

## Definition of done

- Tests added to `plan-creation.service.test.ts`: seeds `checkoutId` when the path resolves and the run config is empty; leaves an explicit `runConfigJson` workspace alone; no-ops on an unresolvable path; no-ops when `workspacePath` is absent; batch create seeds each plan; a path owned by another user seeds nothing.
- Schema + codegen flow run per CLAUDE.md: boot `openthrottle-server:dev` until bootstrap to rewrite `applications/openthrottle-server/schema.gql`, then `pnpm nx affected --target=codegen-graphql,codegen-react-router --parallel`. Commit `schema.gql` and all `__generated__` output.
- `openthrottle-server:test`, `:lint`, `:typecheck` pass.

description:
Audit-first, no production code. Read `skills/ot-skill-sync/scripts/{common.sh,sync.sh,cleanup.sh}`, `packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/foreign-skill-injection/personal-skills-config.ts`, and `packages/openthrottle-skills/src/resolve-foreign-skill-manifest.ts`.

Decide and write down (as a short design section in `docs/monorepo/` — extend the existing foreign-workspace-skill-injection doc rather than starting a new one if it fits):

1. **Root + env.** One definition of the personal root, shared by the shell pipeline and the TypeScript injection path. Default `~/.openthrottle/skills`, override `OPENTHROTTLE_PERSONAL_SKILLS_DIR`. Recommendation: for the in-repo tier, **presence is the opt-in** — if the dir exists with at least one valid skill, sync uses it; no separate ENABLED toggle to forget. Keep `OPENTHROTTLE_PERSONAL_SKILLS_ENABLED` meaning only what it means today (the foreign-injection toggle) and say so explicitly, or unify it — but pick one and state the reasoning.
2. **Collision rule.** Foreign injection locked `ot-curated < personal < target repo`. In-repo the repo *is* the target, so those two rules disagree. Recommendation: a personal skill sharing a name with a committed `skills/<name>` is a **hard error** from sync (`✗ personal skill 'x' collides with committed skills/x`) with an explicit `--allow-shadow` escape, so nobody silently runs a private fork of a team skill. Record whichever is chosen.
3. **Ownership rule extension.** Today inside `.agents/skills/`: real dir = vendored (`skills-lock.json`), symlink = ours from `skills/`. Personal adds a third case — a symlink pointing *outside the repo*. Define how sync/`--check`/cleanup tell it apart from a stale link.

Deliverable: the design section + a short note in the task comments on anything the later tasks must not break. No behaviour change yet.

Why this matters: `AGENTS.md` is loaded into every agent run. A documented ingest command that fails sends an unattended agent down a path that has not existed since mid-2026.

Stale claims:
- `AGENTS.md:104` tells readers to run `pnpm run database:import` / `pnpm run database:import-docs` for Ollama-backed embeddings.
- `AGENTS.md:106` repeats `database:import` as a Caddy/`OLLAMA_BASE_URL` consumer.
- `databases/README.md:63-71` is a whole section titled "Ingest plans from the filesystem" that documents reading plan JSON from `plans/` (root, `completed`, `ideas`, except `templates`) via `pnpm run database:import`.
- `databases/README.md:149` says when `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` or `sOLLAMA_EMBEDDING_MODEL` is set, `database:import` uses Ollama; it also cites `https://localhost/osllama` as a Caddy URL.
- `databases/README.md:385` says to `pnpm run database:reset` then `pnpm run database:import` after dumping test data (and contains the typo `source fsiles`).
- `skills/openthrottle-stack/SKILL.md:73` (mirrored at `.agents/skills/openthrottle-stack/SKILL.md:73`) lists `pnpm run database:import` as "Ingest plan JSON from `plans/`". Line 10 of the same skill uses `database:import` as a trigger phrase.

What is actually true:
- Live root scripts (verified `Object.keys(require('./package.json').scripts)`): `database:import-agent-assets` and `database:import-docs`. There is no `database:import`.
- The only ingest scripts on disk are `scripts/openthrottle-ingest-agent-assets.ts` and `scripts/openthrottle-ingest-docs.ts`. There is no plans-from-filesystem ingest script.
- Repo-root `plans/` does not exist. Plans are created via openthrottle-mcp (`create_plan` / `create_tasks`), not JSON files.
- `sOLLAMA_EMBEDDING_MODEL` and `https://localhost/osllama` are typos for `OLLAMA_EMBEDDING_MODEL` and `https://localhost/ollama` (the latter matches `AGENTS.md:108` Option A).

Suggested correction where unambiguous:
- Delete the "Ingest plans from the filesystem" section (or rewrite it to say plans are authored in OpenThrottle, not ingested from `plans/`).
- In `AGENTS.md` and the stack skill, keep `pnpm run database:import-docs`; replace plan ingest with `pnpm run database:import-agent-assets` only where the subject is skills/personas/prompts, never plans.
- Fix `sOLLAMA_EMBEDDING_MODEL` → `OLLAMA_EMBEDDING_MODEL` and `osllama` → `ollama` in the same edit pass.

Staleness evidence:

- `databases/README.md` last touched `8ff64be1` (`2026-08-13 14:41:15 -0700`).
- `skills/openthrottle-stack/SKILL.md` last touched `2a9c2416` (`2026-07-19 23:00:00 -0700`).

Acceptance criteria:
- `rg 'pnpm run database:import[^\-]' AGENTS.md databases/README.md skills/openthrottle-stack/SKILL.md` returns no matches.
- No remaining instruction to ingest plan JSON from `plans/`.
- `database:import-docs` and `database:import-agent-assets` are documented against the roles they actually have.
- Any edit under `.agents/**` / `skills/**` still leaves `pnpm run check:local:agent-assets` passing. Do not hand-edit the `.agents/skills/` or `.claude/skills/` mirrors — edit `skills/openthrottle-stack/SKILL.md` and re-sync.

description:
Route modules cannot move out of the app (fs-routes + app-scoped typegen), so any domain code reaching INTO `app/routes` becomes a lib -> app cycle the moment the domain is extracted.

1. Invert the 17 `~/routes/*` imports. Typical cause is a loader/action type or a constant living in the route module; push the shared shape down into the domain folder (or the kernel) and have the route module import it, not the reverse. `~/routes/plans.*` (12) is the bulk; the rest are `resources.*` and `settings.keys`, `ide.files`.
2. Replace the 10 `@/*` imports (`.react-router/types/...`) inside `app/routing` with hand-written types. `.react-router/types` is generated per-app from `routes.ts` and will not exist in a library. Where a domain component genuinely needs loader data, define an explicit interface in the domain and let the route module satisfy it.
3. Re-run the reverse-edge grep to prove zero remaining `~/routes` and `@/` references under `app/routing`.

Done when: `grep -rE "~/routes/|from '@/" app/routing` returns nothing, and the app still typechecks.
summary: SUPERSEDED by plan 88f747ff task 8ab97f22 — the reverse-edge and @/ leakage pre-work moves there as a standalone PR.
title: Break the routing -> routes reverse imports and the @/ route-type leakage

description:
Files: `applications/openthrottle-server/src/queues/agentic-ralph/agentic-ralph-orchestrator.service.ts`, `applications/openthrottle-server/src/services/plan-run-worktree-checkout/plan-run-worktree-checkout.service.ts`, plus a new provisioning service under `applications/openthrottle-server/src/services/`.

This is the fix for the core bug: today `maybeRegisterWorktreeCheckout({ filesystemPath: configCwd })` is handed the PARENT repo path, `RepositoryInspectionService.scan()` returns `isLinkedWorktree: false`, registration is skipped, and `plan_runs.checkout_id` stays NULL.

Work (option A):
- New service that provisions a worktree for a run by shelling out to the sanctioned entrypoint `pnpm run worktree:new <name>` (never a bare `git worktree add` — that only self-heals on first `:dev`), from the resolved base checkout, and returns the absolute path. Idempotent: an existing worktree with the run's name is reused, not recreated.
- In `runPlanOrchestratorJob`, resolve the worktree path BEFORE `configCwd` is computed, and use it as the effective `workingDirectory` so `getWorkflowConfigCwd` → `agentCwd` → `iterationRunner.run({ cwd })` all target the worktree.
- Pass the worktree path (not `configCwd`) to `maybeRegisterWorktreeCheckout` so `repository_checkouts` gets the row and `plan_runs.checkout_id` is back-filled.
- Update `run_config_snapshot.workspace.workingDirectory` (and `checkoutId` once registered) so the run record shows the worktree it actually used.
- Do NOT also pass the agent-CLI `-w` flag under option A — assert one worktree per run, not two. Make sure the merged tuning from `mergePlanRunTuningWithWorkflowRalphConfig` cannot reintroduce it.
- Honor the task-1 failure policy (recommended: fail the run with a clear message rather than silently running in the parent repo).
- `validateWorkingDirectory` in `enqueue-plan-ralph-tuning.ts` requires the directory to already exist — confirm ordering works when the worktree is created at job start rather than enqueue, and adjust the validation path if needed.

Tests: extend `agentic-ralph-orchestrator.service.test.ts` and `plan-run-worktree-checkout.service.test.ts` — mock the provisioner and assert (a) `agentCwd` is the worktree path, (b) registration is called with the worktree path, (c) creation failure surfaces per the chosen policy, (d) an existing worktree is reused.

Acceptance: `pnpm nx run openthrottle-server:test -- src/queues/agentic-ralph src/services/plan-run-worktree-checkout` green; a locally-run plan job shows `checkout_id` populated and the agent working inside the worktree.

description:
Direction-independent. The hooks in `@openthrottle/agentic-hooks` phone home to the OT GraphQL API (see `src/data/persist.ts`, `src/utils/scope.ts`, `src/utils/privacy.ts`, `src/config/env.ts`). Everything about that was designed for one repo — this one. Running in someone else's checkout raises questions the current core does not answer:

1. **Which server?** How does a hook running in an arbitrary repo discover the OT endpoint — env var, plugin-bundled config, spawn-time injection? What if the operator runs several OT servers?
2. **How is the repo identified and scoped?** `scope.ts` resolves scope today from monorepo assumptions. What is the identity of a foreign repo in the telemetry — remote URL, path, a registered `WorkspaceLocalRepository` row?
3. **Unreachable server.** The core is already fail-open; confirm that holds when the endpoint is simply absent rather than erroring, and that it stays silent rather than warning on every prompt.
4. **Privacy default** for a repo the OT operator does not own. Overlaps plan `91679bbf`; align rather than re-decide.

Deliverable: a short contract section appended to the plan description (or its own decision record) that any of options A/B/C/E can be built against.
summary: Contract written as its own delivery-mechanism-independent decision record: `docs/monorepo/child-repo-hook-telemetry-contract.md`. Keys everything off one `home` vs `foreign` repo classification (filesystem marker test), leaving all in-monorepo behavior untouched. Answers the four questions: (1) endpoint — the `<repoRoot>/.env` legs of resolveGraphqlUrl/resolveAuthToken are DISABLED in foreign repos (reading a stranger's .env is both a privacy violation and a correctness bug); permitted sources are SKILL_USAGE_* overrides → process env (how leg B supplies it, since the driver owns the child env) → `~/.openthrottle/hooks.json` (how leg A supplies it); never the plugin dir, which must stay operator-agnostic and byte-stable. Multiple servers resolve by precedence, not fan-out. (2) identity — normalized git remote URL, not a per-machine path; no remote → no identity, never a path fallback. Also flags that `detectScope` would misreport every OT-authored skill as `third-party` in a foreign repo, so scope must resolve against the injected/plugin skill set. (3) unreachable — confirmed already silent for a missing URL and bounded by the 750ms timeout + drain budget; the one required change is rate-limiting the resolvable-but-unreachable warning to once per session, since headless `-p` captures stderr into the run output. (4) privacy — foreign defaults to `name-only` (no args) vs home's `truncated`, aligned with 91679bbf; raising it requires explicit machine-global opt-in. FINDING WORTH ESCALATING: the JSONL buffer currently writes `<repoRoot>/.cache/skill-usage/` INTO the target working tree, which falsifies leg B's zero-disk-mutation property in exactly the common case (a foreign repo is the one most likely to have no reachable server). §4 makes relocating the buffer to a machine-global root a hard requirement with a stated test.
title: Define the child-repo scoping and privacy contract for hook telemetry

description:
First real consumer, and the one that just broke. Migrate every editor-list site onto the package:

- `packages/nestjs-repositories/src/modules/workspace-settings/workspace-editor-id.ts` — `WORKSPACE_EDITOR_IDS` + `isWorkspaceEditorId`.
- `.../workspace-editor-config-paths.ts` — already an exhaustive Record; convert to the helper for consistency or leave and document why.
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/settings/config/workspace-editors.ts` — `WORKSPACE_EDITOR_OPTIONS` is a hand-written array of `{label, value}`. Derive it from a `.labelled()` map so a new editor cannot be added without a label.
- `.../config/workspace-editor-affiliate-links.ts` — exhaustive Record already.
- `app/global/config/workspace-editor-deep-links.ts` — exhaustive Record already.
- `app/routing/settings/utils/is-workspace-editor-id.ts` — the derived guard. After migration this should collapse into the vocabulary's own `.is()`; delete the file if nothing else needs it.

**Delete the duplicate guard, do not leave two.** The bug that motivated this plan was two `isWorkspaceEditorId` functions that disagreed — the multi-select used the derived one, the form parser a hardcoded copy. Exactly one may survive.

**Then prove it works.** Add a temporary fourth member to the vocabulary locally and confirm `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:typecheck` fails at *every* consumer, including `workspace-settings-action.ts`, which is the one that silently passed before. Record the error list in the plan output, then revert the temporary member. If any consumer stays green, the migration is incomplete — fix it before completing this task.

Validate sequentially: `openthrottle-developer:typecheck`, `:lint`, `:test`; plus `openthrottle-server:test` and `@openthrottle/nestjs-repositories:test`.
summary: Migrated all six editor-list sites. Server: WORKSPACE_EDITOR_IDS/isWorkspaceEditorId now derive from vocabulary(); config-paths converted to .labelled(). Client: new app/global/config/workspace-editors.ts wraps the generated enum via vocabularyFromEnum (no members re-listed); WORKSPACE_EDITOR_OPTIONS now derives from a new exhaustive WORKSPACE_EDITOR_LABELS map; affiliate-links and deep-links converted to .labelled<T>(). Duplicate guard deleted (is-workspace-editor-id.ts + its test); both consumers call WORKSPACE_EDITORS.is. Tripwire proven: a temporary fourth editor produces 1 server error + 3 client errors, then reverted. workspace-settings-action.ts stays green by design — it derives rather than enumerates, and the picker's options now come from the same tripwired map, so divergence is unrepresentable. All 6 validation targets green.
title: Migrate the workspace-editor vocabulary and prove the tripwire

description:
Variants in the type are only half of it. The pipeline has to be able to render two takes of one episode and keep both.

## Plumb

- `--variant <id>` on `narrate.ts`, `runner/run.ts` and `assemble/assemble.ts`, defaulting to the episode's `selectedVariant`. An unknown id fails loudly with the known ids listed.
- **Namespace outputs**: `output/<slug>/<variant>/…` for audio, frames, manifests, masters, `.srt` and `metadata.json`. Update the package's `.gitignore` and anything that globs those paths (the leak scanner, the assemble input resolution, `scan/`).
- **Record provenance**: variant id in `timings.json` alongside the existing backend/voice/model fields, and in `metadata.json`. Those fields exist precisely so a take traces to what produced it; the words are as much a part of that as the voice is.
- **Render cache**: `narrate/render-cache.ts` keys renders by text and backend. Confirm two variants sharing an identical sentence correctly share the cached render (that is the desired behaviour and a real saving on hosted TTS) and that nothing else in the key silently collides across variants.

## Nx targets

`video-narrate`, `video-record`, `video-assemble` and `video-scan` now belong to the showroom project. Verify `--variant` survives the `nx run … --` boundary and document the invocation in each target's description.

## Done when

Two variants of episode 05 can be narrated and assembled from a single recorded flow without either overwriting the other, and each `metadata.json` names its variant.
summary: DONE — capture shared at output/<episode>/, takes namespaced at output/<episode>/<variant>/, variant recorded in timings.json and metadata.json, cache-key invariant pinned by test. Commit 8972a0f5.
title: Thread --variant through narrate, record and assemble with take provenance

description:
Restructure `setup.sh` + `setup_environment.sh`, `setup_software.sh`, `setup_services.sh`, `setup_troubleshooting.sh`, `setup_update.sh`.

Split by the bootstrap boundary:
- **Pre-install (stays shell):** a minimal `setup.sh` shim that ensures the toolchain exists (brew/node/pnpm checks from setup_environment/setup_software that must run before node_modules exists) and runs `pnpm install`, then delegates everything else to `tsx ./scripts/setup.ts`.
- **Post-install (becomes .ts):** the orchestration currently in setup.sh (skills sync invocation, build, database:build/start/migrate, bootstrap-service-accounts, import-agent-assets, bootstrap-default-user, check:bootstrap-secrets) plus the logic of setup_troubleshooting / setup_update / setup_services. Use the toolkit exec helper so each step gets a chalk heading, timing, and a clear failure banner instead of raw `set -e` death.

Preserve semantics exactly: step order matters (documented in setup.sh comments — e.g. check:bootstrap-secrets must run AFTER both bootstrap scripts; bootstrap-default-user is primary-checkout-only, worktrees must NOT re-seed). Keep the closing instructions block (copy tokens into .env files, run setup:mcp-instructions) — render it with chalk as a proper outro.

Tests: step-plan assembly and ordering as data (array of steps) so the sequence is unit-testable without executing anything; troubleshooting checks' pure predicates.

Validation: run `./scripts/setup.sh` end-to-end on the primary checkout (it is idempotent by design — bootstrap scripts skip existing rows); confirm the terminal output reads well.
title: Convert the setup script family to .ts behind a thin POSIX bootstrap shim

description:
Create `scripts/lib/` — the shared foundation every later task builds on.

Contents:
- `logger.ts`: chalk-based logger — heading, step, info, success, warn, fail — with a `stream` option so stdout-contract scripts can route ALL narration to stderr. Chalk natively respects NO_COLOR and non-TTY; don't reimplement that.
- `env.ts`: read a KEY=VALUE .env file without exporting/mutating process.env (replaces the `get_env()` grep/cut idiom copied across shell scripts).
- `exec.ts`: typed child-process runner (spawnSync/spawn wrapper) with clear failure output and an option to inherit vs capture stdio.
- `args.ts`: tiny flag helper consistent with the existing `--strict` / `--json` / `--check` conventions in audit-*.ts (or standardize on node:util parseArgs — decide and document).
- `index.ts` re-exporting the public surface.

Rules: no new enums (`as const`), explicit return types, `import type`. chalk comes from the pnpm catalog (`"chalk": "catalog:"` already in root package.json).

Tests: Vitest specs in `scripts/__tests__/` for env parsing, arg parsing, and logger stream routing (assert stderr vs stdout writes; don't snapshot ANSI codes — strip or disable color in tests).

Pilot adoption (proves the API before mass adoption): refactor `scripts/setup_mcp-instructions.ts` (the one existing chalk user) and one bare-console script (e.g. `scripts/bootstrap-default-user.ts`) onto the toolkit. Output should read as one coherent tool.

Validation: `pnpm nx affected --target=typecheck,lint,test --parallel`; run both pilot scripts manually and eyeball the UX.
title: Shared scripts toolkit: scripts/lib/ with chalk logger + helpers, piloted on two scripts

description:
Read `packages/react-router-ui-global/src/components/GlobalFeatureOnboardingBody.tsx` and check how `content.secondary` is rendered. Every existing onboarding block passes an internal route; this plan is the first to pass an absolute `https://` URL.

If it renders through react-router's `Link to`, an absolute URL will still render an anchor but bypasses normal external-link handling (no `target`/`rel`). Decide and implement the smallest correct fix:
- preferred: in `GlobalFeatureOnboardingBody`, detect an absolute URL (`/^https?:\/\//`) and render a plain `<a href target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">` instead of `Link`, keeping the same button styling;
- document the behavior in the `GlobalFeatureOnboardingLink` JSDoc on `GlobalFeatureOnboarding.tsx` so future features know external links are supported.

This is a shared package used by 4 apps — keep the change purely additive and covered by a test in the package's `__tests__` (both an internal `to` and an external `to`). Validate with `pnpm nx run react-router-ui-global:typecheck`, `:lint`, `:test`.
title: Confirm GlobalFeatureOnboardingBody handles an external secondary link

description:
Four skills, all **0 recorded invocations**, all thin narration of MCP calls `ot-plans` already covers:

| skill | size | what it actually says |
|---|---|---|
| `ot-create-plan` | 271 words | call `create_plan` / `create_tasks` |
| `ot-ask` | 174 words | call `semantic_search` / `list_sources` / `get_document` |
| `ot-list-by-status` | 151 words | call `list_plans_by_status` |
| `ot-edit-task` | 126 words | call `get_task` / `update_task` |

`ot-plans` (834 words, 10 invocations) is the real skill, and the MCP server ships its own tool instructions describing the same calls. Three of the four are `disable-model-invocation: true`, so they only exist as slash shortcuts — and the telemetry says nobody types them.

**Do:**
1. Verify against the corrected task-1 numbers that these are genuinely unused (they are slash-only, so the hook *should* be catching them via UserPromptExpansion — that makes 0 a trustworthy 0 here).
2. Add a short "common operations" section to `ot-plans` covering create / edit / list-by-status / ask, if anything in the four is not already there.
3. Delete all four skill directories.
4. Grep for `/ot/ask`, `/ot/create-plan`, `/ot/edit-task`, `/ot/list-by-status` in docs, `.cursor/`, `.agents/`, and README/AGENTS files; repoint to `/ot-plans`.
5. Run `/skill-sync`.

**Saves:** 4 skills, ~720 words, ~1.2 KB of always-on description.

**Done when:** `ot-plans` is the single OT plan/task skill and no slash references dangle.
title: Fold the four thin ot-* MCP wrappers into ot-plans

description:
Close the unbounded HTTP path. In packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/conversation-backend/openai.ts and packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/chat-completions/stream.ts (streamChatCompletion), add a per-chunk idle timer that aborts the in-flight OpenAI SDK stream when no part has arrived within idleMs — mirroring the CLI backends' resetIdle() behavior (see claude/claude.ts, teardown.ts resolveAgentTimeouts).

- Reset the idle timer on each streamed part; on expiry, abort the SDK request (combine with any caller-provided options.signal so both the orchestrator abort and the idle abort tear the stream down).
- Surface a clear timeout error so the orchestrator's catch publishes a terminal chunk. This is defense-in-depth beneath the Task 2 orchestrator backstop (which already covers this backend), keeping the failure close to the source and freeing the HTTP socket promptly.
- Reuse resolveAgentTimeouts() for the value.
requirements: ["Idle timer resets on each SDK stream part", "Idle expiry aborts the SDK stream (composed with caller signal)", "Emits a clear timeout error consumable upstream"]
title: HTTP/OpenAI backend: add per-chunk idle timeout

description:
**Gates:**
```
pnpm nx run react-router-shadcn:lint && pnpm nx run react-router-shadcn:typecheck && pnpm nx run react-router-shadcn:test
pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:lint && pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:typecheck && pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:test
pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:build
```
Run them sequentially, not in parallel — the shared Nx cache plus build deps makes concurrent runs produce spurious failures.

Then `pnpm run check:local` for CI parity. Note that `check:local`'s affected-test step is narrowed, so if anything looks suspiciously fast, mirror CI with `pnpm nx run-many --target=test --all`.

**Hands-on verification** — `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:dev`, visit `/settings/repositories`:
- Nested rows: a repository with worktrees expands and collapses; a repository without them shows no chevron.
- Search a worktree branch name → parent appears and its group auto-expands.
- Search nonsense → no-results message, not the onboarding block.
- Sort by each option, both directions; confirm `page` resets where it should.
- Page 2 with `limit` forced small; confirm no group is split across the boundary.
- Each row action: refresh (in-flight disable, drift warnings render), apply editor config, remove (confirmation, then the row disappears).
- Zero repositories → onboarding still shows.

Spot-check one other `DataTable` consumer (`/projects`) to confirm the shared-component change is genuinely inert.

**Done when:** every gate is green and each verification step above is confirmed, with any deviation reported rather than papered over.
summary: Full gate on openthrottle-developer and react-router-shadcn, then hands-on verification of the route against real workspace data.
title: Validate and verify in the running app

description:
`PlanRunConfigStoreProvider.tsx:52` seeds `workflowBranchAtom` at mount via `resolveDefaultRunBranch({ checkoutId, repositories, repositoryId })`, with the documented reason: the branch is required to enqueue, so it must not wait for the Configuration tab's selector to mount. With `workspaceRepositories` deferred, `repositories` is `[]` at mount.

Do this:

1. Keep the provider's mount-time seed for everything derived from the plan alone (run options, iteration timeout, working directory, checkout id, repository id, hook rows). Seed the branch with whatever `resolveDefaultRunBranch` yields from the plan's persisted config with no repositories.
2. Add a `PlanRunConfigRepositoriesHydrator` component (generator-scaffolded, under `app/routing/plans/components/`) rendered inside the provider. It awaits the `workspaceRepositories` promise and, on resolution, re-runs `resolveDefaultRunBranch` and writes `workflowBranchAtom` **only if the user has not touched the branch**. Add a `workflowBranchDirtyAtom` (or equivalent, in `app/routing/plans/data/atom.plan.ts`) set by the branch input's own change handler — back-filling over a user's typed branch is the failure mode to avoid, so make it impossible, not unlikely.
3. Add a `workspaceRepositoriesReadyAtom` (false until the promise resolves). Fold it into the run-gating in `usePlanDetailRoute.ts`: while it is false, Run/Queue is **disabled with a "Resolving workspace…" reason**, not blocked with a validation error — a validation error on a page that is still loading reads as a bug. `runConfigSaveBlockedReason` copy lives in `data.copy.ts` per the component/data-file-boundaries rule.
4. Guard the action path too: `runPlan` in `app/routing/plans/actions/planId.ts` must reject an empty branch with a clear error rather than enqueueing. Client-side disabling is not the security boundary here — a fast click during load must not produce a broken run.

Tests: provider seeds correctly with no repositories; hydrator back-fills a pristine branch; hydrator leaves a dirty branch alone; Run is disabled with the resolving reason while pending and enabled after; the action rejects an empty branch.
summary: The trickiest part: the Jotai store seeds the run branch from repositories at mount, and Run/Queue validity depends on it. Seed without them, back-fill once resolved, and never let an enqueue fire with an empty branch.
title: Keep run-config seeding correct with workspaceRepositories deferred

description:
Root provider that takes applicationKey + flag catalog, fetches evaluations, validates against the catalog, and stores resolved values for hooks.

## Provider props (target)
- applicationKey: string (APP_NAME today)
- flags: catalog from defineRolloutFlags
- fetch adapter / GraphQL client callback (keep package free of app-specific codegen)
- optional cache options (ttlMs, storage: memory | sessionStorage)
- optional initialEvaluations for SSR/loader hydration later

## Work
1. Create React context + RolloutProvider following NotificationsStoreProvider patterns (import * as React).
2. On mount: load cache if fresh → else fetch evaluations with applicationKey → merge.
3. Cross-check: keys in catalog missing on server → keep default + warn/dev log; server keys unknown to catalog → ignore (or optional strict mode); kind mismatch → prefer default + warn.
4. Parse valueJson safely into typed values; fall back to default on parse/kind failure.
5. Expose status: idle | loading | ready | error (discriminated union).
6. Re-hydrate when auth session appears/changes (enrichment) without unmounting tree if practical.
7. Unit tests with mocked fetch adapter covering happy path, cache hit, kind mismatch, network error → defaults.

## Acceptance criteria
- Children can read resolved flags after ready
- Defaults used before ready and on error
- Cache avoids repeat network within TTL for same applicationKey
- Kind/key mismatches do not crash; defaults win
- applicationKey included in fetch adapter call
requirements: ["package must not import app __generated__ graphql directly — inject document/fetcher", "validation should be cached to some degree"]
summary: Landed RolloutProvider + useRolloutContext with injected fetchEvaluations, catalog merge/validation (defaults on miss/kind mismatch), memory|sessionStorage TTL cache keyed by applicationKey+identityKey, hydration status idle|loading|ready|error, and rehydrate on identityKey change. Commit 0b8b6be9. lint/typecheck/test green (31 tests). Typed useRolloutFlag hooks are the next task.
title: Implement RolloutProvider context + hydration

description:
Add a high-level idle timeout around the for-await loop in applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/conversation-stream/conversation-stream.service.ts (runStream, ~line 211-363). This is the single choke point covering ALL backends, including the unbounded HTTP one.

Implementation:
- Race the backend iterator's .next() against an idle timer instead of a bare `for await`, so a backend that ignores its AbortSignal still terminates server-side. Reset the timer on every chunk received.
- On idle expiry: call the existing controller.abort() (already threaded into backendRun.signal) AND break out of the loop; persist whatever streamed so far via the existing persistAssistant path; publish a terminal done chunk with a clear timeout error message and the retryable metadata from Task 1 (metadataJson { timedOut: true, retryable: true }).
- Use the idle value from Task 1's config decision (resolveAgentTimeouts().idleMs or the chat-scoped alias). Idle-only — do not add an orchestrator wall-clock cap.
- Ensure the existing finally{} controller cleanup and replay-buffer eviction still run correctly; the timer must be cleared on normal completion, error, and abort.

Keep runStream's fire-and-forget contract: it must still always resolve, never throw.
requirements: ["Idle timer resets on each chunk; races iterator.next()", "On idle: abort + break + persist partial + publish retryable terminal done chunk", "Timer cleared on completion/error/abort; no leak", "Covers HTTP backend even if it ignores the abort signal"]

description:
## The problem
Every plan run ends with the same manual ritual: after the PR merges, someone must attach_session_subject + record_artifact the squash commit, and flip the plan to COMPLETED — and it routinely doesn't happen. Evidence: a long trail of plans annotated "DONE PR #NNN (unmerged, ledger owed)" in the planning record (e.g. 677dcaab global help modal, 082bf81f scheduled-job run detail, 0cbfffd3 onboarding-in-a-modal, de854c29 appearance regroup); a one-time 506-row commit_links backfill was already needed to reconcile main; and there is a known gap that nothing server-side downward-reconciles a plan whose tasks are all COMPLETED — plans strand. Meanwhile 97 of the last 100 PRs are merged, so the debt is pure bookkeeping, not blocked work. The ingredients now exist: the work ledger shipped (#195/#198/#199/#200) and run provenance shipped on plan_runs — branch, worktree, model, PR linkage (#280) — but nothing consumes that provenance.

## The proposed change
A reconciliation service in openthrottle-server (BullMQ repeatable job first; GitHub webhook later if wanted) that: (1) polls the canonical repo (gh/GitHub API) for merged PRs matching plan_runs' recorded branch/PR provenance from #280; (2) on merge, opens a system work-ledger session and records the squash commit as a git_commit artifact against the plan (and task where resolvable via Plan-Id:/Task-Id: footers); (3) settles status: a plan with all tasks COMPLETED plus a merged PR flips to COMPLETED, stamped with a system actor and an audit note. Surface reconciliation results in the developer app plan detail ("merged via #NNN on <date>"). Mirrors the already-accepted heartbeat/staleness pattern for stranded runs (#226) — this is the same idea applied to the ledger and terminal statuses.

## What it unlocks
Removes the per-plan manual ledger/status step entirely (the single most repeated piece of process debt on record); makes the work ledger trustworthy enough to build on (activity timeline, Institutional Memory theme on roadmap ce7e2773); eliminates future backfills; gives the ten recurring Job_* audit jobs accurate plan-state input.

## Rough size
3–5 days. Touches openthrottle-server (new module + repeatable job), databases (possibly a reconciliation audit column/table), openthrottle-mcp (optional read surface), openthrottle-developer (plan-detail provenance display).

## Migration risk
Low — additive service over existing tables. Risks: mis-attribution when one PR covers several plans or a plan spans several PRs (mitigate: only auto-settle on unambiguous provenance, otherwise flag for review); GitHub API rate limits (poll interval + etag caching). Rollback: disable the repeatable job; no schema unwinding required if audit data is additive.

## The strongest argument against
A merged PR does not always mean the plan's intent shipped — partial implementations, reverted merges, and follow-up PRs are real, and an automated COMPLETED flip can quietly mislabel work, which is worse than a stranded IN_PROGRESS because nobody re-checks a completed plan. For a single-operator system the manual step costs a minute, and the honest fix might be discipline (or the existing skills prompting for it) rather than new always-on infrastructure that itself must be monitored.
summary: Automate the post-merge bookkeeping that every plan currently owes by hand: watch canonical-repo merges, record the squash commit on the work ledger, and downward-reconcile plan status.
title: Merge-driven reconciliation: PR merge → work-ledger artifact → plan/task status settle

description:
Create `docs/marketing/scripts/SEASON-1-NARRATION.md` with its header sections only — no episode content yet. This task decides everything the other seventy-two takes are written against, so it lands first and alone.

**The voice charter.** Write down the 'keys to your first car' tone as rules a writer can fail, not adjectives. At minimum: present tense; second person; sentences that carry momentum rather than list features; the open-road framing (what becomes possible) instead of the problem framing (what is broken today); no hedging verbs (`can help you`, `aims to`, `should`); no enterprise register. Include a short do/don't table with real rewrites drawn from the current scripts — `01`'s 'gives coding agents the one thing they have never had' is a good before, because it frames a lack.

**The word budget.** State the revised targets explicitly, with the derivation: shorts 115–132 spoken words (145 wpm × 55s = 132 hard ceiling from `format.json`), floor of 110 below which a take is under-narrated; long-form 1,200–1,400 words per iteration. Note plainly that this reverses `scripts/README.md`'s 'the budget is a ceiling, not a target' — a reader hitting the two documents in either order needs to know which is current.

**The three theses.** Pick one set of three lenses used consistently across all 24 episodes, so takes are comparable episode to episode rather than three arbitrary rewrites each. Name them by thesis, never by ordinal (`payoff-first`, not `v3`) — this is a hard requirement from `docs/marketing/episode-format.md`, which explains that the ordinal records the one fact nobody needs. Episode 05's existing `-v0`…`-v3` prose is the best available evidence of which lenses were actually worth testing; read all four before choosing.

**The per-episode section template — keep it minimal.** One `##` per episode, three iterations under it, and each iteration is nothing more than a thesis id, one line of thesis prose, and a flat cue list:

```
## 01 — What is OpenThrottle in 60 seconds
beats: 0:00 0:07 0:15 0:24 0:33 0:41 0:49   ·   source: 01-what-is-openthrottle.md

### payoff-first  (127 words)
One line on what this take is betting on.
[
  ['0:00', 'the words'],
  ['0:07', 'the words'],
]
```

No per-iteration front matter, no repeated action column, no tables. The `[[time, text], …]` list is the entire iteration — it is already the `NarrationCue[]` shape the typed episodes take, so migration is a copy, and the beat times sit once per episode as a reference row rather than once per take. Everything about one script lives under that one `##`.
requirements: ["The file exists with charter, budget, theses and template sections, and no episode content", "The three thesis ids are prose names, not ordinals", "The reversal of scripts/README.md's word-budget guidance is stated explicitly, with the derivation of both numbers", "An iteration is a thesis id, one thesis line, and a flat [[time, text], ...] cue list — nothing else", "One ## section per episode holds all three of its iterations", "Episode 05's four existing variant files are read and their rationale is reflected in the chosen theses"]
title: Write the voice charter and pick the three iteration theses

description:

- `is_linked_worktree()` — the `--git-dir` vs `--git-common-dir` comparison lifted verbatim from today's `scripts/create_worktree.sh` / `ensure_worktree.sh`.
- `primary_checkout()` — `dirname "$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir)"`.

## Location
- `packages/nestjs-rbac/src/cors.ts:46-62` — omit / empty / `*` ⇒ `origin: true` (allow-all); credentials default false unless `CORS_CREDENTIALS=true`.
- `applications/openthrottle-server/.env.default` — `CORS_ORIGINS` is a single `"` character (ord 34), not a real allowlist; easy to "fix" into `*` or empty.

## Reachability
Misconfigured hosted server with allow-all origin (+ accidental credentials opt-in) reflects browser Origin and enables cross-site credentialed API calls.

## Remediation
1. In production, refuse to boot if `CORS_ORIGINS` is unset/empty/`*` unless an explicit dangerous override is set.
2. Replace the server `.env.default` value with a documented localhost allowlist (match root compose defaults).
3. Keep credentials default-false for allow-all.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Production boot fails closed on missing CORS allowlist (or requires explicit override env).
- [ ] Server `.env.default` lists real localhost origins, not a stray quote.
- [ ] Existing cors unit tests updated for the production fail-closed behavior.
title: Harden CORS defaults: fail closed in production; fix broken server .env.default

description:
Nothing in this short works unless a seeded rule matches a seeded plan. Three preconditions, all currently unmet or unverified:

**The tag must be in the vocabulary.** `PlanTagChips.tsx` offers a `<select>` populated from `skillTagVocabulary` with an "Add tag…" placeholder and an Add button - it is not a free-text field. If `needs-review` is not in the vocabulary it cannot be picked on camera, and the 0:00 beat has no action.

**The plan owner must resolve to a users row.** The processor resolves the owner from `plan.author` (GitHub username) to a users row, and its own doc comment says "a plan whose author has no user row has no rules and is skipped". The demo records as `GITHUB_USER=atlas-ada`, so that user must exist and must own the seeded rules.

**The rule must be unqualified.** The v1 worker evaluates with `environment=null`, so an environment-qualified rule only matches on qualified read paths, not here. A seeded rule with an environment set will silently never fire.

Use `inject-task` as the action: it is one of only two action types (`summarizeRuleAction` in `app/routing/rules/utils/formatters.ts` handles `inject-task` and `availability-exception`) and the only one with a visible effect on a plan.

Extend `tests/demo/fixtures/demo-content.ts` and `scripts/seed-demo.ts` to write the rule, and confirm end to end that adding the tag by hand produces a ledger row and an injected task before any recording is attempted.
summary: Seeded: needs-review + the FULL default vocabulary in user_skill_tags (server self-seeds defaults only for a user with zero rows), dogfood project nx_project_name=OpenThrottle/monorepo + 3 fictional project_skills (the /rules/new skill dropdown lists only dogfood skills), and one enabled unqualified (environment NULL) inject-task rule for needs-review with titleTemplate. Rule fired on camera; injected row Review: Add rate limiting to the public API.
title: Seed a rule that can actually fire on camera
